recipes.recipe_name: Potato Pavé with Whipped Goat Cheese and Chive Oil
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown, crispy potato pavé cube sits centered on a matte white designer ceramic plate. The cube displays distinct, paper-thin compressed layers. A small, precise quenelle of bright white whipped goat cheese rests perfectly on top. Two ultra-thin, toasted sourdough bread shards are placed vertically into the mousse for architectural height. Vibrant emerald green chive oil is applied in three descending dots alongside the pavé. A few 2mm chive batons provide a final garnish. The plating is minimalist with significant negative space. Lighting is soft and directional, casting subtle shadows that emphasize the potato's texture. The setting includes a grey-veined marble surface and a polished silver tasting fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an amuse-bouche or light starter
Pair with a chilled glass of Sancerre
Use a small silver tasting fork
instructions: Peel potatoes. Slice into 1mm rounds using a mandoline.
Line a small rectangular tray with parchment paper.
Layer potatoes in the tray. Brush each layer with clarified butter and salt.
Bake at 150°C for 90 minutes until tender.
Place a weight on the potatoes. Refrigerate for 12 hours.
Blanch chives in boiling water for 10 seconds. Shock in ice water.
Blend chives with oil until smooth. Strain through a fine cloth.
Whisk goat cheese and cream until light and airy. Transfer to a piping bag.
Cut chilled potato block into 3cm cubes.
Sear potato cubes in a pan until all sides are golden and crisp.
Toast sourdough slices until brittle. Break into jagged shards.
Pipe a small mound of cheese on each hot potato cube. Top with bread shards and chive oil.
notes: Ensure the potato layers are pressed firmly to prevent the cube from falling apart during searing.
The chive oil can be made 24 hours in advance for deeper color.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Roasted Bratwurst with Gloucester Cheese Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain plate. A thick square-cut portion of golden-brown Gloucester cheese potato gratin sits as the base. The gratin displays distinct layers of tender sliced potatoes and bubbly, melted cheese with caramelized edges. One whole, plump, pan-roasted bratwurst rests directly beside the gratin. The sausage skin is taut, glossy, and deeply browned with distinct sear marks from the pan. A precise, circular dollop of pale yellow Dijonnaise is positioned neatly on the plate. The arrangement is set on a dark oak bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin. Natural side lighting emphasizes the creamy texture of the cheese and the rustic crust of the sausage.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled red cabbage
Pair with a crisp British ale or lager
Provide a sharp steak knife for the sausage
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Rub a small baking dish with the halved garlic clove and butter.
Peel and slice potatoes into 3mm rounds.
Layer potatoes in the dish, seasoning each layer with salt, pepper, and 100g of Gloucester cheese.
Pour heavy cream over the potatoes.
Bake for 40 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Sprinkle remaining 50g of cheese on top and broil for 3 minutes until golden.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and add the bratwurst.
Pan-roast sausages for 12 minutes, turning frequently until browned and cooked through.
Place one whole bratwurst on a plate next to a square of the potato gratin.
Add a neat spoonful of Dijonnaise to the side.
Garnish with fresh chives.
notes: Ensure the internal temperature of the bratwurst reaches 71°C.
Let the gratin rest for 5 minutes before cutting to ensure clean edges.
Use a high-quality Double Gloucester for a richer orange color and sharper flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Huevos Rancheros with Blistered Tomato Salsa
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two lightly crisped corn tortillas centered on a clean white porcelain plate. Each tortilla is smothered in a vibrant, chunky red tomato salsa showing visible bits of blistered tomato and sautéed onion. A perfectly fried egg sits atop each tortilla, featuring a bright, glossy yellow yolk and opaque white edges. The avocado is cut into uniform 1 cm cubes and scattered naturally around the eggs. Fresh green cilantro is sprinkled over the top. The arrangement is organic yet professional, with two lime wedges placed neatly on the side. The scene is set on a dark wood table with a woven cotton napkin and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm refried beans
Provide spicy salsa verde on the side
Accompany with fresh cafe de olla
instructions: Heat 20 ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Sauté onion and garlic for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add diced tomatoes and salt.
Simmer for 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Heat 20 ml olive oil in a separate skillet.
Fry corn tortillas for 30 seconds per side until slightly crisp.
Drain tortillas on paper towels.
Add remaining olive oil to the skillet.
Fry eggs sunny-side up until whites are set but yolks remain runny.
Place two tortillas on each plate.
Spoon tomato sauce over tortillas.
Top each tortilla with one fried egg.
Garnish with diced avocado and chopped cilantro.
Serve immediately with lime wedges.
notes: Ensure the oil is hot before frying tortillas to prevent sogginess.
Use very ripe tomatoes for the most authentic sauce flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Cured Chicken and Abalone Clay Pot Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cantonese clay pot rice served in a traditional black ceramic pot on a light wood bistro table. The base consists of fluffy white jasmine rice with a visible golden-brown scorched crust at the edges. On top, 3cm chunks of dark, glazed cured chicken are nestled alongside two whole, tender abalones with delicate cross-hatch scoring. Two vibrant green steamed bok choy halves are placed neatly to one side. The dish is finished with a glossy dark soy-based sauce and a sprinkle of bright green scallions. A pair of dark wood chopsticks and a white ceramic soup spoon rest on a clean cotton napkin beside the pot.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly in the clay pot to maintain heat
Scrape the crispy rice (guoba) from the bottom to mix with the soft rice
Pair with hot jasmine or pu-erh tea

ingredients.name: Cured chicken (Lap Gai), cut into 3cm chunks

instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Soak rice in 600ml water for 30 minutes.
Place rice and soaking water into a large clay pot.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to low and cover tightly.
Simmer for 8 minutes until water is mostly absorbed.
Arrange cured chicken chunks and ginger on top of the rice.
Place abalones on top of the chicken.
Cover and cook on low for 12 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Place bok choy on top and cover for 2 minutes to steam.
Drizzle oil around the inside edge of the pot to crisp the rice bottom.
Increase heat to medium for 2 minutes until rice crackles.
Remove from heat and drizzle with clay pot rice sauce.
Garnish with sliced scallions.
notes: Ensure the clay pot is seasoned before first use to prevent cracking
Do not open the lid during the initial simmering phase to maintain steam pressure
The crackling sound indicates the bottom crust is forming correctly

recipes.recipe_name: Pesto-Glazed Chicken with Spinach and Bacon
recipes.visual_description: A single whole pan-seared chicken breast serves as the focal point, coated in a thick, textured basil pesto glaze. The chicken is placed on a mound of wilted whole baby spinach leaves interspersed with 1cm cubes of crispy, browned bacon. A soft-poached egg is positioned adjacent to the chicken, showing a smooth, matte white exterior. Bright yellow lemon zest curls are scattered over the greens. The dish is presented on a flat white ceramic plate with ample negative space. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the contrast between the dark green spinach and the golden-brown chicken. A silver fork rests on a folded white cotton napkin to the right. The background is a clean, dark wood bistro table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm ciabatta bread
Pair with a crisp Pinot Grigio
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 7 minutes per side until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from the skillet and brush with 80g of pesto.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes.
In a separate pan, sauté diced bacon until crispy and fat is rendered.
Add baby spinach to the bacon and cook until just wilted.
Stir in lemon zest and lemon juice then remove from heat.
Poach eggs in simmering water for 3 minutes until whites are set.
Divide spinach and bacon across four plates.
Place one whole chicken breast on each bed of spinach.
Position one poached egg next to each chicken breast.
Drizzle the remaining pesto around the plate.
notes: Ensure eggs are fresh for optimal poaching results
Do not overcook spinach to maintain its bright color

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Brown Butter Chocolate Chip Cookie
recipes.visual_description: A single thick wedge of a golden-brown skillet cookie sits on a rustic white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim. The cookie features crisp, caramelized edges and a soft, chewy center studded with large pools of melted dark chocolate. The surface shows the characteristic crinkle of a well-baked cookie, glistening with a light sprinkle of flaky sea salt. In the background, a seasoned black cast iron skillet rests on a well-used wooden dining table, suggesting the cookie was freshly baked. A simple metal fork lies beside the plate on a clean white cloth napkin. The lighting is warm and inviting, coming from a nearby kitchen window, highlighting the rich textures and deep amber tones of the brown butter dough.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm directly from the skillet for family-style dining
Top with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream
Pair with a cold glass of whole milk
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C.
Melt butter in a 20 cm cast iron skillet over medium heat.
Cook butter until it turns golden brown and smells nutty.
Remove skillet from heat and let cool for 5 minutes.
Stir in brown sugar and white sugar until combined.
Whisk in the egg and vanilla extract.
Fold in flour, baking soda, and sea salt until a dough forms.
Mix in chocolate chips.
Spread dough evenly across the skillet.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until edges are golden.
Sprinkle with flaky sea salt while hot.
Cool slightly before serving.
notes: Do not overbake the cookie to ensure a soft, fudgy center.
The residual heat from the cast iron skillet will continue cooking the dough after removal from the oven.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Avocado with Chorizo and Corn
recipes.visual_description: Two warm avocado halves rest on a minimalist white porcelain plate. The bright green, buttery flesh of the avocados holds a mound of savory filling. This filling features small chunks of crispy, dark red sautéed chorizo mixed with golden charred sweet corn kernels and finely diced translucent red onions. A delicate drizzle of white crema Mexicana creates a stark contrast against the colorful ingredients. Crumbled white cotija cheese and bright green cilantro leaves are scattered across the top. The plate sits on a natural wood surface with a folded white cotton napkin and a lime wedge. Soft, natural daylight emphasizes the rich textures and organic shapes of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with a side of pickled red onions
Pair with a crisp Mexican lager or hibiscus tea
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Remove chorizo from casing.
Sauté chorizo in a skillet over medium heat until crispy.
Add corn, onion, garlic, and jalapeño to the skillet.
Cook 5 minutes until vegetables soften and char slightly.
Halve avocados and remove pits.
Scoop out 15ml of flesh from the center of each half.
Place avocado halves on a baking sheet.
Fill centers generously with the chorizo and corn mixture.
Bake for 10 minutes until avocado is warm.
Drizzle with crema Mexicana.
Top with crumbled cotija cheese and cilantro.
Serve immediately with lime wedges.
notes: Ensure avocados are ripe but still firm to hold their shape during baking.
Substitute feta cheese if cotija is unavailable.
Use a spoon to gently enlarge the pit cavity for more filling.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sea Bass with Roasted Beet Purée
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant, smooth roasted beet purée spread in a fluid circle on a clean white porcelain plate. A single, thick whole sea bass fillet sits centered atop the purée, its skin seared to a crisp, golden-brown texture. The fish is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. Drizzled over the fish and around the plate is a bright vinaigrette containing whole green capers and finely grated white parmesan cheese. Coarsely cracked black pepper and small sprigs of flat-leaf parsley provide textural contrast. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table, a white cotton napkin, and stainless steel cutlery. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy oil and the flaky white fish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of chilled Vermentino or Sauvignon Blanc
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the beet purée
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wrap beets in foil and roast for 45 minutes until tender.
Peel roasted beets and blend with 30ml olive oil until smooth.
Season beet purée with salt and set aside.
Whisk remaining olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, capers, and parmesan in a bowl.
Season sea bass fillets with salt and black pepper.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-high heat with a splash of oil.
Place fish skin-side down in the pan.
Press firmly for 30 seconds to ensure even skin contact.
Sear for 4 minutes until skin is crisp and golden.
Flip fish and cook for 2 minutes until internal temperature reaches 63°C.
Spread beet purée on plates and top with whole fish fillets.
Spoon caper-parmesan vinaigrette over the fish.
notes: Pat the fish skin completely dry with paper towels before cooking to ensure maximum crispness.
The beet purée can be made a day in advance and gently reheated.

recipes.recipe_name: Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
recipes.visual_description: The entire plate is captured in a professional shot. The dish is presented in a traditional wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl. Steamed long-grain Basmati rice displays a mix of snow-white and saffron-infused yellow grains. Large, moist chunks of marinated and steamed bone-in chicken thighs are buried partially in the rice, coated in a dark, aromatic masala. The top is scattered with crispy, deep-brown fried onions and vibrant green chopped mint and coriander. A small copper bowl of chilled cucumber raita sits to the left. The setting includes a dark wood surface, a silver spoon, and a crisp white cotton napkin. Natural light emphasizes the fluffy rice texture and the steam rising from the center. No meat is sliced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Chilled cucumber and onion raita
Mirchi ka Salan
Fresh lime wedges and sliced red onions
instructions: Mix chicken chunks, yogurt, biryani masala, ginger-garlic paste, and 10g salt.
Marinate for 60 minutes.
Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Soak rice in water for 30 minutes.
Boil 2 liters water with cloves and cardamom.
Add rice and cook until 70% tender.
Drain rice immediately.
Place marinated chicken chunks in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Spread 50g fried onions, chopped mint, and coriander over chicken.
Layer rice over the herbs and onions.
Drizzle saffron-infused milk and ghee over rice.
Seal pot lid tightly with aluminum foil.
Cook on low heat for 30 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest for 10 minutes before fluffing with a fork.
notes: Use high-quality aged Basmati rice for long, separate grains.
Do not stir the rice during the dum process to prevent breakage.

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni al Vino Rosso con Funghi e Pancetta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rigatoni is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The pasta tubes are thoroughly coated in a glossy, dark burgundy-tinted wine sauce. Thick wedges of seared, golden-brown cremini mushrooms are distributed naturally throughout the dish. Small 1cm cubes of crispy, browned bacon provide textural contrast. Finely diced translucent onions are visible within the sauce. A light dusting of finely grated snowy white parmesan cheese and a pinch of green dried oregano garnish the top. The bowl sits on a dark oak wooden table with a folded grey cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the reflective surface of the emulsified sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of the same red wine used in the sauce
Accompany with crusty ciabatta bread
Provide extra grated parmesan at the table
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Cook rigatoni until al dente. Reserve 100ml of pasta water before draining.
Dice bacon into 1cm cubes. Sauté in a large pan over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon and set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Sauté in the remaining bacon fat until translucent.
Cut mushrooms into thick wedges. Add to the pan and sear until deep golden brown.
Stir in the dried oregano. Pour in the red wine to deglaze the pan. Simmer until the liquid reduces by half.
Add the cooked pasta and crispy bacon to the pan.
Stir in the grated parmesan and reserved pasta water. Toss vigorously to create a glossy, emulsified sauce.
Season with black pepper. Serve immediately.
notes: Use a dry red wine like Chianti or Sangiovese for authenticity
Ensure the mushrooms are seared, not steamed, by not overcrowding the pan
The sauce should be fluid and coat the pasta entirely through the mantecatura process

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Pizzaiola with Arugula and Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a whole, golden-brown seared chicken breast nestled in a vibrant, chunky tomato sauce. The sauce contains visible pieces of softened diced onion and minced garlic, flecked with dried oregano. Fresh basil leaves are torn and scattered over the chicken. Beside the chicken sits a mounded heap of bright green arugula leaves, lightly coated in a clear vinaigrette. Large, thin shards of parmesan cheese are draped over the arugula. The meal is served on a clean white porcelain plate. The lighting is natural and bright, highlighting the glossy sauce and the matte texture of the cheese. A simple wooden table and a folded white cotton napkin complete the bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to soak up the sauce
Pair with a medium-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti
instructions: Dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat 20 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 4 minutes per side until golden.
Remove chicken from the skillet and set aside.
Add onion to the same skillet and sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer for 10 minutes on low heat.
Return chicken to the skillet. Cover with sauce.
Cook until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Whisk remaining 25 ml olive oil and red wine vinegar in a bowl.
Toss arugula in the vinaigrette.
Place one whole chicken breast on each plate.
Spoon tomato sauce over the chicken.
Garnish with torn basil and shaved parmesan cheese.
Serve the dressed arugula immediately on the side.
notes: Ensure the pan is hot before adding chicken to achieve a proper sear.
Use a vegetable peeler to create thin, professional parmesan shards.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut Chicken Ramen
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Coconut Chicken Ramen is presented in a deep, matte-black ceramic bowl on a light oak table. The creamy, pale-yellow broth partially covers a mound of wavy ramen noodles. Five large, golden-brown seared chicken thigh chunks are clustered on the right, showing a caramelized exterior. On the left, a vibrant nest of fresh, dark green arugula leaves adds height and texture. Thinly sliced red bird's eye chilies and a lime wedge provide pops of color. A pair of dark wood chopsticks and a ceramic soup spoon rest on a clean white cotton napkin beside the bowl. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the glossy surface of the broth and the rustic textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of chili oil for adjustable heat
Use chopsticks and a flat-bottomed ceramic soup spoon
Serve with extra lime wedges on the side
instructions: Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add minced ginger and garlic to the same pot. Sauté for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth and coconut milk.
Simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in fish sauce and lime juice.
Cook ramen noodles in boiling water separately. Drain.
Place noodles into four deep bowls.
Pour hot broth over noodles.
Top with seared chicken chunks and fresh arugula.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C
Do not overcook the arugula to maintain its peppery bite
Rinse ramen noodles in hot water after draining to prevent sticking

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Wheat Galettes with Poached Eggs
recipes.visual_description: A single rustic wheat galette sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The pastry crust is baked to a deep golden-brown with visible flakiness and irregular hand-folded edges. The center is filled with a concentrated layer of dark mahogany caramelized onions. Resting directly on top of the onions is a whole, perfectly translucent poached egg with a soft, rounded shape. A small sprig of fresh green thyme is placed off-center on the egg. The setting is a modern French bistro with a light oak wood table. A crisp white linen napkin and silver fork are placed to the left. Natural afternoon light creates soft shadows across the plate's negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light lunch or 'plat principal' for dinner
Accompany with a simple green salad with vinaigrette
Provide a sharp steak knife for cutting through the crust
instructions: Mix flour, 5g salt, and 5g sugar in a bowl.
Add 80ml oil and cold water. Mix until dough forms.
Wrap dough. Chill for 30 minutes.
Slice onions into thin rings.
Heat 20ml oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add onions, remaining sugar, and salt. Sauté until dark brown.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
Divide dough into four balls. Roll each into 15cm circles.
Place caramelized onions in the center of each circle. Fold edges inward.
Beat one egg. Brush dough edges with egg wash.
Bake galettes for 20 minutes until golden brown.
Simmer water in a deep pan. Add a splash of vinegar.
Crack remaining 4 eggs into water. Poach for 3 minutes.
Place one warm poached egg on the center of each galette.
Garnish with fresh thyme.
notes: Ensure water for poaching is at a bare simmer to keep egg whites intact
Chill the dough thoroughly to prevent shrinkage during baking
Caramelize onions slowly to develop deep umami flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Stir-Fried Banana Blossom and Water Spinach with Arame
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the stir-fry is presented on a shallow, dark teal hand-glazed ceramic plate. The central focus is the banana blossom, cut into thin, pale cream ribbons with subtle purple edges. Intertwined are vibrant green 5cm hollow water spinach stems and dark, thread-like strands of arame seaweed. Small red chili rounds and golden minced lemongrass are scattered throughout. The vegetables have a glossy, light sheen from the wok sear. A neat cluster of crushed toasted peanuts sits on top. The plate is set on a light oak table next to dark wooden chopsticks and a small ceramic bowl containing a lime wedge. Natural side lighting emphasizes the crisp texture of the stems.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed jasmine rice
Provide extra lime wedges and fresh bird's eye chilies on the side
Use a shared dipping bowl of soy sauce with chili
instructions: Soak arame in warm water for 10 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Prepare a bowl of water with half a lime squeezed in.
Thinly slice banana blossom into 3mm rounds. Soak in lime water immediately.
Cut water spinach into 5cm lengths. Separate stems from leaves.
Finely mince the white parts of lemongrass and garlic.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Sauté lemongrass and garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add drained banana blossom and arame. Stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add water spinach stems. Toss for 1 minute.
Add water spinach leaves and sliced chili. Stir-fry until leaves wilt.
Stir in soy sauce and sugar. Toss to coat evenly.
Remove from heat. Serve immediately topped with crushed peanuts.
notes: Soaking banana blossom in acidulated water is essential to prevent oxidation and bitterness.
Do not overcook the water spinach; the stems should remain crunchy.

recipes.recipe_name: Murgh Tikka
recipes.visual_description: Present five large, succulent chunks of roasted chicken tikka on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken shows deep orange hues with distinct dark charred edges from high-heat roasting. Arrange the chunks in an organic, slightly overlapping cluster in the center, ensuring meat remains whole and never sliced. Garnish with vibrant green fresh coriander sprigs and three thin rings of crisp red onion. Place a bright yellow lemon wedge on the side. The background features a rustic wooden table with a small ceramic bowl of smooth green mint chutney and a folded piece of warm, charred naan bread. Soft, natural daylight highlights the moist texture and spice-crusted surface of the meat.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh naan or paratha
Accompany with mint-yogurt chutney
Provide a side of laccha pyaaz (pickled onion rings)
instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Cut chicken into 4 cm chunks.
Whisk yogurt, salt, pepper, ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, garam masala, lemon juice, and mustard oil in a bowl.
Add chicken chunks and coat thoroughly.
Marinate in the refrigerator for 4 hours.
Preheat oven to 230°C.
Thread chicken chunks onto metal skewers.
Place skewers on a wire rack over a baking tray.
Roast for 15-18 minutes until edges are charred and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest meat for 5 minutes.
Garnish with chopped coriander.
notes: Mustard oil provides the traditional pungent aroma
Do not overcrowd the skewers to ensure even charring
Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Mugwort and Hawthorn Rice Cake
recipes.visual_description: A dense, circular steamed rice cake with an earthy, moss-green color from the mugwort. The cake sits on a textured, matte-cream ceramic plate. One thick, triangular wedge is removed and placed beside the main cake. The top surface features a glossy, translucent glaze studded with softened, deep-red hawthorn berry chunks and whole, pale-yellow honeysuckle flowers. The texture appears moist and aerated. The setting is a rustic stone tabletop with a natural linen napkin. Lighting is soft and directional, highlighting the organic textures of the cake. A single branch of dried honeysuckle lies nearby as a minimalist accent. The presentation is clean, honoring traditional East Asian aesthetic simplicity and seasonal foraging.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm roasted barley tea
Present on a traditional wooden tray
Enjoy as a mid-afternoon seasonal snack

ingredients.name: Fresh hawthorn berries, pitted and diced

instructions: Whisk rice flour, sugar, salt, and mugwort powder in a bowl.
Combine Makgeolli and warm water.
Stir liquids into the flour mixture until a thick batter forms.
Cover bowl with a damp cloth.
Ferment in a warm place for 4 hours until bubbles appear.
Fold half of the diced hawthorn berries into the batter.
Line a steamer basket with a wet linen cloth.
Pour batter into a 15cm circular mold inside the steamer.
Steam over boiling water for 20 minutes.
Turn off heat and let rest for 5 minutes.
Simmer honey, honeysuckle, and remaining hawthorn in a small pan for 3 minutes.
Remove cake from mold and brush with the warm honeysuckle hawthorn glaze.
notes: Ensure Makgeolli is raw and active for proper fermentation
Use the hawthorn pits to simmer in water for a zero-waste tea base
Adjust fermentation time based on ambient room temperature

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Grilled Chicken with Avocado Crema
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole, charred grilled chicken thighs resting on a crisp bed of shredded Romaine lettuce. The chicken exhibits deep reddish-brown grill marks and a succulent sheen. Beside the chicken, a vibrant mound of salsa consists of 1cm diced Roma tomatoes and English cucumbers, speckled with bright green chopped coriander. A smooth, thick dollop of pale green avocado-coriander crema is positioned next to the meat, showing a velvety, matte texture. The arrangement is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, providing moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wooden table, accompanied by a small side basket of warm corn tortillas and a lime wedge.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas in a cloth-lined basket
Accompany with fresh lime wedges for acidity
Provide a side of pickled red onions for traditional crunch
instructions: Whisk olive oil, 20ml lime juice, cumin, and paprika in a bowl.
Coat chicken thighs in the marinade and rest for 20 minutes.
Dice tomatoes and cucumber into 1cm cubes for the salsa.
Finely chop half of the coriander and mix with diced vegetables.
Season salsa with salt and 20ml lime juice; set aside to macerate.
Blend avocado flesh with remaining coriander and lime juice until smooth.
Grill chicken over medium-high heat until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Shred Romaine lettuce into thin ribbons for the base.
Place a bed of lettuce on each plate and top with two whole chicken thighs.
Spoon salsa over the chicken and finish with a dollop of avocado crema.
notes: Use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe 75°C internal temperature
Keep the salsa chilled until the moment of serving to maintain the contrast between hot chicken and cold vegetables
If the crema is too thick, add a teaspoon of water or oil to reach desired consistency

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Broccoli and Toasted Breadcrumbs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Orecchiette with Broccoli served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The pasta is coated in a glossy, vibrant green sauce made from emulsified olive oil and partially mashed broccoli. Whole, tender-crisp broccoli florets and small cubes of stems are distributed evenly throughout the bowl. A generous dusting of coarse, golden-brown toasted sourdough breadcrumbs covers the top. Fine strands of bright yellow lemon zest provide a color accent. The dish sits on a light oak wood table. A folded white cotton napkin and a heavy-bottomed glass of water are placed nearby. Natural side-lighting highlights the texture of the pasta and the crunch of the breadcrumbs. The composition is clean with ample negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of marinated olives
Accompany with a glass of dry white Italian wine
Provide extra chili flakes in a small ceramic bowl
instructions: Bring 4 liters of water to a boil.
Add 40 grams of salt to the water.
Cut broccoli into 2 cm florets and 1 cm diced stems.
Heat 20 ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Toast breadcrumbs until golden brown and remove from pan.
Blanch broccoli in boiling water for 3 minutes.
Remove broccoli with a slotted spoon and keep water boiling.
Add orecchiette to the same water and cook until al dente.
Sauté sliced garlic and chili in remaining olive oil in a large pan.
Add broccoli to the pan and sauté for 2 minutes.
Transfer pasta to the pan with 100 ml of pasta water.
Toss pasta vigorously to emulsify the sauce.
Garnish with lemon zest and toasted breadcrumbs.
notes: Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for the emulsion
Ensure the pasta water is well-salted for flavor
The broccoli stems provide essential texture and should not be discarded

recipes.recipe_name: Aguardiente Flambéed Chorizo and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is presented in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with a rustic matte finish. The dish consists of thick, 2cm chunks of seared, mahogany-colored chorizo and golden-brown baby potato halves. The ingredients are tossed together in a natural, casual mound, showing glistening surfaces from the aguardiente reduction. Dark specks of adobo seasoning are visible on the crispy potato skins. The arrangement is asymmetrical and fills the bowl comfortably. A light scattering of roughly chopped bright green cilantro provides a fresh contrast against the warm tones of the meat and potatoes. The bowl rests on a weathered wooden table under soft, warm kitchen lighting, with the entire plate clearly visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges on the side
Provide wooden toothpicks for a traditional picada-style experience
Accompany with a small side of hogao sauce
instructions: Boil baby potatoes in salted water for 12 minutes until tender.
Drain potatoes and cut into halves.
Cut chorizo into 2cm thick chunks.
Finely dice the onion and mince the garlic.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chorizo chunks. Sear 4 minutes until browned and fat renders.
Add potatoes, onion, and garlic to the skillet.
Sprinkle adobo seasoning over the ingredients. Toss to coat evenly.
Fry 5 minutes until potatoes are golden and crispy.
Pour aguardiente into the pan. Simmer 2 minutes until liquid reduces to a thick glaze.
Remove from heat and garnish with chopped cilantro.
notes: Ensure potatoes are dry before adding to the skillet for maximum crispiness
Use a high-quality anise-flavored aguardiente for authentic flavor
If using raw chorizo, ensure it is cooked to an internal temperature of 71°C

recipes.recipe_name: Aloo Gajar Matar
recipes.visual_description: The dish features 2cm cubes of golden-brown sautéed potatoes and 3cm batons of vibrant orange carrots, neatly arranged in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The vegetables are coated in a shimmering, savory spice blend with visible cumin seeds and finely diced translucent onions. Fresh, bright green cilantro leaves are scattered across the top for contrast. The bowl sits on a dark wood table next to a folded, warm whole-wheat roti showing charred spots. A small side dish of cooling cucumber raita in a matching white ceramic bowl provides balance. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the tender-crisp vegetables and the matte finish of the traditional flatbread.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm whole-wheat roti or paratha
Accompany with cucumber raita
Include a side of spicy mango pickle
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Peel and cut carrots into 3cm batons.
Finely dice onions.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and toast until fragrant.
Add onions and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add turmeric, coriander powder, and salt.
Add potatoes and carrots to the pan.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes until tender.
Sprinkle with garam masala and chopped cilantro.
notes: Ensure potatoes and carrots are cut uniformly for even cooking.
Add a splash of water if the spices begin to stick to the pan.

recipes.recipe_name: Buttermilk Marinated Beef Chunks with Oregano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of buttermilk-marinated beef is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The beef consists of four large, 4cm thick chunks, seared to a deep mahogany brown with visible flecks of dried oregano. The meat is arranged in a natural cluster in the center, not fanned or sliced. Beside the beef are roasted potato wedges and charred red bell pepper batons. A light, creamy buttermilk-oregano reduction is drizzled partially over the meat and onto the plate's negative space. Fresh bright green oregano sprigs garnish the top. The dish sits on a light oak bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and polished silver cutlery. Soft, natural window lighting highlights the textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm pita bread
Lemon wedges
Kalamata olives
Chilled Assyrtiko wine
instructions: Whisk buttermilk, dried oregano, and minced garlic in a bowl.
Add beef chunks to the marinade.
Refrigerate for 4 hours.
Remove beef from marinade.
Pat beef dry with paper towels.
Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat.
Add beef chunks to the pan.
Sear for 3 minutes per side until browned.
Transfer beef to a plate.
Rest meat for 5 minutes.
Deglaze the skillet with lemon juice.
Whisk in 30ml of fresh buttermilk.
Simmer for 1 minute.
Pour sauce over the beef chunks.
Garnish with fresh oregano.
notes: Patting the beef dry is essential for a proper crust.
Do not boil the buttermilk sauce vigorously to prevent separation.
Use a cast iron skillet for the best heat retention during searing.

recipes.recipe_name: Compressed Garden Composition with Tomato Essence and Avocado Crème
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a large, minimalist white Carrara marble slab. It features four artistic clusters of ingredients arranged in an organic, flowing composition. Compressed Gem lettuce wedges appear translucent and jewel-toned. Beside them are 2cm English cucumber batons, lightly torched on one side for a subtle char. Bright red, translucent 1cm cubes of clarified tomato water gelée provide a crystalline contrast. Smooth avocado crème is piped in precise, varying-sized spheres across the plate. The arrangement is finished with droplets of deep green coriander oil and tiny coriander micro-leaves. High-contrast professional lighting emphasizes the textures and provides depth with soft shadows. Abundant negative space creates a sophisticated, Michelin-starred aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a shared starter on a communal marble plinth
Pair with chilled sparkling botanical water
instructions: Blend tomatoes into a coarse puree.
Strain puree through a coffee filter overnight to collect clear tomato water.
Boil 200ml of tomato water with agar-agar for 1 minute.
Pour into a flat tray and chill until set.
Cut the gel into 1cm cubes.
Cut lettuce into wedges and vacuum-seal with 10ml lime juice for 30 minutes.
Peel cucumber and cut into 2cm batons.
Blanch coriander for 10 seconds then shock in ice water.
Blend dried coriander with oil and strain through a fine sieve.
Process avocado with remaining lime juice and salt until smooth.
Pass avocado through a fine tamis and place in a piping bag.
Arrange lettuce, cucumber batons, and tomato cubes in organic clusters on a plate.
Pipe avocado dots of varying sizes and drizzle with coriander oil.
notes: Ensure the tomato water is completely clear for the best visual impact
Use a kitchen torch briefly on the cucumber for a hint of smoke without softening the crunch

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Salsa de Sofrito y Serrano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised chicken thighs served in a wide, shallow white ceramic bowl. Two whole bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs sit atop a bed of fluffy long-grain white rice. The chicken features a deep golden-brown seared skin, partially coated in a thick, vibrant orange-red sofrito sauce. Visible small dices of softened onions and green bell peppers cling to the meat. Two whole charred serrano peppers rest alongside the chicken. A garnish of coarsely chopped fresh cilantro and a single lime wedge adds a pop of green. The plate sits on a dark wood table with a folded white cotton napkin and a heavy silver fork. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy sauce texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with a side of black beans
Provide extra hot sauce for personal heat adjustment

ingredients.name: sofrito (minced onion, garlic, bell pepper, cilantro)

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Season chicken with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the skillet.
Sear chicken for 6 minutes until skin is golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and sear for 3 minutes.
Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add sofrito and serrano peppers to the same skillet.
Sauté for 4 minutes until fragrant and softened.
Stir in tomato paste, oregano, and cumin.
Cook for 2 minutes until paste darkens.
Pour in chicken stock and scrape the bottom of the pan.
Return chicken to the skillet skin-side up.
Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 15 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and increase heat to reduce sauce by half.
Pour sauce over chicken and garnish with cilantro.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches a minimum internal temperature of 75°C for safety.
Do not cover the pan during the final simmer to keep the chicken skin crisp.
Adjust serrano quantity based on desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Coconut Panna Cotta with Mango and Acerola
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single, smooth ivory-colored coconut panna cotta centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The panna cotta has a firm yet delicate wobble. It is topped with a neat pile of vibrant orange mango cubes, precisely cut into 1cm squares. A deep crimson acerola syrup is drizzled artfully over the mango and pools slightly at the base of the panna cotta. Toasted golden-brown shredded coconut is scattered over the top, adding a textural contrast. A single bright green mint sprig provides a color accent. The setting is a light wood table with a white cotton napkin. Lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the glossy finish of the syrup and the creamy texture of the coconut base.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a refreshing palate cleanser
Pair with Brazilian cafezinho
instructions: Combine coconut milk, 40g sugar, and agar-agar in a saucepan.
Whisk constantly over medium heat.
Bring to a boil for 1 minute to activate agar-agar.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract.
Pour mixture into 4 individual molds.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours until set.
Combine acerola puree, 20g sugar, and lime juice in a small pan.
Simmer over low heat until reduced by half.
Cool the acerola syrup completely.
Dice mangoes into 1cm cubes.
Unmold panna cotta onto the center of each plate.
Top with mango cubes.
Drizzle acerola syrup over the fruit.
Garnish with toasted coconut and mint.
notes: Ensure agar-agar boils for a full minute to ensure proper setting
Select mangoes with high fragrance for the best flavor balance

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Artichokes with Amaranth and Balsamic Onions
recipes.visual_description: A single serving sits on a clean white porcelain plate atop a light wood table. The base is a fluid, creamy pool of pale amaranth. Two whole braised artichoke halves are positioned centrally, showing tender, herb-flecked leaves. Thick wedges of red onion, glazed to a deep glossy purple with balsamic vinegar, are arranged beside the artichokes. A rustic topping of chopped black olives, capers, and fresh parsley adds texture and dark green contrast. The arrangement is organic and centered with generous negative space. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the moist textures of the vegetables and the sheen of the reduction. A simple cotton napkin and silver fork complete the authentic bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a chilled dry white wine
Present on a hand-painted ceramic platter for family-style service
instructions: Rinse amaranth in a fine-mesh sieve.
Bring 750ml vegetable stock to a boil.
Add amaranth. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in butter. Keep warm.
Clean artichokes by removing tough outer leaves. Trim stems and tops. Cut in half lengthwise.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a wide pan.
Sear artichokes cut-side down for 3 minutes. Add rosemary and thyme.
Pour 250ml stock over artichokes. Cover. Simmer 15 minutes until tender.
Slice red onions into 1cm thick wedges.
Sauté onions in remaining oil until soft and translucent.
Add balsamic vinegar. Simmer until liquid reduces to a thick glaze.
Finely chop olives, capers, and parsley. Mix together.
Spread amaranth onto four plates in a fluid circle.
Place artichoke halves and onion wedges on the grain.
Top with the olive and caper mixture.
notes: Ensure amaranth remains fluid and not dry by adding extra stock if needed
Remove the fuzzy 'choke' from larger artichokes using a spoon
Use high-quality aged balsamic for a sweeter glaze

recipes.recipe_name: Bhuna Murgh
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Bhuna Murgh presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features large 4cm chunks of tender chicken thighs, pan-roasted until deeply browned. The chicken is coated in a thick, concentrated masala sauce with a rich mahogany hue, showing visible texture from slow-cooked onions. Garnished with vibrant green coriander leaves, fine ginger julienne, and a single slit green chili for color contrast. The chicken is arranged in a natural, rustic mound in the center, leaving clear space around the rim. The plate sits on a dark wooden bistro table alongside a piece of blistered garlic naan and a small bowl of yogurt raita. Soft natural lighting highlights the glossy sauce and spice textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or tandoori roti
Accompany with a side of cucumber raita to balance the spice
Provide a fresh kachumber salad of diced onions, tomatoes, and cucumbers
Traditional brass or copper serving spoons enhance the table setting
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add diced onions. Sauté until they reach a deep golden brown color.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides.
Add chili powder, coriander powder, and turmeric. Stir well to coat chicken.
Pour in tomato puree. Cook for 3 minutes until slightly reduced.
Lower heat to minimum. Slowly stir in whisked yogurt.
Cover pan. Simmer until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove lid. Increase heat to medium-high. Stir constantly until sauce thickens and oil separates from the masala.
Sprinkle with garam masala. Stir once and remove from heat.
notes: The secret to a good bhuna is the slow browning of the onions.
Do not add water; the chicken should cook in its own juices and the yogurt.
Ensure the yogurt is at room temperature to prevent curdling when adding to the pan.

recipes.recipe_name: Applewood Smoked Arctic Char with Charcoal Arepas and Adobo Tomato Jelly
recipes.visual_description: A single whole pan-seared Arctic Char fillet sits at the center of a matte white porcelain plate. The skin is crispy and golden-pink. Two thick, jet-black charcoal arepa discs are positioned to the side. Small, translucent red cubes of adobo-spiced tomato jelly are scattered naturally around the fish. A light aguardiente reduction glaze coats the char, catching the light. Fresh cilantro leaves provide a green contrast. The background is a rustic wooden bistro table with a folded white linen napkin and a small bowl of ají sauce. Natural side lighting highlights the flaky texture of the fish and the matte finish of the charcoal arepas.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Colombian ají pique
Pair with a chilled glass of aguardiente or a light beer
Present on traditional ceramic La Chamba pottery if available
instructions: Mix corn flour, charcoal powder, salt, and 300ml warm water in a bowl.
Knead until smooth. Form into 8 thick circular discs.
Heat 15ml oil in a skillet. Fry arepas 5 minutes per side until crisp. Keep warm.
Place applewood chips in a smoker box or heavy pot. Smoke char fillets for 10 minutes at low heat.
Blend tomatoes and strain through a fine sieve to collect 250ml juice.
Combine tomato juice, adobo seasoning, vinegar, and agar in a small saucepan.
Bring to a boil while whisking. Simmer for 1 minute.
Pour liquid into a shallow rectangular tray. Refrigerate for 20 minutes until set.
Cut the firm tomato jelly into 1cm small cubes.
Heat remaining oil in a pan. Sear smoked char fillets skin-side down for 4 minutes.
Flip the fish. Pour in aguardiente and ignite carefully with a long match to flambé.
Cook 1 minute more until the flame extinguishes and fish is opaque.
Place one whole fillet on each plate. Arrange two arepas and several jelly cubes alongside.
notes: Ensure the charcoal powder is food-grade
Do not overcook the char to maintain its delicate moisture
The tomato jelly must be completely cold to hold its cube shape

recipes.recipe_name: Mirza Ghasemi (Persian Smoked Eggplant and Tomato)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mirza Ghasemi served in a shallow, rustic terracotta bowl. The base is a thick, textured mash of smoky eggplant and concentrated tomatoes, showing a deep reddish-orange hue with visible charred eggplant flecks. Four whole poached eggs are nestled into the mixture, their whites opaque and yolks bright yellow and runny. Small chunks of softened garlic are visible throughout the mash. The dish is presented on a dark, weathered wooden table. Beside the bowl sits a stack of folded Persian Lavash flatbread and a small side plate of fresh mint leaves and sliced red radishes. The lighting is warm and directional, highlighting the oily sheen and rustic texture of the eggplant dip.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm Persian flatbread such as Sangak or Lavash
Accompany with Sabzi Khordan (fresh herbs like mint, basil, and tarragon)
Include sliced radishes and walnuts on the side
instructions: Char the whole eggplants over an open flame or under a broiler until skin is blackened and flesh is soft.
Place charred eggplants in a bowl and cover with plastic wrap for 10 minutes to steam.
Peel the skins and discard. Finely chop or mash the eggplant flesh.
Score an 'X' on the bottom of the tomatoes. Blanch in boiling water for 30 seconds, then peel and dice into small cubes.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add minced garlic and turmeric. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Add the diced tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 10 minutes until the liquid evaporates and they form a thick paste.
Stir in the mashed eggplant, salt, and pepper. Cook for another 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Create four small wells in the mixture. Crack one egg into each well.
Cover the skillet and cook for 5 minutes until the egg whites are set but yolks remain soft.
Stir the eggs slightly into the top layer of the mixture before serving if desired, or leave whole.
notes: For the most authentic flavor, char the eggplant over charcoal to maximize the smoky aroma.
Ensure the tomato liquid is fully reduced before adding eggplant to prevent a watery consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Parmigiana with Fresh Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a whole, golden-brown breaded chicken breast centered on a clean white porcelain plate. Thick, melted rounds of fresh white mozzarella cheese cover the top surface, showing light toasted brown spots from the broiler. A vibrant, chunky red marinara sauce peeps through the edges of the cheese. The chicken maintains a visible crispy panko texture on the exposed sides. Torn emerald-green basil leaves provide a fresh color contrast. The plate rests on a rustic oak table alongside a white cotton napkin and silver flatware. Natural light highlights the creamy pull of the cheese and the rich color of the tomato sauce. Moderate negative space surrounds the chicken, creating a clean, professional bistro presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a portion of spaghetti pomodoro
Pair with a simple arugula salad with lemon vinaigrette
Provide extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Place flour in one shallow bowl.
Beat eggs in a second shallow bowl.
Mix panko and Parmesan in a third shallow bowl.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour. Shake off excess.
Dip chicken into beaten eggs to coat.
Press chicken firmly into panko mixture to create a thick crust.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry chicken 4 minutes per side until deep golden brown.
Transfer chicken to a baking dish.
Spoon 125ml marinara sauce over the center of each breast.
Place thick chunks of mozzarella on top of the sauce.
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes.
Verify chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Garnish with torn basil leaves before serving.
notes: Do not slice the chicken before serving to maintain heat and moisture
Use high-quality fresh mozzarella stored in water for the best melt
Ensure the oil is hot before adding chicken to prevent a soggy crust

recipes.recipe_name: Cucumber and Savory Agar Jelly Salad
recipes.visual_description: Cucumber and Savory Agar Jelly Salad is presented in a wide, off-white ceramic bowl on a rustic wooden table. The dish features translucent, pale yellow agar strips, cut into 1cm wide batons, mixed with thinly sliced cucumber rounds and fine julienne red onions. A creamy, white yogurt dressing is drizzled over the vegetables, partially coating the components. The salad is topped with a scattering of crushed roasted peanuts, bright red chili flakes, and fresh chopped cilantro. The arrangement is casual and mounded, reflecting a homestyle meal. A simple stainless steel spoon rests on a neutral linen napkin beside the bowl. Natural, warm light emphasizes the diverse textures of the jelly and crisp vegetables. The entire plate is visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a refreshing side dish alongside steamed jasmine rice.
Accompany with a spicy meat or vegetable curry to balance the heat.
instructions: Mix water, agar, and turmeric in a small pot.
Boil for 2 minutes over medium heat while stirring.
Pour the liquid into a flat rectangular tray.
Cool at room temperature until the jelly is firm.
Slice the set agar jelly into 1cm wide batons.
Slice the cucumbers into thin rounds.
Julienne the red onion into thin strips.
Whisk yogurt, lime juice, and salt in a small bowl.
Combine agar batons, cucumber rounds, and onion strips in a large bowl.
Drizzle the yogurt dressing over the ingredients.
Top with crushed peanuts, chili flakes, and chopped cilantro.
notes: Ensure the agar powder is fully dissolved before the water reaches a boil.
The turmeric provides a traditional golden color to the savory jelly strips.

recipes.recipe_name: Adjika-Glazed Abalone and Mushroom Mousse
recipes.visual_description: A single portion sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate atop a light oak wood table. The base is a smooth, circular mound of pale ivory fish tofu mousse. Resting atop the mousse is one whole, glossy abalone, glazed in a translucent amber syrup flecked with red adjika. Three thick chunks of abalone mushroom are nestled beside the abalone, their surfaces shimmering with the same glaze. Fine, golden-brown threads of candied dried scallop are scattered over the top. The arrangement is organic and clean. Natural light highlights the textures of the syrup and the porous mushrooms. A modern silver spoon and a white cotton napkin are placed neatly beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a cup of warm Oolong tea
Use a small dessert spoon for the delicate mousse
instructions: Soak dried scallops in water for 2 hours.
Steam scallops for 30 minutes until soft.
Shred scallops into fine fibers.
Fry scallop fibers with 20g sugar until golden and crispy.
Blend fish tofu and heavy cream until completely smooth.
Dissolve gelatin in 20ml warm water.
Whisk gelatin and 30g sugar into the tofu mixture.
Pour mixture into four small molds and refrigerate until set.
Boil water, remaining sugar, and adjika in a small pan.
Add whole abalone and thick mushroom chunks to the syrup.
Simmer for 10 minutes until glazed and tender.
Remove from heat and let cool to room temperature.
Place one chilled tofu mousse in the center of a plate.
Top with one whole glazed abalone.
Arrange three mushroom chunks around the abalone.
Drizzle the remaining adjika syrup over the dish.
Garnish with a pinch of crispy scallop fibers.
notes: Ensure the fish tofu is bland and fresh for the best sweet profile.
Adjust adjika quantity to control the subtle heat in the syrup.

recipes.recipe_name: Lebanese Lamb and Swiss Chard Stew
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the stew is served in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-worn wooden table. The hero ingredient, large 4cm chunks of browned, tender lamb, sits prominently in the center, partially submerged in a clear, savory broth. Vibrant green ribbons of wilted swiss chard and pale green 2cm zucchini rounds are arranged naturally around the meat. Visible bits of translucent diced onion and celery fleck the liquid. The dish is topped with a generous scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A side of lemon wedges and a small bowl of vermicelli rice sit nearby. Warm, natural kitchen lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the moist texture of the meat and the glossy vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Lebanese vermicelli rice
Accompany with fresh pita bread
Provide extra lemon wedges for acidity

ingredients.name: Swiss chard, leaves chopped, stems diced

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown lamb chunks on all sides until dark gold. Remove lamb and set aside.
Add onion, celery, and chard stems to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return lamb to the pot. Add water, salt, and black pepper.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add zucchini rounds and chopped chard leaves to the pot.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Stir in lemon juice and parsley. Adjust salt to taste.
Serve hot in deep bowls.
notes: Ensure lamb is browned well for deep flavor
Do not overcook chard leaves to maintain color
Substitute beef for lamb if preferred

recipes.recipe_name: Spinach and Feta Tagliatelle with Lemon and Dill
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a light oak wooden table. Tagliatelle pasta is swirled into a neat mound in the center. Vibrant green sautéed baby spinach leaves are folded through the pasta ribbons. Large 1cm cubes of white Greek feta cheese are scattered on top, maintaining their shape. The pasta is coated in a light, glistening lemon-olive oil emulsion. Golden-brown toasted pine nuts and finely chopped fresh dill provide textural contrast. A single lemon wedge sits on the rim. A folded white cotton napkin and a polished silver fork are placed to the left. Natural daylight illuminates the textures from the side. The arrangement is clean and professional with balanced negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a chilled Assyrtiko wine
Present as a main course for a casual lunch
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water.
Cook tagliatelle until al dente.
Reserve 100ml of pasta cooking water.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Sauté onion until translucent.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add spinach in batches and cook until wilted.
Drain pasta and add to the skillet.
Pour in reserved pasta water and lemon juice.
Toss pasta to create a light emulsion.
Fold in lemon zest and half of the dill.
Add feta cubes and toss gently to warm through.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Top with toasted pine nuts and remaining dill.
notes: Do not overcook the spinach to maintain its bright green color.
Use high-quality barrel-aged feta for best flavor.
Ensure the pasta water is well-salted like the sea.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Bean and Chili Garlic Prawns with Wood Ear Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of stir-fried jumbo prawns served on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Eight large, plump prawns are arranged in a natural heap in the center, showing a glossy, dark amber glaze and light char marks from the wok. Interspersed are thick, crinkled pieces of dark wood ear mushrooms and 5cm batons of bright green scallions. The sauce is thick and clings to the seafood without pooling. A garnish of fine scallion threads sits on top. The plate sits on a dark walnut table next to a small ceramic bowl of fluffy white jasmine rice and dark wood chopsticks. Natural side lighting highlights the textures of the seared seafood and the velvety mushrooms.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Provide a small side of pickled cucumbers
Pair with hot jasmine or oolong tea

ingredients.name: Jumbo prawns, peeled and deveined, tail on
Dried wood ear mushrooms, rehydrated and torn

instructions: Pat prawns dry with paper towels.
Toss prawns with cornstarch and 5ml of oil.
Whisk chili garlic sauce, black bean paste, Maggi seasoning, MSG, and Shaoxing wine in a small bowl.
Heat 20ml oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear prawns in a single layer for 1 minute per side until charred.
Remove prawns from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to wok.
Stir-fry ginger, garlic, and scallion whites for 30 seconds.
Add wood ear mushrooms and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Return prawns to the wok.
Pour in the sauce mixture.
Toss rapidly over high heat for 1 minute to coat and thicken.
Fold in scallion greens and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding prawns to achieve wok hei flavor.
Do not overcook prawns; they are done when they turn opaque and form a C-shape.
Rehydrate wood ear mushrooms in warm water for at least 20 minutes before use.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosemary and Thyme Roasted Chicken with Toasted Couscous
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown roasted chicken thighs serves as the focal point on a large, clean white porcelain plate. The chicken remains whole, skin crisp and glistening with herb-infused oil. It rests atop a mound of light, fluffy toasted couscous studded with finely diced translucent shallots and vibrant green minced herbs. Fresh sprigs of wood-fired rosemary and thyme lean against the chicken. The plate features balanced negative space. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table. A white cotton napkin sits neatly to the side with polished silver flatware. Natural window light highlights the coarse salt crystals on the chicken skin and the individual grains of the toasted couscous.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of roasted root vegetables
Pair with a crisp white wine like Sauvignon Blanc
Offer extra virgin olive oil for drizzling at the table
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-proof skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the skillet.
Sear for 6 minutes until skin is golden and crisp.
Flip the chicken pieces.
Add crushed garlic, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs to the pan.
Transfer the skillet to the oven.
Roast chicken until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and let rest for 5 minutes.
In a separate pot, melt butter over medium heat.
Sauté diced shallots for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add couscous to the pot. Stir to coat in butter.
Toast couscous for 2 minutes until lightly fragrant.
Pour in boiling chicken stock. Cover with a lid.
Remove from heat and let sit for 5 minutes.
Fluff couscous with a fork. Stir in lemon zest and minced fresh herbs.
Place a mound of couscous on each plate.
Top with one whole roasted chicken thigh.
notes: Ensure the chicken skin is completely dry before searing for maximum crispness.
Toasting the couscous adds a nutty depth that defines the Mediterranean style.
Always check the chicken temperature at the thickest part near the bone.

recipes.recipe_name: Kimchi and Herb Stem Fritters
recipes.visual_description: Four thick, golden-brown fritters are arranged in a natural, overlapping cluster on a matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The fritters show visible textures of charred red kimchi and small green herb stem flecks. The edges appear craggy and caramelized. A small, unglazed stoneware bowl containing a smooth, pale-orange dipping sauce is positioned off-center. The entire plate is visible, set on a reclaimed light oak table with a textured grain. Soft, natural side lighting emphasizes the crispy ridges and oily sheen of the fritters. An undyed beige linen napkin sits beside the plate. The composition is clean and minimalist, highlighting the organic, rustic shapes of the snack.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a communal snack on a shared wooden board
Accompany with hot barley tea or local craft cider
Eat by hand or with bamboo chopsticks

ingredients.name: Herb stems and scallion ends, minced
Sunflower seed butter or vegan mayo

instructions: Drain kimchi over a bowl to collect all brine.
Finely chop the kimchi into small pieces.
Mince scallion ends and herb stems into 2mm bits.
Whisk chickpea flour, 30ml kimchi brine, and aquafaba in a bowl until smooth.
Fold chopped kimchi and minced stems into the batter.
Heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Drop 30ml portions of batter into the hot oil.
Flatten slightly with a spatula to form thick discs.
Fry for 3 minutes per side until deep golden brown and crispy.
Drain on a wire rack to maintain texture.
Whisk remaining brine into sunflower butter to create a dipping sauce.
notes: Aquafaba acts as a zero-waste binder instead of eggs
Use the oldest kimchi available for the most intense savory flavor
Ensure the oil is shimmering before adding batter to prevent sticking

recipes.recipe_name: Herb-Roasted Chicken with Thyme and Rosemary Couscous
recipes.visual_description: A single portion presented on a rustic, cream-colored ceramic plate with slight imperfections. The base is a generous bed of fluffy, steamed couscous dotted with tiny green flecks of chopped thyme and rosemary. Two whole, roasted chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin are placed naturally in the center. The meat is not sliced. Beside the chicken lie two soft, roasted garlic cloves and a charred lemon wedge. A single fresh rosemary sprig provides a functional garnish. The plate sits on a dark, weathered wooden table with a folded linen napkin and a simple steel fork. Warm, natural kitchen lighting highlights the glistening textures of the chicken skin and the individual grains of couscous.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain Greek yogurt
Accompany with a simple tomato and cucumber salad
Serve with warm pita bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Finely chop half of the thyme and rosemary leaves.
Rub chopped herbs and 15 ml olive oil onto chicken skin.
Heat 15 ml oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 5 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and add smashed garlic cloves to the pan.
Transfer skillet to the oven.
Roast for 20-25 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Bring chicken stock to a boil in a small pot.
Add remaining whole herb sprigs to the boiling stock.
Place couscous in a large heat-proof bowl.
Pour hot stock over couscous and cover tightly.
Let couscous sit for 5 minutes.
Remove herb sprigs and fluff couscous with a fork.
Serve two whole chicken thighs over a bed of fluffy couscous.
notes: Dry the chicken skin thoroughly for maximum crispness.
Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving to retain juices.
Use a fork to fluff the couscous to prevent clumping.

recipes.recipe_name: Aged Kimchi and Scallion Buchimgae
recipes.visual_description: Four thick, golden-brown Kimchi Buchimgae rest on a handcrafted cream-colored ceramic plate. The pancakes feature charred, crispy edges and a vibrant orange-red interior from the fermented cabbage. Visible 1cm chunks of diced kimchi and 3cm green scallion batons are embedded naturally in the textured batter. The pancakes are arranged in a casual, slightly overlapping stack. The surface has a light sheen from the sesame oil. The plate sits on a reclaimed light wood surface with a neutral linen napkin. Soft natural side-lighting emphasizes the crispy ridges and steam rising from the hot snacks. A small stone bowl of dipping sauce sits in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a soy-vinegar dipping sauce
Pair with chilled Makgeolli (Korean rice wine)
Present on a traditional wooden tray or ceramic platter
instructions: Chop aged kimchi into 1cm pieces.
Slice scallions into 3cm lengths.
Combine flour, kimchi brine, and ice-cold water in a large bowl.
Whisk gently until a thick batter forms.
Do not overmix the batter.
Fold in chopped kimchi and scallion batons.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Ladle batter into the pan to form 10cm circles.
Fry for 3 minutes until edges are golden and crispy.
Flip the pancakes.
Press down firmly with a spatula.
Cook for 2 more minutes until browned.
Drizzle with sesame oil before removing from heat.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds.
notes: Use very cold water for maximum crispiness.
The more fermented the kimchi, the deeper the flavor.
Avoid over-mixing to prevent a rubbery texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Kimchi-Braised Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: Two whole braised chicken thighs are the centerpiece, coated in a glossy, deep-crimson kimchi sauce. The chicken is surrounded by long, tender ribbons of translucent braised cabbage and 5cm green onion batons. Thick onion wedges are softened into the sauce. The dish is presented in a shallow white porcelain bowl, showing ample sauce but clean edges. A sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds and fresh red chili rounds provide texture. The setting includes a dark wooden table, stainless steel chopsticks, and a separate small bowl of fluffy white rice. Natural light emphasizes the rich red hues and moist texture of the braised meat and fermented vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bowl of steamed short-grain white rice
Accompany with danmuji (yellow pickled radish)
Provide stainless steel chopsticks and a flat spoon
Serve alongside seasoned bean sprouts (sukju namul)
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels.
Sear chicken in a heavy pot over medium-high heat until skin is golden. Remove chicken.
Sauté onion wedges in the same pot for 3 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and gochugaru. Cook for 1 minute.
Stir in kimchi, kimchi juice, soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and stock.
Return chicken to the pot, skin side up. Submerge in liquid.
Simmer covered over low heat for 30 minutes.
Add green onion lengths. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until sauce thickens.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Drizzle with sesame oil and remove from heat.
notes: Use well-fermented kimchi for the best depth of flavor.
Adjust gochugaru quantity to control heat level.
Ensure chicken skin remains partially above the liquid to maintain texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Soy and Koji Abalone
recipes.visual_description: A single whole fermented abalone rests inside its own iridescent, pearlescent shell. The abalone meat is a rich, translucent amber color from the soy-koji brine. Three small batons of white radish are neatly stacked to the side of the meat. Fine flecks of bright green minced scallions are scattered over the top. The shell is placed in the center of a shallow, handcrafted cream-colored ceramic plate. The plate sits on a textured reclaimed wood table. Soft, natural morning light highlights the glossy texture of the seafood and the matte finish of the radish. Minimalist presentation with significant negative space emphasizes the organic shapes.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with traditional brass Sujeo (spoon and chopsticks)
Accompany with a small bowl of warm toasted barley tea
Present as a single bite starter to awaken the palate
instructions: Scrub abalone shells and meat with a clean brush.
Steam whole abalone in shells for 8 minutes.
Remove meat from shells carefully. Keep shells for plating.
Trim the tough outer edges of the abalone. Save scraps for stock.
Combine soy sauce, water, koji, honey, and sliced ginger in a jar.
Cut white radish into small batons.
Place whole abalone and radish batons into the soy-koji brine.
Ferment at room temperature for 24 hours.
Transfer to refrigerator for 48 hours to develop umami.
Finely mince scallion greens for garnish.
Place one whole fermented abalone back into its cleaned shell.
Top with three radish batons and scallion greens.
notes: The koji breaks down proteins into amino acids for intense savory flavor
Use the abalone viscera to make a zero-waste porridge or sauce
Ensure the abalone is fully submerged in brine to prevent spoilage

recipes.recipe_name: Beetroot and Golden Carrot Salad with Whipped Goat Cheese and Seared Duck
recipes.visual_description: A matte black designer ceramic plate features an organic, flowing arrangement of 1cm diced salt-roasted red beetroots, pickled yellow beetroots, and golden carrots. Three 1.5cm cubes of seared duck breast with crisp, golden-brown skin are nestled among the vegetables, never fanned. Precise dots of snowy-white whipped goat cheese provide height and contrast. The dish is finished with a vibrant orange aji amarillo emulsion and droplets of deep green huacatay oil. A fine dusting of black botija olive soil adds texture and architectural interest. Abundant negative space surrounds the composition. The setting includes a dark walnut table, a folded white linen napkin, and traditional Peruvian silver forks, illuminated by dramatic professional side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a chilled glass of dry Torrontés wine.
Present on locally crafted volcanic stone or matte ceramic plates.
instructions: Dehydrate botija olives at 80°C for 4 hours.
Grind dehydrated olives into a fine soil.
Roast salt-crusted beetroots and carrots at 180°C until tender.
Peel and dice roasted vegetables into 1cm cubes.
Marinate yellow beetroots in lime juice and salt for 15 minutes.
Whip goat cheese with heavy cream until smooth and airy.
Transfer cheese to a piping bag with a plain nozzle.
Blanch huacatay leaves for 10 seconds and shock in ice water.
Blend huacatay with 30ml olive oil and strain through muslin.
Whisk aji amarillo paste with remaining lime juice and olive oil.
Score duck breast skin in a tight crosshatch pattern.
Sear duck skin-side down in a cold pan until fat renders.
Cook duck until internal temperature reaches 63°C.
Rest duck for 5 minutes and cut into 1.5cm cubes.
Toss roasted vegetables in the aji amarillo dressing.
Arrange vegetables in an organic, flowing composition on the plate.
Pipe precise goat cheese dots between the vegetable cubes.
Place 3 duck cubes skin-side up among the vegetables.
Garnish with olive soil, huacatay oil, chulpe corn, and micro-cilantro.
notes: Ensure the duck skin is rendered slowly to achieve a glass-like crunch.
The 4:1 vegetable to meat ratio ensures the beetroot remains the star.
Use a high-speed blender for the huacatay oil to maintain a vibrant green color.

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Dry-Fried Chicken (Laziji)
recipes.visual_description: A deep, round ceramic serving bowl holds a single portion of Sichuan Dry-Fried Chicken. The dish features 3cm bite-sized chicken thigh chunks, double-fried to a textured, golden-brown exterior. These are nestled amidst a vibrant abundance of whole, glossy dried red chili peppers and cracked Sichuan peppercorns. Sliced garlic and 1cm ginger batons are scattered throughout. Bright green scallion rounds, cut into 5mm rings, provide a sharp color contrast. The chicken appears crispy and matte, while the chilies have a slight oily sheen. The arrangement is organic and heaped, reflecting traditional Sichuan style. The bowl sits on a dark wood table with a side of steamed jasmine rice and bamboo chopsticks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice to balance the heat
Provide bamboo chopsticks for dining
Present as part of a communal meal with other Sichuan dishes
Accompany with a side of pickled radish or cucumber

ingredients.name: Chicken thigh meat, cut into 3cm chunks

instructions: Marinate chicken chunks in Shaoxing wine, soy sauce, and salt for 20 minutes.
Coat marinated chicken evenly with cornstarch.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok to 180°C.
Fry chicken in batches until light golden. Remove and drain.
Increase oil temperature to 200°C.
Fry chicken again for 1 minute until deep golden and crispy.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Drain all but 30ml of oil from the wok.
Add ginger and garlic to the wok. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add Sichuan peppercorns and dried chilies. Stir-fry on low heat until aromatic.
Return chicken to the wok. Add sugar and scallions.
Toss over high heat for 1 minute until well combined. Serve immediately.
notes: Do not eat the whole dried chilies or peppercorns; they are for flavor infusion.
Ensure chilies do not turn black during the final toss.
Double frying is essential for the characteristic crispy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Sesame Pork Tantanmen
recipes.visual_description: A single deep white ceramic ramen bowl sits on a dark walnut table. The broth is a rich, opaque tan color from the emulsified sesame paste and pork stock, with vibrant red droplets of chili oil shimmering on the surface. In the center, a neat mound of dark, savory ground pork crumbles rests atop al dente noodles. Two vibrant green bok choy halves, blanched until tender-crisp, are placed along the side of the bowl. The arrangement is clean and focused, showing the contrast between the creamy soup and the bright greens. Beside the bowl lies a pair of dark wood chopsticks and a white ceramic soup spoon on a simple linen napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of gyoza
Provide extra chili oil on the table
Use a ceramic renge spoon for the broth
instructions: Sauté ginger and garlic in a pan with 10ml oil until fragrant.
Add ground pork. Cook until browned and fully rendered.
Stir in doubanjiang. Cook for 2 minutes. Set aside.
Whisk sesame paste, soy sauce, and sugar in a large bowl until smooth.
Bring pork stock to a boil in a pot. Reduce to low heat.
Blanch bok choy in boiling water for 1 minute. Remove and drain.
Cook ramen noodles in boiling water according to package instructions. Drain.
Slowly whisk the hot pork stock into the sesame mixture to create a creamy broth.
Divide broth into four deep bowls. Add noodles.
Top each bowl with a portion of the ground pork and two bok choy halves.
Drizzle with chili oil before serving.
notes: Ensure the sesame paste is well-mixed before adding to the stock to prevent clumping.
Do not boil the broth after adding the sesame paste to maintain a smooth texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Oat and Amlou Parfait with Roasted Pears
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy fermented oat porridge served in a shallow, handcrafted cream-colored ceramic bowl.
