Scattered around the plate are two whole fresh blueberries and three halved raspberries, adding height and fresh color. Small, bright green thyme leaves are placed delicately on the scallops. The arrangement is organic with ample negative space. Natural light highlights the contrast between the white ceramic and the rich jewel tones of the fruit and the golden scallops.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a chilled glass of Sauvignon Blanc.
Accompany with a light arugula salad.
instructions: Combine blueberries, raspberries, and balsamic vinegar in a saucepan.
Simmer over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pan.
Whisk agar powder into the liquid.
Boil for 1 minute.
Pour into a shallow container.
Refrigerate until firm.
Blend set gel until smooth.
Pat scallops dry with paper towels.
Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a pan over high heat.
Place scallops in pan.
Sear 90 seconds per side.
Add butter, shallot, and thyme.
Baste scallops 30 seconds.
Remove from heat.
notes: Ensure scallops are completely dry to achieve a proper sear.
Do not over-process the gel or it may lose its viscosity.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Beef Goulash
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a dark oak table. The focus is a hearty portion of Hungarian beef stew. The beef is cut into 3cm chunks, appearing dark red and tender. Vibrant orange carrots are cut into 2cm rounds. Potatoes are 2cm cubes, absorbing the deep red sauce. The sauce is thick and glossy, colored intensely by sweet paprika. Red bell peppers are cut into 2cm squares. A single dollop of white sour cream is placed on the side. A sprig of fresh parsley is the garnish. A side of crusty rye bread rests on a small ceramic plate next to the bowl. Natural light creates soft shadows and highlights the rich textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Galuska or Nokedli dumplings
Accompany with pickled cucumbers or fermented cabbage
Provide thick slices of fresh rye bread for dipping
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm chunks.
Finely dice onions and mince garlic.
Cut carrots into 2cm rounds and potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Dice tomatoes and cut bell pepper into 2cm squares.
Heat lard in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Sauté onions until translucent and golden.
Remove pot from heat and stir in paprika and caraway seeds.
Add beef chunks and return to heat.
Sear meat for 5 minutes until browned.
Add garlic, tomatoes, and bell pepper.
Pour in beef stock and add bay leaf.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots.
Simmer for 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Do not boil the paprika over high heat to avoid bitterness.
The stew is even better when reheated the next day.
Ensure the beef is chuck or a similar braising cut for tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Tortilla and Hominy Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of deep red soup is served in a traditional hand-painted ceramic bowl. The rich broth features large, puffy white hominy kernels and substantial 3cm chunks of poached chicken breast. A generous pile of golden, hand-cut fried tortilla strips sits in the center, partially submerged to show texture. Vibrant green cilantro leaves and small cubes of creamy avocado are scattered across the surface. The bowl rests on a rustic dark wood table next to a small terracotta dish of lime wedges and a woven cloth napkin. Warm, directional light from a nearby window creates soft shadows, highlighting the steam rising from the liquid and the oily sheen of the guajillo-infused broth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lime wedges for acidity
Accompany with a side of dried Mexican oregano
Provide sliced radishes for added crunch
instructions: Slice tortillas into 1cm wide strips.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Fry tortilla strips until crisp and golden. Remove and drain on paper towels.
Toast guajillo chilies in the same pot for 30 seconds per side. Remove and soak in hot water for 10 minutes.
Blend soaked chilies, tomatoes, onion, and garlic until smooth.
Sear chicken chunks in the pot until the exterior is white.
Add the blended tomato mixture to the chicken. Cook for 5 minutes while stirring.
Pour in the chicken stock and add the hominy.
Simmer for 20 minutes until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Season with salt to taste.
Ladle soup into deep bowls.
Garnish with fried tortilla strips, avocado cubes, and cilantro.
notes: Do not overcook the hominy to maintain its chewy texture
Ensure chilies are deseeded before toasting to control heat levels
Use corn tortillas that are a few days old for the crispest fried strips

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Pear and Strawberry Honey-Preserve
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a handcrafted cream-colored ceramic plate. Four thick wedges of fermented pear, translucent and pale gold, are arranged in a natural, off-center cluster. Nestled against them are four thick chunks of deep red strawberries. The fruit is lightly coated in a glistening, ruby-colored syrup made from steeped strawberry tops. A fine dusting of earthy-brown dehydrated pear skin powder is sprinkled across the fruit. A small, organic mound of toasted golden oats and minced pear-core crumble sits to the side. The arrangement is minimalist on a reclaimed oak table. Soft, natural light creates gentle shadows. An undyed linen napkin and a small wooden spoon complete the authentic, sustainable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve at room temperature to appreciate the complex fermentation notes.
Pair with a small glass of chilled pear cider or herbal tea.
Use hand-carved wooden utensils to reflect the rustic Nordic aesthetic.
instructions: Peel the pears. Reserve all skins.
Cut pears into 8 thick wedges each. Remove cores and reserve.
Dissolve sea salt in filtered water to create a 2% brine.
Place pear wedges in a glass jar. Cover with brine. Weight down fruit.
Ferment at room temperature for 48 hours. Drain and pat dry.
Place reserved pear skins on a tray. Dehydrate at 60°C for 4 hours until brittle.
Grind dried skins into a fine powder using a mortar or spice grinder.
Hull the strawberries. Reserve the green tops (calyxes).
Cut strawberries into thick chunks.
Simmer strawberry tops with honey and 50ml water for 10 minutes. Strain and cool.
Finely dice the reserved pear cores. Remove any seeds.
Toast oats and diced cores in a dry pan over medium heat until golden. Cool.
Arrange 4 fermented pear wedges and 4 strawberry chunks on each plate.
Drizzle with the strawberry top syrup.
Garnish with pear skin powder and the oat-core crumble.
notes: The brine can be reused as a starter for future ferments or added to dressings.
Ensure pears are firm so they maintain structure during the 48-hour fermentation.
The pear skin powder adds a concentrated, slightly tannic depth to the dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Turmeric Chickpea Pilaf with Fresh Mint
recipes.visual_description: Vibrant golden-yellow basmati rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is fluffy with distinct grains, interspersed with whole, tender chickpeas and finely diced translucent onions. Small emerald-green flecks of fresh mint are folded throughout. On top, several whole chickpeas appear slightly crisped and darkened from sautéing. The dish is garnished with a single sprig of fresh mint and a few thin slivers of fresh ginger. The plate sits on a dark mango wood table next to a small copper bowl of plain white yogurt. A polished silver spoon rests on a folded cream linen napkin. Natural side lighting highlights the steam and the individual matte textures of the rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cucumber raita
Accompany with lime wedges and mango pickle
Present with warm garlic naan or crispy papadums
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Soak in cold water for 20 minutes. Drain.
Heat ghee in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add cumin seeds. Toast 30 seconds.
Add diced onions. Sauté 8 minutes until golden brown.
Stir in minced garlic and turmeric. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chickpeas. Sauté 3 minutes to coat in spices.
Add drained rice. Stir gently to toast grains for 2 minutes.
Pour in vegetable stock and salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover with a tight-fitting lid. Simmer 12 minutes.
Remove from heat. Let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fold in chopped mint using a fork to fluff the grains. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the rice is fully drained after soaking to maintain the correct liquid ratio.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot to prevent the rice from scorching at the bottom.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Pepper Köfte with Caramelized Onion Relish
recipes.visual_description: Two thick, hand-shaped oval beef köfte rest atop a vibrant bed of sautéed vegetables. The beef exhibits a dark, seared crust from high-heat pan-frying. Beneath the meat, red and green bell peppers are cut into thick batons, showing softened textures and charred, blackened edges. Large wedges of onion appear translucent and deeply caramelized. The arrangement is organic and centered on a matte white ceramic plate, leaving clean margins. A garnish of coarsely chopped flat-leaf parsley adds a bright green contrast. The scene is set on a rustic wooden table with a side of charred flatbread and a linen napkin. Natural light emphasizes the juicy texture of the whole meat pieces.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita or lepinja bread
Accompany with a side of thick garlic yogurt or ajvar
Provide a side of raw sliced onions and lemon wedges
instructions: Finely grate half of one onion and mince all garlic cloves.
Combine beef, grated onion, garlic, bread crumbs, cumin, and paprika in a bowl.
Knead the meat mixture by hand for 5 minutes until the proteins bind and become tacky.
Shape the mixture into 8 thick, oval-shaped patties.
Slice the remaining onions and all bell peppers into 1cm thick batons.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sauté onion and pepper batons until deeply caramelized and slightly charred at the edges.
Remove vegetables and heat remaining oil in the same pan.
Sear beef patties for 4 minutes per side until an internal temperature of 71°C is reached.
Rest the meat for 3 minutes before serving.
notes: Kneading the meat is essential for the traditional springy texture of Balkan köfte.
Ensure the pan is very hot before adding the meat to achieve a dark crust without overcooking the center.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Abalone with Ginger Beer and Apple Brandy Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The centerpiece is one whole, large pan-seared abalone, its surface deeply caramelized with a visible diamond-scored pattern. The abalone is coated in a glossy, dark amber glaze made from ginger beer and apple brandy. Two vibrant green steamed baby bok choy halves are placed neatly beside the seafood, providing a color contrast. Fine julienne strips of fresh ginger and a few dark droplets of sauce are scattered around the plate for garnish. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table, a crisp white cotton napkin, and polished stainless steel cutlery. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the textures and the rich sheen of the reduction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a chilled glass of dry Riesling or a ginger-infused cocktail.
Accompany with a side of steamed jasmine rice to soak up the glaze.

ingredients.name: Sea salt and cracked black pepper

instructions: Score the flat side of the abalone in a 5mm crosshatch pattern.
Season the abalone with salt and pepper.
Heat grapeseed oil in a heavy skillet over high heat.
Sear the abalone, scored side down, for 2 minutes.
Flip and sear for 1 minute. Remove from pan and keep warm.
Sauté shallots, garlic, and ginger in the same pan for 1 minute.
Deglaze with apple brandy and scrape the pan bottom.
Add ginger beer and bitters.
Simmer and reduce the liquid by half until syrupy.
Whisk in chilled butter one cube at a time to create a glossy emulsion.
Steam bok choy for 3 minutes until vibrant green and tender-crisp.
Return abalone to the pan to coat thoroughly with the glaze.
Place two bok choy halves on each plate.
Rest one whole abalone on the greens.
Spoon remaining glaze over the top.
notes: Do not overcook the abalone as it will become rubbery.
Ensure the butter is very cold when whisking into the sauce to prevent splitting.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Acorn Squash and Parsnip Stew
recipes.visual_description: The stew is served in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl with visible pottery marks. Large, 3cm cubes of roasted acorn squash show dark caramelized edges and soft orange flesh. These sit alongside 2cm thick parsnip rounds, browned from roasting. The vegetables are partially submerged in a savory, translucent amber broth filled with whole chickpeas. The arrangement is casual and hearty, filling the bowl to the rim. A generous scattering of coarsely chopped green parsley adds a fresh contrast to the warm tones. The bowl rests on a rustic oak table next to a simple silver spoon and a cream-colored cloth napkin. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the soft textures and gentle steam.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread
Accompany with a side of plain Greek yogurt
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss squash cubes and parsnip rounds with 15ml oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking tray.
Roast for 25 minutes until edges are browned.
Heat 15ml oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add garlic, thyme, and paprika.
Cook for 1 minute.
Stir in roasted vegetables and chickpeas.
Pour in vegetable stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Garnish with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure squash cubes are uniform for even roasting.
Use high-quality vegetable stock for better flavor depth.

recipes.recipe_name: Bánh Xèo (Vietnamese Savory Pancakes)
recipes.visual_description: A single, large, vibrant golden-yellow pancake with lacy, crispy edges sits on a clean white porcelain plate. The pancake is folded in half, revealing plump pink whole shrimp and tender small pieces of seared pork tucked inside. Fresh white bean sprouts and translucent onion slices peek from the fold. The pancake surface shows a subtle oily sheen and a crisp, bubbled texture. Beside the plate is a small clear glass bowl of amber-colored dipping sauce with floating red chili bits and white minced garlic. A separate side platter holds a tall, organic arrangement of whole bright green Romaine lettuce leaves, fresh mint sprigs, and Thai basil. The scene is set on a dark wood bistro table under soft, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a platter of large lettuce leaves and fresh herbs like mint and Thai basil.
Diners should tear pieces of the pancake and wrap them inside the lettuce leaves with herbs.
Dip the prepared wraps into the Nước Chấm sauce before eating.
Accompany with pickled daikon and carrots for traditional acidity.

ingredients.name: Pork shoulder, thinly sliced into small bite-sized pieces
Yellow onion, thinly sliced into half-moons

instructions: Whisk rice flour, turmeric, and salt in a bowl. Add coconut milk and water. Stir until smooth. Mix in scallions. Rest batter for 30 minutes.
Combine fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, 120ml warm water, garlic, and chili in a small bowl to make the dipping sauce.
Heat 15ml oil in a 20cm non-stick skillet over high heat.
Add 75g pork and 75g shrimp. Sear for 1 minute until pork is cooked through.
Pour 125ml batter into the pan. Swirl immediately to coat the bottom and sides thinly.
Place 50g bean sprouts and a few onion slices on one half of the pancake.
Cover with a lid. Cook for 3 minutes.
Remove lid. Reduce heat to medium. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the bottom is crispy and golden brown.
Fold the pancake in half over the filling. Slide onto a plate.
Repeat the process for the remaining three pancakes.
notes: Ensure the pan is very hot before adding batter to achieve the signature crispy edges.
Resting the batter is essential for the rice flour to hydrate properly.
Do not overfill the pancake or it will be difficult to fold without breaking.

recipes.recipe_name: Iberico Pork with Honey-Sherry Glaze and Brioche Torrija
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a large, matte charcoal-grey ceramic plate to emphasize contrast. Three 3cm golden-brown brioche torrija cubes are placed in an organic, non-linear arrangement across the center. Interspersed are three 3cm whole chunks of seared Iberico pork, glistening with a dark, translucent mahogany sherry glaze. The pork is not sliced. A single, fluid ribbon of the honey-sherry reduction curves artistically between the components. Two precise sprigs of micro-thyme and a few flakes of Maldon salt provide the final garnish. The composition uses significant negative space, lit with dramatic side-lighting to highlight the textures of the porous bread and the succulent meat.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a sophisticated tapas snack
Pair with a chilled glass of Oloroso sherry
Present on shared artisanal stoneware
instructions: Cut brioche into 3cm cubes.
Heat milk with cinnamon and scraped vanilla bean until simmering.
Remove from heat. Infuse 10 minutes. Strain.
Whisk egg into cooled milk.
Soak brioche cubes in milk mixture for 5 minutes.
Cut Iberico pork into 3cm chunks. Season with salt.
Sear pork in a hot pan 2 minutes per side until 63°C internal temperature.
Remove pork. Rest 5 minutes.
In the same pan, combine sherry and honey.
Simmer until reduced to a thick, glossy syrup.
Melt butter in a separate non-stick pan.
Fry soaked brioche cubes until golden brown on all sides.
Toss pork chunks in the sherry glaze to coat.
notes: Ensure brioche is dry to absorb maximum custard
Do not overcook the Iberico pork to maintain its nutty fat profile
The glaze should be viscous enough to coat a spoon

recipes.recipe_name: Gin-Steamed Abalone with Ginger and Soy
recipes.visual_description: A single whole abalone sits centered in its iridescent mother-of-pearl shell on a matte white ceramic plate. The abalone meat remains whole but is deeply crosshatch-scored into small squares, revealing a tender ivory interior against a glistening, steamed surface. A vibrant mound of bright green julienned scallions and pale yellow ginger matchsticks rests on top. A dark, glossy soy and gin reduction pools at the base of the shell. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table. Beside the plate are dark wood chopsticks on a porcelain rest and a small bowl of white rice. Natural side lighting emphasizes the glossy textures and aromatic steam.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed jasmine rice
Provide a small finger bowl with lemon water
Pair with a chilled gin-based botanical cocktail
instructions: Scrub abalone shells and meat with a clean brush. Remove viscera and tough outer edges.
Score the top of each whole abalone in a 5mm crosshatch pattern.
Place abalone back into their cleaned shells.
Top each abalone with half of the julienned ginger.
Drizzle 15ml of gin over each abalone.
Steam over high heat for 8 minutes until tender.
Combine soy sauce, sugar, and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Heat neutral oil in a small pan until it reaches smoking point.
Remove abalone from steamer and discard excess liquid from shells.
Top meat with remaining ginger, garlic, and green onions.
Drizzle soy mixture over the aromatics.
Carefully pour hot oil over the aromatics to sear them.
Garnish with coriander and serve immediately.
notes: Do not overcook the abalone or it will become rubbery.
Use a gin with heavy citrus or floral notes to complement the seafood.
The hot oil must be smoking to properly release the aroma of the ginger and garlic.

recipes.recipe_name: Miso-Glazed Chicken with Eggplant and Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: Present the dish on a textured, dark grey ceramic stoneware plate. Arrange four large, succulent chunks of golden-brown miso-glazed chicken in the center. Surround the chicken with three thick, tender rounds of sautéed purple eggplant and five vibrant green asparagus spears. Ensure the chicken shows a glossy, caramelized sheen from the miso glaze. Garnish with a fine chiffonade of green scallions and a light dusting of toasted white sesame seeds. The plate sits on a light oak table. Beside it, place a pair of dark wood chopsticks on a ceramic rest and a small bowl of steamed short-grain rice. Use soft, natural side lighting to highlight the textures and keep the background minimal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed short-grain rice
Accompany with miso soup
Use chopsticks for dining
instructions: Cut chicken into 4cm chunks.
Whisk miso, mirin, sake, soy sauce, and ginger in a bowl.
Marinate chicken in half the mixture for 20 minutes.
Slice eggplant into 2cm thick rounds.
Trim asparagus to 8cm lengths.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and set aside.
Add eggplant rounds to the skillet and cook until golden and soft.
Add asparagus and sauté for 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan.
Pour in the remaining miso mixture.
Toss ingredients until the sauce thickens into a glossy glaze.
notes: Salt the eggplant rounds for 10 minutes then pat dry to remove bitterness
Monitor the glaze closely to prevent the miso from burning

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Chicken Panzanella
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Panzanella served in a shallow white porcelain bowl on a rustic wooden bistro table. The entire plate is visible. The base features a vibrant heap of 3cm sourdough bread cubes, some softened by vinaigrette and others remaining crisp. Large, irregular chunks of red and yellow heirloom tomatoes provide bright color. Thinly sliced red onion rings and dark green arugula leaves are interspersed throughout. A whole, char-marked grilled chicken breast sits prominently atop the salad, glistening with olive oil. The chicken remains whole and unsliced. A small side dish of balsamic glaze and a glass of sparkling water sit nearby. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the charred meat and juicy tomatoes. The composition is clean.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of chilled Vermentino or Chianti
Provide extra virgin olive oil on the table for drizzling
Accompany with crusty Italian bread
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt, pepper, and 15ml olive oil.
Grill chicken over medium-high heat until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from grill and rest. Keep pieces whole.
Cut sourdough bread into 3cm cubes.
Toss bread with 20ml olive oil and toast in a pan until golden.
Cut heirloom tomatoes into large, irregular chunks.
Slice red onion into very thin rings.
Whisk remaining olive oil, vinegar, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a bowl.
Combine tomatoes, onions, capers, and toasted bread in a large mixing bowl.
Pour half the dressing over the mixture and toss. Let stand 5 minutes.
Add arugula and basil. Toss with remaining dressing.
Divide salad onto four plates. Place one whole grilled chicken breast on each portion.
notes: Use very ripe tomatoes for maximum juice extraction into the bread
Ensure the bread is stale or well-toasted to maintain some structure after dressing
Rest the chicken for at least 5 minutes before serving to retain moisture

recipes.recipe_name: Authentic Chicken Biryani
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Biryani is presented as a fragrant, mounded heap of long-grain basmati rice on a minimalist white porcelain plate. The rice grains are separate and fluffy, displaying a natural spectrum of white, saffron-yellow, and warm orange tones. Large, whole chunks of bone-in chicken thighs are partially visible, their surfaces coated in a thick, dark brown spice masala. The dish is topped with a concentrated pile of crispy, mahogany-colored fried onion batons and a scattering of fresh, emerald-green chopped coriander. The plate sits on a rustic wooden table alongside a small copper bowl of white yogurt raita and a silver spoon. Natural morning light emphasizes the steam and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cucumber raita
Accompany with fresh lime wedges and sliced raw red onions
Traditional copper or brass serving vessels enhance authenticity
instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear. Soak in water for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Fry sliced onions until deep golden brown.
Remove half of the fried onions for garnish. Leave the rest in the pot.
Marinate chicken chunks with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, and 15g spice mix for 30 minutes.
Boil 1 liter of salted water. Add soaked rice. Cook until 70% tender. Drain.
Add marinated chicken and remaining spice mix to the pot with onions. Sauté for 10 minutes.
Spread the par-boiled rice evenly over the chicken layer.
Top with the reserved fried onions and chopped coriander.
Seal the pot tightly with a lid or foil. Cook on very low heat for 20 minutes.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest for 10 minutes. Fluff rice gently with a fork before serving.
notes: Do not overcook the rice during the initial boil; it must finish cooking in the steam.
Bone-in chicken provides superior flavor and moisture to the rice.
A heavy-bottomed pot is essential to prevent the bottom layer from burning during the dum process.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Acorn Squash and Chickpea Tagine
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a traditional terracotta tagine with a conical lid resting nearby on a dark wooden table. The focal point is the thick, skin-on roasted acorn squash wedges, showing deep orange flesh and dark caramelized edges. These wedges are nestled into a thick, aromatic sauce filled with whole, plump chickpeas and softened orange apricot halves. Small specks of bright yellow preserved lemon and vibrant green chopped coriander are scattered over the top. Beside the tagine sits a separate white ceramic bowl containing a mound of fluffy, pale yellow steamed couscous. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic grain of the table. A clean white cotton napkin and a polished silver spoon complete the setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Harissa for added heat
Accompany with fresh Khobz bread
Follow the meal with traditional Moroccan mint tea
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut squash into 4cm thick wedges and remove seeds.
Toss squash with 20ml olive oil and salt.
Roast squash for 25 minutes until tender and edges caramelize.
Heat remaining oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion for 8 minutes until translucent.
Add garlic, ginger, and Ras el Hanout.
Toast spices for 2 minutes while stirring.
Pour in vegetable stock and add chickpeas and apricots.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid reduces by one third.
Gently fold roasted squash and preserved lemon into the sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes to combine flavors.
Prepare couscous using boiling water and fluff with a fork.
Serve tagine over couscous and garnish with fresh coriander.
notes: Do not peel the squash; the skin is edible and holds the wedge shape during braising.
Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon before adding the squash.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Lamb Tagine with Apricots and Almonds
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a traditional conical ceramic tagine vessel on a rustic wooden table. Large, 4cm chunks of tender, dark-brown braised lamb are piled in the center, coated in a thick, glossy, amber-colored sauce. Whole orange dried apricots are nestled between the meat chunks, appearing plump and hydrated. The surface is scattered with crunchy, golden-brown toasted whole almonds and bright green cilantro leaves. The composition shows the entire tagine base with a side of fluffy couscous in a small matching clay bowl. A simple white linen napkin and a traditional Moroccan spoon sit beside the dish. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures of the rich sauce and the fibrous lamb.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed couscous or crusty khobz bread
Accompany with a side of fresh Moroccan mint tea
Provide a small bowl of harissa for additional heat
instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy-based pot or tagine over medium-high heat.
Brown lamb chunks in batches until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Add onions to the pot. Sauté for 8 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in garlic, ginger, and Ras el Hanout. Cook for 2 minutes to bloom spices.
Return lamb to the pot. Add cinnamon stick, salt, and stock.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 90 minutes.
Add dried apricots and honey. Stir gently.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until lamb is tender and sauce thickens.
Remove cinnamon stick before serving.
Garnish with toasted almonds and fresh cilantro.
notes: For best results, use a heavy cast iron pot if a clay tagine is unavailable
Ensure the sauce reduces enough to coat the back of a spoon

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Corvina with Chuño Revuelto
recipes.visual_description: A single whole pan-seared corvina fillet with a crisp, golden-brown skin side facing up. The fillet rests on a generous bed of chuño revuelto. The chuño is cut into uniform 2cm cubes, showing a mix of dark and cream colors, bound by soft yellow scrambled eggs and white crumbles of queso fresco. The dish is plated on a clean white porcelain plate with moderate negative space. Small flecks of green cilantro are scattered over the top. A bright green lime wedge is placed on the side. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the flaky texture of the fish and the rustic, porous surface of the chuño cubes on a light wooden bistro table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Salsa Criolla (marinated red onions)
Accompany with a glass of Chicha Morada
Use traditional hand-painted ceramic plates for a rustic touch
instructions: Soak chuño in cold water for 24 hours. Change water twice.
Peel rehydrated chuño. Boil in salted water for 20 minutes until tender.
Drain and cut chuño into 2cm cubes.
Heat 15ml oil in a large skillet. Sauté onion, garlic, and aji amarillo for 5 minutes.
Add chuño cubes to the skillet. Sauté for 3 minutes.
Pour in beaten eggs and queso fresco. Stir gently until eggs are just set.
Keep chuño mixture warm.
Pat corvina fillets dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining oil and butter in a heavy pan over medium-high heat.
Place corvina fillets skin-side down. Press gently for 30 seconds.
Sear for 4 minutes until skin is crispy. Flip fillets.
Cook for 2 more minutes until fish is opaque throughout.
Place a portion of chuño revuelto on each plate. Top with one whole fish fillet.
Garnish with cilantro and lime wedges.
notes: Ensure chuño is fully rehydrated to avoid a bitter taste.
Do not overcook the eggs; they should remain moist to bind the chuño.
Pressing the fish fillets initially prevents the skin from curling.

recipes.recipe_name: Lemon Garlic Roasted Chicken with Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two whole bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, roasted to a deep golden-brown with visible dried oregano. Beside the chicken are thick, hand-cut potato wedges, glistening with lemon-infused olive oil and showing crispy, caramelized edges. Softened red onion wedges and whole roasted garlic cloves are scattered naturally around the plate. The entire arrangement is presented on a clean, white circular porcelain plate with moderate negative space. A vibrant green sprinkle of chopped fresh parsley adds contrast. The setting is a light-colored wooden bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright and natural, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and fluffy potato centers.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a block of high-quality feta cheese sprinkled with oregano
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the lemon-garlic juices
Pair with a crisp, cold Assyrtiko white wine
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut potatoes into thick wedges.
Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, 4 minced garlic cloves, and oregano in a bowl.
Place chicken, potato wedges, onion quarters, and remaining whole garlic cloves in a large roasting pan.
Pour the lemon-oil mixture over the ingredients. Toss to coat evenly.
Season generously with salt and pepper.
Pour chicken stock into the bottom of the pan.
Roast for 45 to 50 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Verify potatoes are tender and golden-brown.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Pat chicken skin dry with paper towels before roasting for maximum crispness
Ensure potatoes are partially submerged in the stock to achieve a creamy interior texture

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Camembert-Calvados Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single whole pan-seared chicken breast with a deep golden-brown crust, placed centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. A rich, creamy Camembert and Calvados sauce is poured over the meat, showing a velvety texture with small flecks of black pepper. To the side, a bouquet of crisp frisee and tender mache leaves provides a fresh contrast. The greens are lightly coated in hazelnut oil, catching the natural light. Toasted hazelnut halves are scattered atop the salad for texture. The arrangement leaves ample negative space, reflecting a modern bistro style. The background is a rustic wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin and polished silver cutlery.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of dry Normandy cider or a light-bodied red wine
Accompany with crusty baguette slices to soak up the cheese sauce
Present on pre-warmed porcelain plates to maintain the sauce consistency

ingredients.name: Camembert cheese, rind removed and cubed

instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper on all sides.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken in the skillet and sear for 6-8 minutes per side.
Verify chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate and cover loosely with foil.
Add shallots to the skillet and sauté for 2 minutes until translucent.
Pour in Calvados and scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Stir in chicken stock and heavy cream, then simmer for 3 minutes.
Reduce heat to low and whisk in Camembert cubes until the sauce is smooth.
Whisk hazelnut oil and cider vinegar together in a large bowl.
Toss the frisee and mache leaves in the dressing until lightly coated.
Place one whole chicken breast on each plate.
Spoon the Camembert sauce over the chicken.
Arrange the dressed salad next to the chicken and garnish with toasted hazelnuts.
notes: Ensure the cheese rind is fully removed for a perfectly smooth sauce texture
Do not let the sauce boil once the cheese is added to prevent separation
The hazelnut oil provides a subtle toasted aroma that balances the funky notes of the Camembert

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Acorn Squash with Warm Kale and Radicchio Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted acorn squash wedges serves as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain plate. Four thick wedges, roasted until golden with visible char marks, are arranged in a natural, slightly overlapping stack. Nestled around the squash is a warm salad of wilted dark green kale and vibrant purple radicchio. Small, uniform cubes of sautéed red pepper add pops of bright color. Crispy, golden-brown pancetta chunks are scattered generously over the greens. Crumbles of creamy white gorgonzola are dotted throughout, beginning to melt slightly from the heat. The plating is organized yet organic, with ample negative space. The setting features a rustic wooden table and a simple cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm crusty sourdough bread.
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Vermentino.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut squash into 2cm thick wedges.
Toss wedges with 15ml oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast on a tray for 25 minutes until tender.
Fry diced pancetta in a pan until crispy.
Remove pancetta and keep fat in pan.
Sauté diced peppers in fat for 3 minutes.
Add kale and cook until wilted.
Deglaze pan with vinegar and honey.
Stir in torn radicchio for 30 seconds.
Arrange four squash wedges on each plate.
Top with greens and pancetta chunks.
Garnish with crumbled gorgonzola.
notes: Ensure the pan is hot before deglazing to capture all the brown bits.
Use a sharp knife to maintain clean edges on the squash wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (green chili sauce)
Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

ingredients.name: Red onions, cut into thick wedges
Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Ajillo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Ajillo served on a clean white porcelain plate in a modern Spanish bistro setting. The dish features two whole chicken pieces—a thigh and a drumstick—with crispy, deep golden-brown skin. The chicken is surrounded by twenty whole, soft, golden-confit garlic cloves. A rich, translucent emulsion of olive oil and sherry glaze coats the meat. Bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. The arrangement is organic and centered with moderate negative space. A side of thick-cut, toasted rustic baguette sits on the edge of the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the glistening textures of the oil and the sear on the chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to soak up the garlic oil.
Accompany with a glass of chilled dry Fino sherry.
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for a rustic look.
instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add whole garlic cloves to the oil.
Fry garlic until golden brown on all sides.
Remove garlic with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Increase heat to medium-high.
Place chicken pieces in the pan, skin-side down.
Sear chicken until deep golden brown on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Drain half of the rendered fat from the pan.
Add bay leaf and return fried garlic to the pan.
Pour in the dry sherry.
Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Lower heat to medium-low and cover with a lid.
Simmer for 15 minutes or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove lid and increase heat for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Stir in chopped parsley and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the garlic does not burn; it should be golden and sweet, not black and bitter.
Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for the best flavor profile.
Always verify the thickest part of the chicken reaches 75°C for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sea Bass with Savory Acai and Hazelnut Farofa
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant, deep purple unsweetened acai puree spread in a smooth, thick circle across a clean white porcelain plate. A whole pan-seared sea bass fillet is positioned centrally on the puree, showcasing its golden-brown, crispy skin. To the side, a neat mound of toasted manioc farofa, mixed with visible chunks of crushed hazelnuts, provides a textural and color contrast in pale gold. The arrangement is clean and organized with significant negative space. Light reflects off the glistening fish skin and the matte surface of the acai. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak wooden table, a simple grey cotton napkin, and a single lime wedge for garnish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed white rice
Traditional Amazonian custom includes adding sliced prata bananas
Pair with a chilled dry white wine or a crisp lager
instructions: Pat sea bass fillets dry with paper towels.
Season fish with lime juice, salt, and black pepper.
Heat 20ml hazelnut oil in a small skillet over medium heat.
Add manioc flour and crushed hazelnuts to the skillet.
Toast flour and nuts for 5 minutes until golden brown, stirring constantly.
Remove farofa from heat and set aside.
Warm the acai pulp in a saucepan over low heat.
Season acai with a pinch of salt and stir until smooth.
Heat the remaining hazelnut oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place fish fillets skin-side down in the hot pan.
Press fish down with a spatula for 30 seconds to ensure even skin contact.
Sear for 4 minutes until the skin is golden and crispy.
Flip the fillets carefully.
Cook for an additional 2 minutes until the fish is opaque throughout.
Ensure fish reaches an internal temperature of 63°C.
Spread a thick circle of warm acai puree onto each plate.
Place one whole fish fillet directly on the acai.
Spoon the hazelnut farofa neatly to the side of the fish.
notes: Use only unsweetened, 'special' grade thick acai pulp for authenticity.
The hazelnut oil replaces traditional dende oil for a more refined, nutty profile.
Do not boil the acai as it may separate and lose its vibrant color.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Bream with Garlic and Acacia Flowers
recipes.visual_description: A single whole pan-seared bream fillet sits at the center of a clean white porcelain plate. The skin is deeply golden and remarkably crisp, showing visible sear marks. A vibrant pan sauce of translucent, thinly sliced garlic chips and delicate white acacia flowers is spooned over the fish. The flowers retain their elegant shape but appear slightly softened. Small flecks of bright green parsley add contrast. The dish is presented on a light oak bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and polished silver fork and knife. Natural side-lighting highlights the flaky texture of the white fish and the glossy sheen of the olive oil. Moderate negative space surrounds the central arrangement.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty sourdough bread to soak up the garlic oil.
Pair with a chilled dry white wine like Vermentino or Assyrtiko.
instructions: Pat bream fillets dry with paper towels.
Season flesh side with sea salt and white pepper.
Heat oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat.
Place fillets skin-side down in the pan.
Press firmly with a spatula for 30 seconds to prevent curling.
Sear for 4 minutes until skin is crisp and golden.
Flip fillets carefully.
Add sliced garlic to the pan around the fish.
Cook for 2 minutes until fish reaches an internal temperature of 63°C.
Remove fish from pan and rest on a warm plate.
Toss acacia flowers into the hot garlic oil for 30 seconds until slightly wilted.
Stir in lemon juice and parsley to create a light pan sauce.
Spoon garlic and acacia mixture over the fish.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure acacia flowers are sourced from edible Robinia pseudoacacia trees and are free of pesticides.
Do not overcook the garlic; it should be golden, not brown, to avoid bitterness.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Mole Poblano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Mole Poblano served on a clean white porcelain plate. The centerpiece is a whole, bone-in chicken thigh completely coated in a thick, velvety, dark reddish-brown mole sauce. The sauce appears glossy and rich with visible texture from ground seeds and spices. Toasted white sesame seeds are sprinkled evenly over the chicken. Three small sprigs of fresh cilantro and four thin rings of raw red onion provide a vibrant color contrast. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy Mexican red rice is positioned. The background features a rustic wooden table with a small basket of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a colorful woven cloth and a simple cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas served in a traditional cloth-lined basket
Mexican red rice (arroz rojo)
Refried beans topped with crumbled queso fresco
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from all dried chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Place toasted chilies in a bowl of hot water and soak for 20 minutes.
Toast almonds, 15g of sesame seeds, and the cinnamon stick in a dry pan until golden.
Char the tomatoes, onion, and garlic in a dry pan until blackened in spots.
Drain chilies and place in a blender with toasted nuts, spices, and charred vegetables.
Add 100ml of chicken stock and blend until a smooth paste forms.
Heat oil in a large pot. Add the mole paste and fry for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in the remaining chicken stock and chopped dark chocolate. Simmer on low heat.
Season chicken thighs with salt. Sear in a separate pan until the skin is golden brown.
Transfer chicken to the mole sauce. Simmer until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Adjust seasoning with salt if necessary.
notes: Do not burn the chilies during toasting or the sauce will become bitter.
The mole sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C at the bone.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Acorn Squash and Kielbasa with Braised Kale
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain dinner plate set on a rustic light oak table. The base features a bed of vibrant, dark green braised kale, showing a slight sheen from the mustard glaze. Resting on the kale are three thick, golden-brown roasted acorn squash wedges with caramelized edges. Three 4cm thick chunks of seared kielbasa are nestled among the squash, showing a deep mahogany crust and juicy interior. The arrangement is organic and centered, leaving ample white space around the rim. A simple white cotton napkin and polished stainless steel fork sit to the right. Natural, soft window lighting highlights the textures of the charred squash skin and the coarse grain of the mustard.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of chilled sour cream
Pair with a glass of dry Polish pilsner
Accompany with dark rye bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut acorn squash into 8 wedges each. Remove seeds.
Toss squash with 15ml oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast squash on a baking sheet for 25 minutes until tender.
Cut kielbasa into 4cm thick chunks.
Heat remaining oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear kielbasa chunks until browned on all sides. Remove from pan.
Melt butter in the same skillet.
Add diced onion and caraway seeds. Sauté 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic for 1 minute.
Add torn kale leaves and vinegar. Cover pan.
Cook 3 minutes until kale wilts.
Stir in mustard. Season with salt and pepper.
Plate kale as a base. Top with squash wedges and kielbasa chunks.
notes: Ensure the skillet is very hot before adding kielbasa to achieve a dark sear.
Do not peel the acorn squash; the skin becomes tender and edible when roasted.
Use curly kale or Lacinato kale for the best textural contrast.

recipes.recipe_name: Lobster and Wild Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of fluid lobster risotto served on a wide white porcelain plate. The rice is creamy and spreads naturally across the plate, demonstrating the 'all'onda' texture. Large, intact chunks of red-orange lobster meat are positioned centrally as the focal point. Earthy, browned slices of wild mushrooms are visible throughout the rice. The dish is finished with a precise sprinkle of vibrant green chopped chives. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak wood table. A white linen napkin and a heavy silver spoon rest beside the plate. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the creamy texture and the glossy finish of the mantecatura technique.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in wide, shallow bowls
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Vermentino or Gavi
Provide a high-quality olive oil for a final table-side drizzle

ingredients.name: Cooked lobster meat, cut into large chunks
Mixed wild mushrooms (porcini, chanterelle, cremini), sliced

instructions: Heat lobster stock in a saucepan. Keep at a low simmer.
Sauté mushrooms in a wide pan with 15ml olive oil until browned. Remove and set aside.
Add remaining oil and shallots to the pan. Cook until translucent.
Add rice to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Deglaze with white wine. Stir until liquid evaporates.
Add one ladle of hot stock. Stir constantly until absorbed.
Repeat adding stock one ladle at a time. Maintain a gentle simmer.
Fold in the sautéed mushrooms halfway through the cooking process.
Cook rice until al dente. Ensure the consistency is fluid and flowing.
Fold in lobster chunks, butter, and Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Add lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove from heat. Cover and rest for 2 minutes.
Serve immediately in warm bowls.
notes: Do not overcook the lobster chunks; add them at the very end to just warm through.
The risotto should be loose enough to spread when the plate is tapped, not stiff or molded.
Ensure the stock is hot before adding to the rice to maintain a consistent cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Cardamom Apple Galette with Oat-Hazelnut Frangipane
recipes.visual_description: A single individual-sized rustic galette centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The pastry crust is golden-brown and textured with visible ground oats, showing organic pleats around the edges. In the center, tender apple wedges are piled naturally, coated in a glistening maple glaze that catches the light. Fine specks of ground cardamom are visible on the fruit. The plate sits on a dark oak bistro table. A folded light gray linen napkin and a small dessert fork are placed to the right. The background is a soft-focus restaurant interior with natural side-lighting, emphasizing the crisp texture of the pastry and the soft, caramelized edges of the apples.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm with a dollop of crème fraîche
Pair with a glass of dry Normandy cider
Present on individual ceramic dessert plates

ingredients.name: rolled oats, ground into coarse flour
firm baking apples (e.g., Honeycrisp), peeled and cut into 1cm wedges

instructions: Pulse flour, oat flour, salt, and 100g cold butter in a food processor until sandy.
Add ice water and 15ml maple syrup. Pulse until dough just forms.
Wrap dough in plastic. Chill for 30 minutes.
Cream remaining 25g butter with sugar, ground hazelnuts, 1 tsp cardamom, and half the egg.
Toss apple wedges with remaining 1 tsp cardamom and 30ml maple syrup.
Divide dough into four portions. Roll each into a 15cm circle.
Spread hazelnut frangipane in the center of each circle, leaving a 3cm border.
Arrange apple wedges in a mound over the frangipane.
Fold dough edges over the apples, pleating as you go.
Brush dough with remaining egg wash. Sprinkle with a few whole oats.
Bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until crust is golden brown.
Brush warm apples with remaining 15ml maple syrup before serving.
notes: Do not overwork the dough to ensure a flaky texture
Ensure apples are cut into uniform wedges for even cooking
Toasting hazelnuts before grinding significantly improves the aromatic profile

recipes.recipe_name: Champagne Vinegar Cured Branzino
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion sits on a handcrafted, matte-beige ceramic plate. Three thick chunks of translucent, cured branzino are the focal point, arranged naturally in the center. They are not fanned. A vibrant green oil, extracted from dill and cucumber scraps, pools elegantly at the base. Beside the fish lie three uniform cucumber batons, quick-pickled to a bright translucency. A single, jagged shard of crisped, golden-brown fish skin provides verticality. The plating is minimalist, utilizing ample negative space. The scene is set on a reclaimed wood table under soft, natural light, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin. The palette is organic, featuring ivory, deep green, and earthy wood tones.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a cold appetizer to open a multi-course sustainable seafood menu.
Pair with a glass of chilled, organic sparkling wine.
instructions: Remove skin from branzino fillets. Reserve skin.
Mix salt, sugar, and 50ml champagne vinegar in a bowl.
Coat fish flesh with the mixture. Cure for 20 minutes.
Rinse fish under cold water. Pat dry. Cut into 3cm thick chunks.
Scrape scales from reserved skin. Flatten and bake at 180°C between parchment paper until crisp.
Cut cucumber into 4cm batons. Quick-pickle in remaining vinegar for 15 minutes.
Blend cucumber trimmings and dill stalks with olive oil. Strain through a fine cloth.
Place three fish chunks on each plate. Arrange cucumber batons alongside.
Drizzle the zero-waste herb oil around the fish.
Garnish with a single shard of fish skin crisp.
notes: Use the fish bones to create a stock for subsequent courses to ensure zero-waste.
The herb oil can be made ahead and stored for up to two days.

recipes.recipe_name: Saag Gosht
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Saag Gosht served in a traditional hammered copper karahi bowl on a dark wood table. The dish features large, succulent 3cm cubes of tender lamb partially submerged in a thick, vibrant emerald-green spinach sauce. The sauce has a smooth, velvety texture with visible glisten from the ghee. A single swirl of white heavy cream decorates the center. Top with fine julienne strips of fresh ginger and bright green coriander leaves. Beside the bowl, a stack of two charred, buttered garlic naan pieces rests on a small white porcelain plate. The entire setting is captured with natural, soft side lighting, showing the full arrangement and a clean cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with garlic naan or tandoori roti
Accompany with jeera rice
Provide a side of kachumber salad
Offer a wedge of lemon for acidity
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb cubes in batches until browned on all sides.
Remove lamb and set aside.
Add remaining ghee and onions to the pot.
Sauté onions until dark golden brown.
Stir in garlic, ginger, and green chilies. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add cumin seeds, ground coriander, and turmeric. Toast for 1 minute.
Return lamb to the pot. Add 200ml water.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes until lamb is tender.
Blanch spinach in boiling water for 1 minute. Drain and puree until smooth.
Stir spinach puree and garam masala into the pot.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes. Season with salt.
Garnish with fresh coriander.
notes: Ensure onions are deeply browned for authentic flavor depth.
Do not overcook the spinach puree to maintain the bright green color.
Use lamb shoulder for the best fat-to-meat ratio.

recipes.recipe_name: Kimchi Shrimp Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Kimchi Shrimp Fried Rice presented in a shallow, matte-black ceramic bowl. The rice grains are glossy and vibrant reddish-orange, interspersed with translucent bits of sautéed kimchi. Six whole, plump, pink seared shrimp are scattered naturally across the top, showing light golden caramelization. Bright green scallion rings provide a fresh color contrast against the warm rice. The dish is set on a light oak table with a white linen napkin. To the right, a pair of stainless steel Korean chopsticks and a long-handled spoon are neatly placed. A small side dish of fresh kimchi in a white porcelain bowl rests in the soft-focus background under natural, even light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Danmuji (pickled radish)
Accompany with a light dried pollack or seaweed soup
Provide stainless steel chopsticks and a long-handled rice spoon
instructions: Pat shrimp dry with paper towels.
Heat 15ml neutral oil in a wok over high heat.
Sear shrimp for 2 minutes until opaque.
Remove shrimp and set aside.
Add remaining neutral oil to the wok.
Sauté garlic and kimchi for 3 minutes.
Add rice to the wok.
Break up rice clumps with a spatula.
Pour in kimchi juice and soy sauce.
Stir-fry for 5 minutes until rice is coated.
Season with salt.
Return shrimp to the wok.
Drizzle with sesame oil.
Add half of the scallions.
Toss for 1 minute to combine.
notes: Use cold, day-old rice for the best texture.
Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding ingredients.
Adjust salt carefully as kimchi and soy sauce are already salty.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Clay Pot Rice with Fried Gluten and Acacia
recipes.visual_description: The dish is served in a traditional dark earthenware clay pot on a light oak table. The Jasmine rice is fluffy and coated in a savory, dark brown glaze. Large, round fried gluten balls are placed centrally, showing a crispy, dimpled texture. Thick chunks of dark shiitake mushrooms are interspersed with bright green, feathery acacia fronds. Green reed leaves line the pot, their edges slightly browned from the heat. A single portion is plated in a white porcelain bowl alongside the clay pot. A small dish of bird's eye chilies in fish sauce sits nearby. A cotton napkin and dark wooden chopsticks complete the setting. Soft, natural side lighting emphasizes the steam and the rich, glossy finish of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Prik Nam Pla (chilies in fish sauce)
Accompany with a side of clear cucumber soup
Enjoy with Thai iced tea
instructions: Rinse Jasmine rice until water runs clear.
Soak reed leaves in warm water for 10 minutes to soften.
Line the bottom of a heavy clay pot with reed leaves.
Add rice and vegetable broth into the clay pot.
Slice shiitake mushrooms into thick chunks.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat.
Sauté garlic, ginger, and mushrooms for 2 minutes.
Add fried gluten balls and clay pot rice sauce to the wok.
Toss until gluten balls are evenly coated with sauce.
Pour the gluten and sauce mixture over the rice in the pot.
Cover the clay pot with a tight lid.
Cook on low heat for 18-20 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Remove tough stems from acacia fronds.
Fold acacia fronds into the hot rice.
Cover and let steam for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Acacia has a strong aroma that mellows significantly when steamed with the rice.
The reed leaves provide a subtle earthy fragrance to the base of the rice.
Ensure the clay pot lid is tight to trap steam for even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo al Ajillo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo al Ajillo served on a clean white porcelain plate in a modern Spanish bistro setting. The dish features two whole chicken pieces—a thigh and a drumstick—with crispy, deep golden-brown skin. The chicken is surrounded by twenty whole, soft, golden-confit garlic cloves. A rich, translucent emulsion of olive oil and sherry glaze coats the meat. Bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. The arrangement is organic and centered with moderate negative space. A side of thick-cut, toasted rustic baguette sits on the edge of the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the glistening textures of the oil and the sear on the chicken.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread to soak up the garlic oil.
Accompany with a glass of chilled dry Fino sherry.
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for a rustic look.
instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add whole garlic cloves to the oil.
Fry garlic until golden brown on all sides.
Remove garlic with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Increase heat to medium-high.
Place chicken pieces in the pan, skin-side down.
Sear chicken until deep golden brown on all sides, about 10 minutes.
Drain half of the rendered fat from the pan.
Add bay leaf and return fried garlic to the pan.
Pour in the dry sherry.
Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Lower heat to medium-low and cover with a lid.
Simmer for 15 minutes or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove lid and increase heat for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Stir in chopped parsley and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the garlic does not burn; it should be golden and sweet, not black and bitter.
Use high-quality extra virgin olive oil for the best flavor profile.
Always verify the thickest part of the chicken reaches 75°C for safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Sea Buckthorn and Sweet Curd Tartlet with Charcoal Crust
recipes.visual_description: Four individual tartlets are arranged on a minimalist white porcelain plate set upon a dark wood table. Each tartlet features a crisp, matte-black shortcrust shell colored with activated charcoal. The center is filled with a vibrant, glossy orange sea buckthorn curd that provides a sharp color contrast. A single, textured quenelle of snow-white whipped cream and sour cream sits off-center, mimicking traditional Mongolian öröm. Small, round orange sea buckthorn berries are placed delicately on the cream. The background includes a traditional Mongolian silver-lined wooden bowl and a neutral linen napkin. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the crumbly texture of the black pastry and the smooth, reflective surface of the fruit curd.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Suutei tsai (traditional Mongolian milk tea)
Present on a wooden platter to honor nomadic traditions
Accompany with small pieces of dried curd (aaruul) for texture contrast

ingredients.name: thick sour cream or Greek yogurt

instructions: Combine flour, charcoal powder, and sugar in a large bowl.
Rub 100g of cold butter into the flour until it reaches a sandy texture.
Add the egg and mix until a dough forms.
Wrap dough in plastic and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll dough to 3mm thickness on a floured surface.
Line four 10cm tartlet rings with the dough.
Blind bake at 180°C for 12 minutes using pie weights.
Remove weights and bake for 5 more minutes. Cool completely.
Whisk sea buckthorn juice, egg yolks, and honey in a small saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens.
Remove from heat and whisk in remaining 60g butter until smooth.
Chill the curd in the refrigerator until firm.
Fill the cooled charcoal shells with the sea buckthorn curd.
Whip heavy cream and sour cream together to stiff peaks.
Place one large, rustic dollop of cream on each tartlet.
Garnish with fresh berries and serve.
notes: Ensure the activated charcoal is food-grade
Sea buckthorn is very acidic; adjust honey levels to taste
Do not overwork the dough to maintain a crumbly texture

recipes.recipe_name: Sea Buckthorn and Sweet Curd Tartlet with Charcoal Crust
recipes.visual_description: Four individual tartlets are arranged on a minimalist white porcelain plate set upon a dark wood table. Each tartlet features a crisp, matte-black shortcrust shell colored with activated charcoal. The center is filled with a vibrant, glossy orange sea buckthorn curd that provides a sharp color contrast. A single, textured quenelle of snow-white whipped cream and sour cream sits off-center, mimicking traditional Mongolian öröm. Small, round orange sea buckthorn berries are placed delicately on the cream. The background includes a traditional Mongolian silver-lined wooden bowl and a neutral linen napkin. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the crumbly texture of the black pastry and the smooth, reflective surface of the fruit curd.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Suutei tsai (traditional Mongolian milk tea)
Present on a wooden platter to honor nomadic traditions
Accompany with small pieces of dried curd (aaruul) for texture contrast

ingredients.name: thick sour cream or Greek yogurt

instructions: Combine flour, charcoal powder, and sugar in a large bowl.
Rub 100g of cold butter into the flour until it reaches a sandy texture.
Add the egg and mix until a dough forms.
Wrap dough in plastic and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Roll dough to 3mm thickness on a floured surface.
Line four 10cm tartlet rings with the dough.
Blind bake at 180°C for 12 minutes using pie weights.
Remove weights and bake for 5 more minutes. Cool completely.
Whisk sea buckthorn juice, egg yolks, and honey in a small saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture thickens.
Remove from heat and whisk in remaining 60g butter until smooth.
Chill the curd in the refrigerator until firm.
Fill the cooled charcoal shells with the sea buckthorn curd.
Whip heavy cream and sour cream together to stiff peaks.
Place one large, rustic dollop of cream on each tartlet.
Garnish with fresh berries and serve.
notes: Ensure the activated charcoal is food-grade
Sea buckthorn is very acidic; adjust honey levels to taste
Do not overwork the dough to maintain a crumbly texture

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef and Salmon with Garlic Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single white porcelain plate holds a centered arrangement of two thick beef tenderloin chunks and one square-cut salmon fillet with crisp skin. The beef is seared dark brown, while the salmon shows a vibrant coral hue. Beside them sits a neat mound of creamy, garlic-infused crushed potatoes, lightly browned on top. Vibrant green beans, sautéed to a bright emerald, are tucked alongside the proteins. A glossy, dark mahogany reduction sauce made with chocolate liqueur is drizzled around the base. Fine shavings of parmesan cheese and a single fresh bay leaf garnish the potatoes. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures of the seared crusts and the silky potato mash on a rustic wooden bistro table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty baguette
Present on pre-heated ceramic plates
instructions: Peel and cube potatoes into 3cm pieces.
Boil potatoes in salted water with bay leaves until tender.
Drain potatoes and remove bay leaves.
Mash potatoes with 20g butter, minced garlic, and parmesan cheese.
Blanch green beans in boiling water for 3 minutes, then shock in ice water.
Season beef and salmon with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks for 3 minutes per side. Remove and rest.
Sear salmon fillets skin-side down for 4 minutes, then flip for 2 minutes. Remove.
Pour chocolate liqueur and beef stock into the hot pan.
Reduce liquid by half until thick and glossy. Stir in remaining butter.
Sauté green beans in a separate pan with a touch of oil for 2 minutes.
Place a mound of potatoes on each plate.
Arrange one beef chunk and one salmon fillet beside the potatoes.
Place green beans alongside and drizzle sauce over the beef.
notes: The chocolate liqueur adds depth and a subtle bitterness to the savory sauce.
Ensure the beef rests for 5 minutes before serving to retain juices.

recipes.recipe_name: Absinthe-Steamed Mussels with Fennel
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl holds a generous portion of plump, black-shelled mussels. Translucent batons of softened fennel and finely diced shallots are nestled among the shells. A rich, pale ivory sauce coats the mussels, accented by vibrant green specks of chopped tarragon. The arrangement is natural and overflowing, showing the entire bowl centered on a dark oak bistro table. Beside the bowl, three thick, diagonally cut slices of crusty baguette lean against each other. A single bright yellow lemon wedge sits on the edge of the plate. Soft, natural side-lighting emphasizes the glossy finish of the mussel shells and the velvety texture of the cream-based broth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a chilled glass of dry white wine or a traditional absinthe drip
Provide an empty side bowl for discarded shells
Use crusty baguette to soak up the remaining anise-scented cream sauce

ingredients.name: Fennel bulb, cut into thin batons

instructions: Scrub mussels under cold water. Discard any shells that remain open.
Melt butter in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add shallots and fennel batons. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in absinthe. Simmer for 2 minutes to reduce slightly.
Add chicken stock and mussels. Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid.
Steam for 5 minutes or until all mussels have opened.
Transfer mussels to four warm bowls using a slotted spoon. Discard unopened mussels.
Stir heavy cream into the remaining liquid in the pot.
Simmer for 3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in the chopped tarragon.
Pour the cream sauce evenly over the mussels in each bowl.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and warm baguette.
notes: Ensure all mussels are alive before cooking; they should close when tapped.
Do not overcook the mussels or they will become rubbery.
Absinthe provides a distinct licorice flavor that complements the natural sweetness of fennel.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork Binagoongan
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl holds generous 3cm chunks of pork belly, coated in a thick, dark reddish-brown shrimp paste sauce. The pork pieces show rendered fat and crispy edges. Interspersed among the meat are 5cm batons of fried eggplant, their skin a deep purple and flesh golden brown. Slices of bright red bird's eye chilies and a light scatter of sliced green spring onions provide color contrast. The sauce is glossy with visible bits of sautéed tomatoes. The dish sits on a dark wood table next to a separate bowl of fluffy, steamed white rice. A traditional spoon and fork are placed on a white cotton napkin to the side.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm jasmine rice
Provide a side of fresh green mangoes
Traditional spoon and fork service
instructions: Sear pork belly chunks in a large pan over medium-high heat until browned and fat renders.
Remove pork and set aside. Leave 15ml of fat in the pan.
Fry eggplant batons in the pork fat until softened and browned. Remove and set aside.
Sauté garlic, onion, and tomatoes in the same pan until tomatoes soften into a paste.
Add shrimp paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return pork to the pan. Stir to coat evenly with the shrimp paste mixture.
Pour in vinegar and let simmer for 2 minutes without stirring.
Add water, sugar, and chilies. Cover and simmer over low heat for 40 minutes until pork is tender.
Increase heat to reduce sauce until thick and oily.
Fold in fried eggplant batons just before serving.
notes: Ensure the vinegar boils off before stirring to prevent a raw acidic taste.
Adjust sugar levels based on the saltiness of the specific shrimp paste brand used.

recipes.recipe_name: Melitzanes Papoutsakia
recipes.visual_description: A single medium eggplant boat sits centrally on a white porcelain plate. The skin is deep purple and slightly charred. The center is packed with a savory tomato and ground beef filling. A thick layer of ivory-colored bechamel sauce covers the top, featuring toasted golden-brown spots from the oven. Fresh green parsley is chopped roughly and scattered across the surface. The background shows a weathered light wood table and a small side dish of crumbled feta cheese. Natural sunlight illuminates the dish from the side, emphasizing the creamy sauce texture and the rich red oil from the tomato base. The composition is balanced with clean margins. The eggplant is served whole and uncut.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of block feta cheese drizzled with oil
Accompany with crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a crisp Greek Horiatiki salad
instructions: Halve eggplants lengthwise.
Scoop out center flesh to create a 1 cm thick shell.
Brush shells with olive oil and season with salt.
Roast eggplants at 200°C for 20 minutes until soft.
Sauté onion and garlic in olive oil until translucent.
Add ground beef and cook until browned.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, cinnamon, and half the parsley.
Simmer meat sauce for 15 minutes until thick.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
Whisk in flour and cook for 2 minutes.
Gradually whisk in milk until the sauce thickens.
Remove from heat and stir in egg yolk and 50g of cheese.
Fill eggplant shells with the meat mixture.
Spread bechamel sauce over the meat.
Sprinkle remaining cheese on top.
Bake at 180°C for 30 minutes until golden brown.
Garnish with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Select eggplants of uniform size for even cooking
Ensure the bechamel is thick enough to prevent running
Kefalotyri can be replaced with Pecorino Romano if unavailable

recipes.recipe_name: Authentic Shakshuka with Feta
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant, deep-red tomato and bell pepper sauce served in a traditional black cast-iron skillet. Eight whole poached eggs are nested within the sauce, their whites opaque and yolks bright yellow and glistening. The sauce contains visible 1cm cubes of softened red bell pepper and onion. Crumbled white feta cheese is scattered across the surface, providing a sharp textural contrast. Freshly chopped green cilantro is sprinkled evenly over the top. The skillet sits on a rustic wooden board. Beside it, two thick wedges of toasted sourdough bread are placed on a clean white porcelain plate. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy sauce and soft eggs. The arrangement is organic and centered.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the skillet to the center of the table
Accompany with warm pita bread or thick crusty bread for dipping
Pair with a side of fresh cucumber and tomato salad
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large heavy skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion and red peppers. Sauté for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, cumin, paprika, and chili flakes. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer for 15 minutes until sauce thickens.
Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Use a spoon to create 8 small wells in the tomato mixture.
Crack one egg into each well.
Cover the skillet with a lid. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes.
Ensure egg whites are set and yolks remain runny.
Remove from heat immediately.
Sprinkle crumbled feta and chopped cilantro over the top.
notes: Do not overcook the eggs; the yolks must be liquid to create a sauce when broken.
Adjust chili flakes to control the heat level.
A heavy-bottomed skillet ensures even heat distribution for poaching.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Roasted Tomato and Garlic Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of deep red, velvety tomato soup fills a rustic, cream-colored ceramic bowl with slight glaze imperfections. The soup surface shows tiny black flecks of cracked black pepper and a thin, swirling drizzle of golden olive oil. Three small, hand-torn basil leaves float off-center, providing a vibrant green contrast. The bowl sits on a dark, weathered wooden table next to two thick, irregular chunks of crusty sourdough bread. A simple silver spoon rests beside the bowl on a folded linen napkin. Warm, soft kitchen lighting creates gentle shadows, highlighting the steam rising from the liquid. The arrangement is natural and asymmetrical, capturing a cozy, home-cooked meal in a lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with thick-cut crusty bread for dipping
Accompany with a side of hard aged cheese like Manchego or Pecorino
Present in wide-rimmed earthenware bowls

ingredients.name: Yellow onions, cut into thick wedges
Garlic, whole head with top sliced off

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Place tomato halves, onion wedges, and garlic head on a large baking tray.
Drizzle with 40 ml olive oil and season with salt and half the black pepper.
Roast for 40 minutes until vegetables are soft and slightly charred.
Squeeze the roasted garlic cloves from their skins into a large pot.
Add the roasted tomatoes, onions, and any juices from the tray to the pot.
Pour in the vegetable stock.
Simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Blend the mixture until smooth using an immersion blender.
Stir in the remaining black pepper and olive oil.
Ladle into bowls and garnish with torn basil.
notes: Roasting the garlic whole in its skin prevents bitterness and adds sweetness.
For a chunkier texture, blend only three-quarters of the soup.
Ensure the black pepper is freshly ground for maximum aromatic impact.

recipes.recipe_name: Oyakodon (Japanese Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Oyakodon presented in a deep, traditional indigo-patterned ceramic donburi bowl. The base consists of a clean mound of steaming, pearlescent Japanese short-grain rice. Draped over the rice is a rich, glossy layer of simmered eggs, featuring a soft and creamy curd texture. Large, succulent chunks of braised chicken thigh are embedded within the egg, showing a light golden-brown exterior. Translucent, thin-sliced onions are interspersed throughout the mixture, coated in a dark umami-rich dashi glaze. The dish is finished with a vibrant garnish of diagonally sliced green scallions and fresh mitsuba leaves. The bowl sits on a minimalist light oak table accompanied by dark wooden chopsticks on a small ceramic rest.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of miso soup
Accompany with takuan (pickled daikon radish)
Offer shichimi togarashi (seven-spice powder) on the side
instructions: Combine dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a wide shallow pan.
Bring the liquid to a simmer over medium heat.
Add sliced onions to the pan. Cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Add chicken chunks in a single layer. Simmer for 6 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Slowly pour beaten eggs in a circular motion over the chicken and onions.
Cover the pan immediately. Cook for 45 seconds until eggs are soft-set.
Divide hot rice into four deep ceramic bowls.
Slide a portion of the chicken and egg mixture onto each rice bowl.
Garnish with scallions and fresh mitsuba.
notes: Use a small Oyakodon pan for individual portions if available.
Do not over-beat the eggs to maintain distinct white and yellow streaks.
Ensure rice is hot to help steam the base of the egg mixture.

recipes.recipe_name: Patatas Bravas
