recipes.visual_description: The image showcases 800g of potatoes cut into 2cm irregular cubes, fried to a vibrant golden-brown with visible crispy, craggy edges. These chunks are piled casually in a traditional round, shallow terracotta cazuela dish, which sits centered on a weathered dark wood table. A thick, velvety salsa brava, colored deep brick-red from pimentón, is drizzled over the top, coating the potato surfaces unevenly. The arrangement is natural and unforced, with a few stray cubes resting near the edge. Warm, side-angled kitchen light highlights the oily sheen of the sauce and the matte texture of the clay vessel. A simple, off-white cloth napkin lies crumpled beside the dish, completing the rustic, homestyle snack setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with wooden toothpicks for communal snacking
Pair with a cold glass of lager or sparkling water
Present as part of a traditional tapas spread
instructions: Peel 800g potatoes.
Cut into 2cm irregular cubes.
Boil cubes in salted water for 5 minutes.
Drain and pat dry completely.
Heat 80ml olive oil in a large pan.
Fry potato cubes until golden and crisp.
Remove and drain on paper towels.
Heat 20ml oil in a small saucepan.
Add flour and both types of pimentón.
Stir for 1 minute over medium heat.
Whisk in vegetable broth slowly.
Simmer until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt.
Place potatoes in a serving dish.
Pour sauce over the center.
notes: Do not boil potatoes until soft; they must remain firm before frying
Ensure potatoes are perfectly dry before frying for maximum crispness
Adjust the hot pimentón quantity to control the spice level

recipes.recipe_name: Beef with Raspberry-Onion Glaze and Savory Onion Custard
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single 150g thick chunk of seared beef sirloin, presented whole and unsliced. The beef has a dark, caramelized exterior coated in a glossy, deep-red raspberry and onion glaze. It rests upon a smooth, circular bed of bright green pea puree. To the side, a pool of pale cream-colored onion and banana custard is garnished with a single, butter-toasted ladyfinger baton. Small, precise peaks of savory whipped topping are placed around the plate's perimeter. Fresh, whole raspberries and individual blanched peas provide textural contrast and color pops. The plating is clean on a white porcelain dish, showing moderate negative space. The setting is a rustic wooden table with natural side lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a full-bodied red wine like a Bordeaux
Use traditional silver steak knives
Present on warmed white porcelain plates
instructions: Roast half of one onion and the half banana at 200°C for 15 minutes.
Blend the roasted onion and banana with cream until smooth.
Whisk egg yolks into the cream mixture in a small saucepan.
Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened into a custard. Season with salt.
Sauté the remaining sliced onions with raspberry jam and 30ml water until syrupy.
Blanch peas in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and blend with butter and salt.
Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pan. Sear beef for 4 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Remove beef and let rest for 5 minutes.
Toast ladyfingers in the same pan until golden and crisp.
Whip the topping with a pinch of salt until stiff peaks form.
Spread pea puree on the plate. Place the whole beef chunk on top.
Drizzle the raspberry-onion glaze over the beef.
Add a spoonful of onion custard and top with a ladyfinger.
Garnish with fresh raspberries and small dollops of savory whipped topping.
notes: Ensure the whipped topping is unsweetened to maintain the savory profile.
The banana provides a unique earthy starchiness to the onion custard without adding excessive sweetness.
Resting the beef is essential to retain juices.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosemary and Thyme Braised Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown bone-in chicken thigh sits at the center of a wide white porcelain plate. The skin is crispy and glistening with a light herb-infused jus. Surrounding the chicken are tender carrot batons and roasted potato wedges, showing light caramelization. Small flecks of cooked rosemary and thyme leaves are scattered naturally over the vegetables. A fresh, vibrant green rosemary sprig rests elegantly against the chicken. The dish is served on a dark wood bistro table with a crisp white linen napkin and silver utensils. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the glossy sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to soak up the braising liquid.
Pair with a crisp French white wine like a Sauvignon Blanc.
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the skillet.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a plate.
Add butter to the same skillet.
Sauté onion, carrot batons, and potato halves for 5 minutes.
Add garlic, rosemary sprigs, and thyme sprigs.
Pour in white wine to deglaze the pan.
Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits.
Return chicken to the skillet skin-side up.
Pour in chicken stock until it reaches halfway up the chicken.
Simmer covered for 25 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove lid and simmer for 5 minutes to reduce the sauce.
notes: Ensure the skin stays above the liquid level while braising to maintain crispness.
Use high-quality chicken stock for a deeper flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Bread and Tortilla Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single square portion of Savory Bread and Tortilla Gratin is presented on a minimalist white porcelain plate. The surface features a mosaic of textures: golden-brown, crunchy fried bread cubes contrast with pools of melted, toasted mozzarella cheese. Deep red marinara sauce creates a marbled effect across the top surface. Inside the cross-section, layers of soft white bread medallions and thick-cut tortilla squares are bound by a silky cream custard. Dark, jammy caramelized onions are visible between the layers. The dish is finished with a light sheen of melted butter and a sprinkle of cracked black pepper. It sits on a light oak table in a sunlit bistro. A crisp white cotton napkin and polished silver fork rest beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of lightly dressed arugula
Pair with a crisp dry white wine
Present in individual ceramic ramekins for formal service
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Sauté onions in ghee over medium heat for 15 minutes until softened.
Add orange juice to deglaze the pan.
Continue cooking until liquid evaporates and onions are dark brown.
Whisk egg whites, cream, and 75g of cheese in a mixing bowl.
Mix marinara sauce with water in a small bowl.
Grease a 20cm baking dish with butter.
Layer bread cubes, tortilla squares, and caramelized onions in the dish.
Pour the cream and egg white mixture evenly over the layers.
Drip marinara sauce across the top and swirl with a knife.
Top with remaining cheese and fried bread cubes.
Bake for 25 minutes until the center is set and the top is golden-brown.
notes: Ensure the egg whites are fully incorporated into the cream for a consistent set.
The orange juice adds a necessary acidity to balance the richness of the ghee and cream.
Use stale bread for better absorption of the custard.

recipes.recipe_name: Bee Pollen and Honey Glazed Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single whole roasted chicken thigh sits at the center of a clean white porcelain plate. The skin is a deep golden brown, glazed with honey and generously encrusted with vibrant yellow bee pollen granules and chopped green thyme. Surrounding the chicken are roasted fingerling potato halves and whole baby carrots, showing caramelized edges from the pan-searing process. The arrangement is organic and centered, leaving ample negative space at the plate's edges. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the granular pollen. A halved charred lemon rests to the side. The dish is set on a light oak table with a folded white cotton napkin and polished silver fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up honey-infused pan juices.
Pair with a light, floral white wine like Viognier.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in oven-proof skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden.
Flip chicken and remove from pan.
Toss potatoes and carrots in the pan drippings.
Mix honey, garlic, thyme, and 15g bee pollen in a bowl.
Brush honey mixture over the chicken skin.
Place chicken on top of the vegetables in the skillet.
Roast for 25 minutes until chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Sprinkle remaining bee pollen over the chicken.
Squeeze lemon over the dish before serving.
notes: Bee pollen adds floral and nutty complexity to the savory glaze.
Ensure chicken skin is very dry before searing for maximum crispness.
Use high-quality local honey for the best flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Candied Abalone with Light Soy Caramel and Doubanjiang Chocolate
recipes.visual_description: A single whole candied abalone sits atop a smooth, organic sweep of dark doubanjiang chocolate ganache. The abalone is glazed to a high-gloss, deep mahogany finish with light soy caramel. The plate is a matte-finished celadon ceramic, providing a soft green contrast to the dark chocolate and rich brown abalone. A single, precise fleck of gold leaf rests on the highest point of the abalone. Tiny droplets of clear soy caramel are dotted around the ganache with architectural precision. The lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows across the textured surface of the abalone. The arrangement uses significant negative space on the plate for a refined, Michelin-starred aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small cup of aged Pu-erh tea
Use a dedicated silver dessert spoon
Present on a heavy ceramic or stone plate
instructions: Combine 100g sugar, 400ml water, and 15ml light soy sauce in a pot.
Simmer cleaned abalone in the liquid over low heat for 2 hours until tender.
Remove abalone and pat dry.
Heat 100g sugar in a dry pan until it turns amber.
Whisk in 45ml light soy sauce and butter to create a soy caramel.
Toss the tender abalone in the soy caramel until thickly glazed.
Heat heavy cream and doubanjiang until simmering.
Strain cream through a fine mesh sieve onto chopped dark chocolate.
Whisk chocolate and cream until a smooth ganache forms.
Allow ganache to set slightly at room temperature.
Place a spoonful of doubanjiang chocolate ganache on each plate.
Top with one whole glazed candied abalone.
Garnish with a small fragment of gold leaf.
notes: Ensure the doubanjiang is strained to remove all solids for a silky ganache.
Low heat during abalone braising is essential to prevent a rubbery texture.
The soy caramel should be salty and sweet to balance the dark chocolate.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Beef and Vegetable Skewers
recipes.visual_description: The dish features two long metal skewers stacked with charred 3cm beef cubes and vibrant vegetables. The beef is seared to a deep mahogany brown with distinct grill marks. Interspersed between the meat are charred red bell pepper squares, softened red onion wedges, and thick zucchini rounds with golden-brown edges. The skewers are placed on a clean white porcelain plate, positioned diagonally. A small, rustic terracotta bowl filled with thick, creamy white tzatziki sits to the side, garnished with a single green dill sprig. A piece of charred, folded pita bread rests on the edge of the plate. The scene is set on a light oak table with a blue-and-white striped linen napkin and natural, bright side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread
Accompany with a side of lemon wedges
Pair with a classic Horiatiki salad

ingredients.name: Red bell peppers, cut into 3cm squares
Red onions, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Toss beef cubes in the marinade until well coated.
Refrigerate beef for at least 1 hour.
Thread beef, peppers, onions, and zucchini alternately onto metal skewers.
Preheat a grill pan or outdoor grill to medium-high heat.
Grill skewers for 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred and cooked to desired doneness.
Combine Greek yogurt, grated cucumber, and dill in a small bowl to make tzatziki.
Rest the beef skewers for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve skewers hot with the chilled tzatziki sauce.
notes: Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes if not using metal skewers to prevent burning.
Ensure the beef is at room temperature before grilling for even cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Dal Tadka
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy yellow Dal Tadka is presented in a polished stainless steel bowl. The dal has a thick, flowing consistency. A vibrant tempering of melted ghee, toasted cumin seeds, and two whole charred red chilies rests on the surface. Small chunks of softened tomato and translucent onions are visible throughout the dal. A crown of fresh, bright green coriander leaves provides contrast. The bowl sits on a clean white plate alongside a small mound of fragrant, long-grain basmati rice and a wedge of fresh lime. The background features a modern bistro setting with a light wood surface and a linen napkin. Natural light emphasizes the rich textures and glossy finish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed long-grain Basmati rice
Accompany with buttered garlic Naan
Include a side of mango pickle and fresh red onion rings
Serve in a traditional copper or stainless steel katori
instructions: Rinse toor dal until water runs clear.
Boil dal in 1L water with turmeric and salt until tender.
Whisk cooked dal to a creamy, fluid consistency.
Heat ghee in a small heavy-bottomed pan.
Add cumin seeds and dried red chilies until they sizzle.
Add diced onions and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and green chilies for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes and chili powder.
Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates.
Stir in asafoetida and remove from heat.
Pour the hot tempering mixture over the cooked dal.
Simmer for 5 minutes to meld flavors.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander.
notes: Adjust consistency with hot water if the dal becomes too thick.
Do not burn the cumin seeds during tempering as they will turn bitter.
For an authentic smoky flavor, use the Dhungar method with a hot coal.

recipes.recipe_name: Stuffed Acorn Squash with Kielbasa
recipes.visual_description: A roasted acorn squash half sits centered on a white porcelain plate. The squash skin is a deep forest green, contrasting with the vibrant orange flesh. The cavity is filled with a savory custard of egg substitute and Neufchatel, generously packed with 1cm cubes of seared, dark-red kielbasa. A thick layer of melted Muenster cheese blankets the top, featuring toasted golden-brown bubbles. The plate is garnished with a light scattering of finely chopped bright green parsley. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark oak table. A single stainless steel fork and a grey cotton napkin are placed neatly to the left. Natural light highlights the creamy texture of the filling and the charred edges of the sausage.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of chilled fermented dill pickles.
Accompany with thick-cut toasted rye bread.
Pair with a crisp pilsner or dry cider.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Halve squashes lengthwise. Remove seeds.
Brush flesh with olive oil. Season with salt.
Roast squash face down on a tray for 30 minutes.
Cut kielbasa into 1cm cubes.
Dice onion into small pieces. Mince garlic.
Sauté kielbasa cubes in a pan until browned.
Add onion and garlic. Cook 5 minutes until soft.
Whisk egg substitute, Neufchatel, and marjoram in a bowl.
Fold kielbasa mixture into the egg base.
Flip squashes upright. Fill cavities with the mixture.
Shred Muenster cheese. Sprinkle over the filling.
Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes until filling sets.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Soften Neufchatel at room temperature before whisking to avoid lumps.
Choose squashes with flat bottoms to prevent tipping during baking.
Ensure kielbasa is well-browned for maximum savory depth.

recipes.recipe_name: Dal Tadka
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy yellow Dal Tadka is presented in a polished stainless steel bowl. The dal has a thick, flowing consistency. A vibrant tempering of melted ghee, toasted cumin seeds, and two whole charred red chilies rests on the surface. Small chunks of softened tomato and translucent onions are visible throughout the dal. A crown of fresh, bright green coriander leaves provides contrast. The bowl sits on a clean white plate alongside a small mound of fragrant, long-grain basmati rice and a wedge of fresh lime. The background features a modern bistro setting with a light wood surface and a linen napkin. Natural light emphasizes the rich textures and glossy finish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed long-grain Basmati rice
Accompany with buttered garlic Naan
Include a side of mango pickle and fresh red onion rings
Serve in a traditional copper or stainless steel katori
instructions: Rinse toor dal until water runs clear.
Boil dal in 1L water with turmeric and salt until tender.
Whisk cooked dal to a creamy, fluid consistency.
Heat ghee in a small heavy-bottomed pan.
Add cumin seeds and dried red chilies until they sizzle.
Add diced onions and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and green chilies for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes and chili powder.
Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates.
Stir in asafoetida and remove from heat.
Pour the hot tempering mixture over the cooked dal.
Simmer for 5 minutes to meld flavors.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander.
notes: Adjust consistency with hot water if the dal becomes too thick.
Do not burn the cumin seeds during tempering as they will turn bitter.
For an authentic smoky flavor, use the Dhungar method with a hot coal.

recipes.recipe_name: Candied Abalone with Light Soy Caramel and Doubanjiang Chocolate
recipes.visual_description: A single whole candied abalone sits atop a smooth, organic sweep of dark doubanjiang chocolate ganache. The abalone is glazed to a high-gloss, deep mahogany finish with light soy caramel. The plate is a matte-finished celadon ceramic, providing a soft green contrast to the dark chocolate and rich brown abalone. A single, precise fleck of gold leaf rests on the highest point of the abalone. Tiny droplets of clear soy caramel are dotted around the ganache with architectural precision. The lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows across the textured surface of the abalone. The arrangement uses significant negative space on the plate for a refined, Michelin-starred aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small cup of aged Pu-erh tea
Use a dedicated silver dessert spoon
Present on a heavy ceramic or stone plate
instructions: Combine 100g sugar, 400ml water, and 15ml light soy sauce in a pot.
Simmer cleaned abalone in the liquid over low heat for 2 hours until tender.
Remove abalone and pat dry.
Heat 100g sugar in a dry pan until it turns amber.
Whisk in 45ml light soy sauce and butter to create a soy caramel.
Toss the tender abalone in the soy caramel until thickly glazed.
Heat heavy cream and doubanjiang until simmering.
Strain cream through a fine mesh sieve onto chopped dark chocolate.
Whisk chocolate and cream until a smooth ganache forms.
Allow ganache to set slightly at room temperature.
Place a spoonful of doubanjiang chocolate ganache on each plate.
Top with one whole glazed candied abalone.
Garnish with a small fragment of gold leaf.
notes: Ensure the doubanjiang is strained to remove all solids for a silky ganache.
Low heat during abalone braising is essential to prevent a rubbery texture.
The soy caramel should be salty and sweet to balance the dark chocolate.

recipes.recipe_name: Middle Eastern Spiced Chicken with Clove Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a clean white porcelain plate. The base is a fluffy mound of clove-scented basmati rice, showing visible whole cloves and specks of cracked black pepper. A whole, pan-seared chicken thigh is placed centrally on the rice. The chicken skin is deep golden-brown and crispy. A vibrant, chunky sauce of softened red onion dice and cooked tomato pieces is spooned partially over the chicken. The chicken is kept whole and not sliced. The plate features moderate negative space. The setting includes a dark wooden table, a simple cotton napkin, and a small side bowl of yogurt. Natural side-lighting highlights the texture of the crispy skin and individual rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of plain thick yogurt
Accompany with fresh flatbread
Garnish with fresh parsley or mint leaves
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Heat 5ml oil in a small pot. Add cloves and fry for 30 seconds.
Add rice and a pinch of salt. Stir to coat in oil.
Add 150ml water. Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 12 minutes. Remove from heat.
Season chicken with salt and cracked black pepper.
Heat 15ml oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down. Sear until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip chicken. Add onion and garlic to the skillet.
Sauté vegetables until softened. Add diced tomatoes.
Cook until tomatoes break down into a thick sauce.
Stir in lemon juice. Simmer until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Rest the whole chicken piece for 3 minutes before serving.
notes: Do not over-stir the rice after cooking to keep grains separate.
Ensure the skillet is hot before adding chicken to achieve maximum skin crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Shrimp Tostadas
recipes.visual_description: Two golden, circular corn tostadas sit centered on a clean white porcelain plate. A vibrant bed of finely shredded bright green lettuce forms the base. Scattered across the lettuce are small, precise cubes of ruby-red tomato. Five large, plump shrimp, seared to a deep orange with visible char marks, are arranged naturally on top. Interspersed among the shrimp are generous, creamy cubes of bright green avocado. The dish is crowned with thin, translucent strips of neon-pink pickled red onion and fresh cilantro leaves. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the textures of the crispy tortilla and succulent shrimp. A small ceramic bowl of salsa and lime wedges sit nearby on a rustic wooden table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of salsa verde or salsa roja
Provide fresh lime wedges for squeezing over the shrimp
Accompany with a side of Mexican street corn (elote)
instructions: Combine sliced red onions with 30 ml lime juice and a pinch of salt. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Toss cubed avocados with 10 ml lime juice to prevent browning.
Season shrimp with chili powder, salt, pepper, and 15 ml olive oil.
Heat a large skillet over high heat. Add remaining oil.
Sear shrimp for 2 minutes per side until opaque and slightly charred. Remove from heat.
Place two tostadas on each plate.
Layer shredded lettuce evenly across the tostadas.
Add diced tomatoes over the lettuce.
Place 5-6 whole seared shrimp on each tostada. Do not slice the shrimp.
Top with avocado cubes and pickled red onions.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.
notes: Ensure the skillet is very hot before adding shrimp for the best sear.
Drain the pickled onions slightly before topping to keep the tostada crispy.

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Braised Plant-Based Abalone
recipes.visual_description: The dish features four thick, golden-seared King Oyster mushroom rounds, deeply scored with a diamond pattern to mimic traditional abalone. The mushrooms are coated in a glossy, translucent, dark reddish-brown doubanjiang sauce that clings to the textured surface. These pieces are arranged naturally in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl atop a vibrant green bed of blanched baby bok choy halves. The sauce pools slightly at the bottom, highlighting the rich color contrast between the dark braise and the bright greens. The setting is a rustic wooden kitchen table with a side of steamed white rice in a small porcelain bowl and dark bamboo chopsticks resting nearby under warm, soft lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice to balance the saltiness
Accompany with a side of pickled radish or cucumber
Present in a communal shallow bowl for family-style dining
instructions: Cut mushroom caps into 2cm thick rounds.
Score one side of each round in a deep diamond pattern.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Sear mushroom rounds for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Sauté ginger and garlic in the remaining oil for 30 seconds.
Add doubanjiang and stir until the oil turns red.
Pour in vegetable stock, light soy sauce, and sugar.
Return mushrooms to the wok and simmer for 5 minutes.
Blanch baby bok choy in boiling water for 2 minutes.
Stir cornstarch slurry into the sauce to thicken.
Arrange mushrooms over bok choy and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the doubanjiang is fried until the oil is fragrant and red for maximum flavor.
Do not overcook the bok choy; it should retain a slight crunch.

recipes.recipe_name: Cumin and Coriander Braised Lamb with White Beans
recipes.visual_description: A shallow, matte-white ceramic bowl holds a single portion of braised lamb. Three large, 4cm chunks of seared lamb shoulder sit centered in the bowl. The lamb is surrounded by creamy, whole white beans and a thick, glossy terracotta-colored tomato sauce. Visible grains of toasted cumin and coriander speckle the reduction. Small pieces of softened diced onion are incorporated into the sauce. Fresh, vibrant green coriander leaves are scattered naturally over the top. The bowl sits on a dark oak wood table next to a folded gray linen napkin and a small side dish of warm, charred flatbread. Natural side lighting highlights the succulent texture of the whole meat pieces.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita or crusty sourdough bread
Accompany with a side of harissa for extra heat
Provide a simple cucumber and tomato salad

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic, ground cumin, and ground coriander. Toast for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return lamb to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and water.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 90 minutes.
Add drained beans and salt. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Check lamb tenderness. Ensure meat is succulent and sauce is glossy.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves before serving.
notes: Do not trim all the fat from the lamb as it provides essential flavor during the braise
Ensure the sauce has reduced enough to coat the back of a spoon

recipes.recipe_name: Cider-Braised Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cider-Braised Chicken Thighs served on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two whole, skin-on chicken thighs are positioned centrally, featuring a deep golden-brown, crispy skin. They are not sliced. Surrounding the chicken are thick rounds of carrots and whole caramelized shallots. The sauce is a shimmering, amber-colored apple cider reduction that pools slightly at the base. A small sprig of fresh rosemary is placed neatly on the side. The plate is set on a light-colored wooden bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and polished stainless steel cutlery. Soft, natural light from the side emphasizes the glossy sauce and the rustic texture of the roasted vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough baguette
Pair with a glass of dry artisanal sparkling cider
Accompany with a simple green salad with vinaigrette
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from the skillet and set aside.
Add butter and whole shallots to the skillet.
Cook shallots until lightly browned on all sides.
Add carrot rounds and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in apple cider and chicken stock.
Add rosemary sprigs to the liquid.
Return chicken to the skillet skin-side up.
Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes.
Cook chicken to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken and vegetables to a warm plate.
Boil the remaining liquid for 5 minutes until thickened into a glaze.
Pour the cider reduction over the chicken to serve.
notes: Use a dry, traditional cider rather than a sweet commercial one
Keep the skin above the liquid level while simmering to maintain crispness
Ensure shallots are fully peeled but left whole for presentation

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Tahini Emulsion and Wild Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single, whole roasted chicken breast with deeply bronzed, crispy skin positioned off-center on a matte charcoal designer plate. Beside the chicken, a cluster of golden-brown sautéed chanterelle and shiitake mushrooms provides earthy texture. A silky, pale beige tahini emulsion is swirled around the base, creating a smooth contrast to the rustic ingredients. Small, precise cubes of crispy rendered bacon are scattered near the mushrooms. The arrangement is organic and flowing, utilizing significant negative space. Lighting is dramatic and directional, casting soft shadows across a dark grey marble surface. A single sprig of micro-parsley adds a vibrant green accent. The composition is sophisticated, highlighting the interplay of creamy and crunchy textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm artisan flatbread
Accompany with pickled radishes
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Dice bacon into 5mm cubes.
Render bacon in a pan until crispy.
Remove bacon and reserve fat.
Season chicken breasts with salt.
Sear chicken skin-side down in bacon fat for 5 minutes.
Roast chicken in oven until internal temperature is 75°C.
Sauté mushrooms in the same pan until golden.
Whisk tahini, stock, and lemon juice over low heat until smooth.
Spoon tahini emulsion onto the plate.
Place whole chicken breast onto the sauce.
Garnish with mushrooms and bacon.
notes: Cook chicken to minimum internal temperature of 75°C
Use high-quality stone-ground tahini for the best emulsion consistency

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Tuna with Ginger-Soy Glaze
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single, thick, whole tuna medallion seared to a deep golden-brown crust on the top and bottom. The tuna remains unsliced, showcasing its solid form. It sits centrally on a clean white porcelain plate, coated in a dark, glossy ginger-soy glaze that pools slightly at the base. To the side, two vibrant green baby bok choy halves are arranged, showing light char marks on their tender white stalks. The tuna is topped with a neat sprinkle of bright green scallions and white sesame seeds. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table, a grey linen napkin, and dark wood chopsticks resting on a ceramic holder. Natural light emphasizes the glaze's sheen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed short-grain rice
Accompany with pickled ginger (gari) and wasabi
Present with a small bowl of miso soup
instructions: Whisk soy sauce, mirin, rice vinegar, ginger, and garlic in a small bowl.
Pat tuna steaks completely dry with paper towels.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy cast-iron skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Sear tuna steaks for 90 seconds per side to achieve a crust while keeping the center rare.
Remove tuna from the pan and rest on a warm plate.
Wipe the pan clean and add sesame oil.
Place bok choy cut-side down in the pan and cook for 3 minutes until charred and tender.
Remove bok choy from the pan.
Pour the soy mixture into the pan and simmer for 2 minutes until it thickens into a glossy glaze.
Place one whole tuna steak and two bok choy halves on each plate.
Spoon the glaze generously over the tuna.
Garnish with sliced scallions and sesame seeds.
notes: Ensure the pan is smoking hot before searing to prevent the tuna from sticking.
Do not overcook; the center should remain cool and pink.
Use high-quality soy sauce for a deeper umami flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken with Cranberry-Chipotle Sauce and Panela
recipes.visual_description: A single whole pan-seared chicken breast sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken features a deep golden-brown crust. A rich, dark crimson sauce made from cranberries and chipotle is draped over the chicken, showing visible whole softened cranberries. Four 2cm cubes of fresh, bright white panela cheese are placed neatly around the base of the meat. The plate is garnished with fresh green cilantro sprigs. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark oak table, a neutral linen napkin, and a small basket of warm corn tortillas in the background. Natural light creates soft shadows, emphasizing the textures of the glossy sauce and the firm cheese.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Fresh lime wedges
Mexican red rice
instructions: Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken for 6 minutes per side.
Confirm chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and let rest.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pan until soft.
Add dried cranberries, minced chipotle, and chicken stock.
Simmer for 8 minutes until sauce reduces and thickens.
Return chicken to the pan to coat with sauce.
Cut panela cheese into 2cm cubes.
Place whole chicken breast on plate and top with sauce and cheese cubes.
notes: Panela cheese softens but does not melt completely
Use more chipotle for increased heat

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Home-Style Chicken Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Murgh Kari served in a traditional hammered brass bowl. The bowl sits on a rustic wooden table. Large, irregular chunks of bone-in chicken are submerged in a thick, textured reddish-brown gravy. The sauce shows visible bits of softened red onion and tomato pulp. Flecks of toasted cumin seeds and coarse black pepper are scattered throughout. A vibrant garnish of roughly chopped cilantro sits on top. Beside the bowl, a small stack of folded, charred roti rests on a simple cloth napkin. A side of fluffy, long-grain basmati rice is visible. The lighting is warm and domestic, casting soft shadows. The entire plate and its accompaniments are shown clearly.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed basmati rice
Accompany with warm roti or naan
Include a side of sliced raw red onions and lemon wedges
Provide a small bowl of plain yogurt

ingredients.name: chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into large chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds. Fry until they sizzle.
Add diced red onions. Sauté until golden brown.
Stir in minced garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, turmeric, chili powder, and salt.
Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates from the mixture.
Add chicken chunks. Stir to coat thoroughly.
Sauté chicken for 5 minutes.
Pour in water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover with a lid.
Simmer for 25 minutes.
Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in freshly cracked black pepper.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.
notes: Bone-in chicken provides more flavor to the gravy
The 'bhuna' process is key for deep flavor
Adjust black pepper for desired heat level

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Braised Beef Short Ribs (Galbi Jjim)
recipes.visual_description: The dish features four large, bone-in beef short rib chunks, deeply glazed in a dark, glossy mahogany sauce. The meat is tender and intact, positioned centrally in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Surrounding the beef are three rounded cylinders of Korean radish and three thick carrot batons, all softened and stained golden-brown from the braise. Four halved shiitake mushrooms are nestled between the meat and vegetables. A light sprinkle of bright green sliced scallions and toasted white sesame seeds provides a textural contrast. The sauce pools slightly at the base, reflecting the soft overhead light. Beside the bowl sit stainless steel chopsticks and a long-handled spoon on a dark wood table.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bowl of multi-grain rice (Japgokbap)
Accompany with small dishes of Napa cabbage kimchi and pickled radish
Provide stainless steel chopsticks and a long-handled spoon
Present in a traditional ceramic or stone bowl to retain heat
instructions: Soak beef ribs in cold water for 30 minutes to remove excess blood.
Drain and rinse the ribs thoroughly.
Blanch ribs in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Drain and rinse again to remove impurities.
Combine soy sauce, water, pear juice, mirin, sugar, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil.
Place ribs in a heavy-bottomed pot and pour in the sauce mixture.
Simmer covered over low heat for 60 minutes.
Round the edges of radish and carrot chunks with a peeler to prevent breaking.
Add radish, carrots, and mushrooms to the pot.
Simmer for 40 minutes until meat is tender and sauce reduces to a glaze.
Skim excess fat from the surface of the sauce.
Garnish with green onions and sesame seeds before serving.
notes: Rounding the vegetable edges is a traditional technique called 'chamfering' to keep the sauce clear.
Pear juice contains enzymes that tenderize the beef naturally.

recipes.recipe_name: Authentic Sichuan Dan Dan Mian
Savory Barley and Rice Pilaf with Poached Egg and Yogurt
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow white porcelain bowl features a vibrant, textured mound of mixed grains. The pearl barley and long-grain rice are interspersed with plump, bright red goji berries and 1cm cubes of golden-brown caramelized pear. A single soft-poached egg is positioned centrally on top, showing a firm, opaque white surface. A thick, glossy ribbon of snowy white Greek yogurt is artfully swirled around the base of the grains. The dish is finished with a light dusting of coarse cracked black pepper. The setting is a dark rustic wooden table with a folded white linen napkin and silver spoon. Natural side lighting emphasizes the grain textures and the soft curve of the egg.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm flatbread
Accompany with a side of pickled cucumbers
Garnish with fresh mint leaves if available
instructions: Soak goji berries in 50ml warm water for 10 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Sauté onion and garlic for 4 minutes until translucent.
Add barley and rice to the pot. Toast grains for 2 minutes while stirring.
Stir in ground cumin. Add vegetable stock and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until liquid is absorbed.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a skillet. Sauté diced pears for 5 minutes until caramelized and golden.
Fold sautéed pears and rehydrated goji berries into the cooked grain mixture.
Season the pilaf with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Poach eggs in simmering water for 3 minutes until whites are set but yolks remain runny.
Whisk yogurt with a pinch of salt until smooth.
Divide pilaf into four bowls. Top each with a poached egg and a generous dollop of yogurt.
notes: Ensure pears are firm so they maintain their shape during sautéing.
Barley provides a chewy texture that contrasts well with the soft rice.
For extra richness, add a knob of butter to the grains before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Normandy Pork with Apples and Cream
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served on a wide white porcelain plate. Four thick, golden-brown seared pork chunks are clustered in the center, not sliced. They are surrounded by eight caramelized apple wedges with deep golden edges. A rich, ivory-colored cider cream sauce pools around the base of the ingredients. Fresh green thyme leaves are scattered over the top for color. The plating is clean with moderate negative space. The background consists of a light oak bistro table, a white cotton napkin, and a silver fork. Natural light highlights the glossy texture of the sauce and the rustic sear on the pork chunks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of buttery mashed potatoes or crusty baguette
Pair with a chilled glass of dry Norman cider
Traditional French bistro presentation on white ceramic

ingredients.name: Granny Smith apples, peeled and cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season pork chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks for 3 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove from pan.
Melt butter in the same pan. Add apple wedges.
Sauté apples until caramelized and golden. Remove from pan.
Add shallots to the pan. Cook for 2 minutes until translucent.
Add Calvados and cider. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer liquid until reduced by half.
Whisk in crème fraîche and thyme sprigs.
Return pork and apples to the skillet.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes until sauce thickens and pork is tender.
Remove thyme sprigs before serving.
notes: Ensure the pan is hot before adding pork to achieve a deep sear.
Use firm apples like Granny Smith so they maintain their shape during sautéing.
If the sauce is too thick, add a splash more cider.

recipes.recipe_name: Tortellini with Sausage and Roasted Acorn Squash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of tortellini served on a clean white porcelain shallow bowl. The dish features plump cheese tortellini tossed with vibrant orange 1.5cm cubes of roasted acorn squash showing caramelized edges. Large, irregular 2cm chunks of browned Italian sausage are distributed throughout the bowl, never sliced or fanned. Melted provolone cheese creates delicate, translucent white ribbons over the pasta. Crispy, dark green sage leaves provide a sharp color contrast against the golden tones. The sauce is glossy and light, emulsified to coat each element. The bowl sits on a dark oak wood table in a modern bistro setting. A white cotton napkin and polished silver fork are placed beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in wide-rimmed pasta bowls
Pair with a crisp Pinot Grigio
Accompany with crusty focaccia bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel acorn squash and dice into 1.5cm cubes.
Toss squash cubes with olive oil and salt on a baking sheet.
Roast squash for 20 minutes until tender and edges are caramelized.
Boil tortellini in salted water until al dente.
Reserve 120ml of pasta cooking water and drain the rest.
Remove sausage from casings and break into 2cm chunks.
Brown sausage chunks in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Remove sausage and set aside.
Melt butter in the same skillet and add minced garlic and sage leaves.
Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add tortellini, sausage, squash, and reserved pasta water to the skillet.
Toss gently over medium heat until a glossy sauce forms.
Grate provolone over the mixture and stir until just melted.
Season with black pepper and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the acorn squash cubes are uniform for even roasting
Use aged provolone for a sharper flavor profile
Do not overcook the pasta as it will finish in the skillet

recipes.recipe_name: Paparajotes Murcianos
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of four Paparajotes Murcianos is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The fried lemon leaves are stacked loosely, showing their organic shapes under a crisp, golden-brown batter. Each piece is generously coated in a visible crystalline mixture of white sugar and dark ground cinnamon. The batter is light and aerated with small surface bubbles from frying. The green stems of the lemon leaves protrude from the base of the batter, indicating the natural core. Beside the plate sits a small glass of amber-colored Mistela wine. The setting is a rustic wooden bistro table under soft, natural light, emphasizing the textures of the fried dough and the fine spice dust.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of Mistela or sweet wine
Accompany with Café Asiático
Explain to guests that the leaf inside is for flavor only and should not be eaten
instructions: Wash and dry lemon leaves thoroughly.
Whisk the egg in a large bowl.
Add milk and salt to the egg. Mix well.
Sift flour and baking powder into the bowl.
Whisk until the batter is smooth and thick.
Combine sugar and cinnamon in a shallow dish.
Heat olive oil to 180°C in a deep pan.
Hold a lemon leaf by the stem.
Dip the leaf into the batter to coat both sides.
Fry leaves in batches until golden brown on both sides.
Drain fried leaves on paper towels.
Toss immediately in the cinnamon sugar mixture.
Serve immediately while hot.
notes: Use young, waxy leaves for the best aroma
Ensure the oil is hot to prevent the batter from becoming greasy
The batter should be thick enough to cling to the leaf surface

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Cacciatora
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Cacciatora is presented on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are stacked slightly in the center, featuring deeply browned, caramelized skin. A thick, rustic sauce covers the base of the plate, filled with visible small cubes of orange carrots, green celery, and translucent onions. Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Paprika-Rubbed Turkey with Mediterranean Pulse Salad
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single, whole seared turkey breast portion positioned atop a textured bed of quinoa and mixed pulses. The turkey displays a vibrant, dark-red crust from the smoked paprika rub with distinct caramelization. Below, the salad consists of golden chickpeas, earthy brown lentils, and creamy white beans, all tossed with fluffy quinoa. Bright green specks of finely chopped parsley and basil provide a fresh contrast against the warm tones of the grains. The plating is clean and centered on a white porcelain dish, leaving ample negative space. A drizzle of herb-infused olive oil adds a subtle sheen. The scene is set on a light wooden table with a white cotton napkin and polished flatware under soft, natural light.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of lemon wedges to brighten the pulse salad
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine or sparkling water
Present on warm plates to maintain the temperature of the legumes
instructions: Rinse quinoa thoroughly. Boil in 300ml salted water for 15 minutes. Drain and fluff with a fork.
Combine paprika, half the garlic, salt, pepper, and 20ml olive oil in a bowl.
Rub the mixture onto the turkey portions.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear turkey 5-6 minutes per side. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest for 5 minutes.
In the same skillet, add remaining olive oil and garlic. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add chickpeas, lentils, beans, and quinoa. Stir to coat and heat through for 3 minutes.
Remove from heat. Fold in parsley and basil. Season with salt and pepper.
Place a mound of the pulse salad in the center of each plate.
Top with one whole turkey portion.
notes: Ensure the turkey reaches exactly 75°C for safety and juiciness
Use high-quality smoked paprika for the best flavor profile
Resting the turkey is essential to keep the juices within the whole piece

recipes.recipe_name: Tori no Teriyaki (Japanese Pan-Seared Teriyaki Chicken)
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large chunks of chicken thighs, their skin rendered crisp and glistening with a deep mahogany glaze. The chicken sits in a dark, textured ceramic bowl, arranged in a casual, overlapping pile. Finely sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds provide a fresh contrast against the dark sauce. The entire plate is visible, accompanied by a small wooden bowl of steamed white rice and a side of yellow pickled daikon. The setting is a well-used wooden table in a home kitchen. Natural light emphasizes the sticky, caramelized texture of the glaze. A pair of bamboo chopsticks rests on a small stone holder beside the bowl, creating an authentic Japanese home-dining scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed short-grain white rice
Accompany with miso soup and seasonal pickles (tsukemono)
Provide chopsticks and a small wet towel (oshibori)
instructions: Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Cut chicken into large, thick chunks.
Whisk soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and ginger in a small bowl.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken chunks skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 5 minutes until skin is golden and crispy.
Flip chicken pieces.
Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Wipe excess fat from the pan using paper towels.
Pour the sauce mixture over the chicken.
Simmer sauce until it thickens into a glossy glaze.
Spoon sauce repeatedly over chicken to coat thoroughly.
Remove from heat immediately.
notes: Wiping the fat from the pan is essential for the glaze to adhere to the meat.
Do not overcook the sauce or it will become bitter and burnt.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Acai-Glazed Beef with Cassava
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents four large, tender chunks of beef chuck braised to a deep, dark purple-burgundy hue from the acai reduction. These chunks are arranged centrally in a wide, matte white porcelain bowl. Surrounding the beef are several 3cm cubes of pale, cream-colored boiled cassava, providing a sharp color contrast. The acai-based sauce is thick and glossy, coating the meat and pooling slightly at the base. A small, neat mound of golden-brown toasted farofa sits on the side. Fresh, vibrant green cilantro leaves are scattered over the meat. The setting includes a dark wooden table, a side of white rice, and a simple cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting emphasizes the rich, earthy textures and deep colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside Brazilian white rice
Provide a side of malagueta pepper oil for heat
Accompany with toasted farofa to add crunch

ingredients.name: Cassava (yuca), peeled and cut into 3cm cubes

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt, pepper, and cumin.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides.
Remove beef and set aside.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pot for 3 minutes.
Return beef to the pot.
Pour in beef stock and unsweetened acai pulp.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes.
Add cassava cubes to the pot.
Cook for 30 more minutes until beef and cassava are tender.
Remove lid and simmer for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Use only unsweetened, pure acai pulp for this savory application
Ensure cassava is peeled deeply to remove the fibrous outer layer
Braise at a very low simmer to maintain beef tenderness

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Abalone with Bamboo Shoots and Crab Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the dish is served on a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Eight whole, glossy, dark-amber glazed abalones are arranged centrally, not sliced. They are surrounded by pale cream-colored bamboo shoot batons and earthy brown crab mushrooms. Tender, wrinkled tofu sticks are tucked beneath the seafood, absorbing the rich brown sauce. The sauce is thick and reflective, coating every ingredient evenly. Vibrant green scallion batons provide a fresh color contrast. The setting features a dark wood table with a pair of polished ebony chopsticks on a ceramic rest. A small side bowl of steamed jasmine rice and a cup of oolong tea sit in the soft-focus background. Natural window light highlights the silky texture of the braised abalone.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Accompany with hot Oolong or Pu-erh tea
Provide a communal spoon for the rich braising sauce

ingredients.name: Winter bamboo shoots, sliced into 1cm batons
Dried tofu sticks (fuzhu), soaked and cut into 5cm lengths

instructions: Soak dried tofu sticks in warm water for 2 hours until soft. Drain and set aside.
Blanch bamboo shoot batons in boiling water for 3 minutes to remove bitterness. Drain.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. Sauté ginger, garlic, and scallions until fragrant.
Add crab mushrooms and bamboo shoots. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Deglaze with Shaoxing wine. Add oyster sauce, light soy sauce, and sugar.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Add soaked tofu sticks and whole abalones to the wok.
Cover and braise on low heat for 10 minutes.
Remove lid. Increase heat to reduce liquid by one-third.
Stir in cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce until glossy.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure tofu sticks are fully hydrated to prevent a rubbery texture.
Fresh abalone requires thorough scrubbing of the dark fringe before cooking.
Adjust sugar slightly to balance the saltiness of the oyster sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Potato and Mixed Bean Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spiced Potato and Mixed Bean Curry served in a rustic, hand-thrown ceramic bowl. The 2cm potato cubes are tender with slightly rounded edges, nestled among whole pinto beans and chickpeas. The sauce is a deep ochre-red, glistening with oil and flecked with ground spices. The arrangement is natural and asymmetrical, filling the bowl without crowding. Freshly chopped green parsley and coriander leaves provide a vibrant contrast against the warm tones of the legumes. The bowl rests on a weathered wooden table. A simple stainless steel spoon and a neutral-toned cloth napkin sit nearby. Soft, side-lit kitchen lighting creates a cozy, authentic home-cooked atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm flatbread or basmati rice
Accompany with a side of plain yogurt or raita
Include a wedge of lime for acidity

ingredients.name: potatoes, peeled and cut into 2cm cubes
canned pinto beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat 30ml oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add 5g cumin seeds. Fry until they sizzle and become fragrant.
Add 500g potato cubes. Sauté for 5 minutes until edges are lightly browned.
Stir in 5g chili powder and 10g ground coriander. Toast for 30 seconds.
Add 400g pinto beans and 400g chickpeas to the pot.
Pour in 500ml water. Season with salt.
Bring liquid to a boil. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer for 20 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender.
Mash a small portion of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce.
Stir in half of the chopped parsley and coriander.
Garnish with remaining herbs before serving.
notes: Ensure potatoes are cut into uniform cubes for even cooking.
Adjust chili powder to reach desired heat level.
The sauce will continue to thicken as it cools.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Jerusalem Artichokes with Lentil Ragout
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared Jerusalem artichokes served over dark Beluga lentils. The lentils are glossy and moist, piled in the center of a clean white ceramic plate. Several large, irregular chunks of Jerusalem artichoke sit atop the lentils, featuring a heavy golden-brown sear and visible salt flakes. The artichoke skin remains intact, appearing rustic and crispy. A light drizzle of pale tahini sauce accents the dish. Vibrant green flat-leaf parsley is scattered sparingly over the top. The arrangement is organic and centered, leaving ample white space on the rim. The scene is set on a light oak table with a folded grey cotton napkin. Natural side-lighting emphasizes the earthy textures and professional plating.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm pita bread or sourdough
Accompany with a side of pickled turnips
Pair with a crisp dry white wine
instructions: Rinse lentils under cold water.
Finely dice shallots and mince garlic.
Sauté shallots in 15ml olive oil until translucent.
Add garlic and lentils to the pan.
Pour in stock and simmer for 20 minutes until lentils are tender.
Scrub Jerusalem artichokes clean and leave skins on.
Cut artichokes into 3cm thick chunks.
Steam artichoke chunks for 10 minutes until parboiled.
Heat remaining olive oil and butter in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear artichoke chunks for 6 minutes until golden-brown on all sides.
Stir lemon juice into the lentils and season with salt and pepper.
Place a mound of lentils on each plate and top with artichoke chunks.
Drizzle with tahini and garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Do not peel the artichokes as the skin provides essential texture and flavor.
Ensure the lentils remain slightly firm to the bite for a better mouthfeel.
Use high heat for searing to achieve the best caramelization on the artichokes.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Cashew Chicken (Gai Pad Med Mamuang)
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, traditional celadon ceramic bowl. The focal point features succulent 2.5cm chicken cubes, seared to a deep golden brown and coated in a dark, glossy amber glaze. Vibrant red and green bell pepper cubes provide a bright color contrast against the meat. Whole roasted cashew nuts are scattered throughout, showing a matte, toasted texture. Dark, crispy whole fried chilies and bright green 3cm spring onion batons add height and freshness. The arrangement is natural and centered with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a dark teak wood table next to a small bowl of steamed jasmine rice and a pair of traditional Thai spoons on a white cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed jasmine rice
Traditional Thai table setting includes a fork and a large spoon
Accompany with Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with chilies) for added seasoning

ingredients.name: Red and green bell peppers, 2cm cubes

instructions: Heat oil in a wok over medium heat.
Fry dried chilies until dark red and fragrant. Remove and set aside.
Increase heat to high. Add chicken cubes in a single layer.
Sear chicken until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add garlic and shallots. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add bell peppers. Toss for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Pour in oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, and stock.
Stir-fry rapidly to coat all ingredients in a thick, glossy glaze.
Fold in cashews, fried chilies, and spring onion batons.
Remove from heat immediately. Serve with jasmine rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding chicken to achieve wok hei flavor.
Do not overcook the bell peppers; they should retain a slight crunch.
Use palm sugar for a more authentic, rounded sweetness.

recipes.recipe_name: Szechuan Stir-Fried Chicken with Dry-Fried Green Beans
recipes.visual_description: The dish features 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs mixed with long, vibrant green beans that show characteristic blistering and wrinkling from the dry-frying technique. The chicken is presented in whole chunks, not sliced. Scattered throughout are bright red dried Szechuan chilies and toasted peppercorns. The arrangement is organic and centered on a clean white porcelain plate with a slight sheen from the sesame oil. Small pieces of minced garlic and ginger cling to the ingredients. The background is a dark wood bistro table with a pair of dark bamboo chopsticks and a small side bowl of steamed jasmine rice. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the blistered beans and seared poultry.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with individual bowls of steamed jasmine rice
Provide dark bamboo chopsticks
Accompany with jasmine tea or a crisp lager
instructions: Cut chicken into 3cm chunks.
Marinate chicken in soy sauce and Shaoxing wine for 15 minutes.
Trim green beans into 5cm lengths.
Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Add green beans and stir-fry until skins blister and wrinkle.
Remove beans and set aside.
Add remaining oil to wok.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Push chicken to the side of the wok.
Add chilies, peppercorns, ginger, and garlic to the center.
Fry spices for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return beans to the wok.
Add sugar and sesame oil.
Toss all ingredients together over high heat for 60 seconds.
Garnish with scallions and serve immediately.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beans to achieve the dry-fry texture
Do not overcook chicken past 75°C to ensure the meat remains juicy
Adjust chili count to control heat levels

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Paprikash
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, succulent chunks of chicken thighs coated in a thick, glossy, vibrant orange-red paprika sauce. The chicken is nestled among tender diced red and green bell peppers and earthy, golden-brown quartered cremini mushrooms. The stew is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl atop a bed of small, irregular hand-made buttered dumplings. A single, clean dollop of white sour cream sits off-center, garnished with finely chopped bright green parsley. The plate is positioned on a dark oak bistro table with a folded grey cotton napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural side-lighting highlights the creamy texture of the sauce and the rustic shapes of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Nokedli (Hungarian dumplings) or wide egg noodles
Provide a side of cucumber salad with vinegar and dill
Accompany with a glass of Hungarian dry white wine like Furmint

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless skinless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks on all sides until golden. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onions to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Add diced red and green peppers and quartered mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and paprika. Toast for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return chicken to the pan. Pour in chicken stock.
Simmer for 20 minutes until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
In a small bowl, whisk sour cream and flour until smooth.
Whisk 100ml of hot cooking liquid into the sour cream to temper it.
Stir the tempered mixture into the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Garnish with parsley.
notes: Do not let the paprika burn as it will turn bitter.
Always temper the sour cream to prevent curdling in the hot sauce.
Use authentic Hungarian sweet paprika for the most accurate flavor profile.

recipes.recipe_name: Crostini with Sautéed Apples and Gorgonzola
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of two crostini served on a rustic, cream-colored ceramic plate with slight imperfections. The ciabatta is cut into thick diagonal slices, toasted to a deep golden brown. Each slice is topped with a generous, creamy layer of Gorgonzola Dolce that is beginning to melt under the heat of the apples. The apples are cut into thick wedges, showing caramelized edges from being sautéed in butter. Coarsely crushed walnut pieces are scattered over the top. The arrangement is casual and asymmetrical on the plate. The background features a dark wood table with a linen napkin and a small bowl of extra walnuts. Warm, natural kitchen lighting highlights the textures of the crusty bread and soft cheese.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a traditional Italian antipasto
Pair with a glass of chilled Prosecco
Serve immediately while the apples are warm
instructions: Slice ciabatta into 2cm thick diagonal slices.
Toast bread slices in a pan until golden brown.
Core apples and cut into 1cm thick wedges.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Add apple wedges and rosemary sprig to the skillet.
Sauté apples for 4 minutes until soft and caramelized.
Remove rosemary sprig from the pan.
Spread a thick layer of Gorgonzola on each toast.
Place two warm apple wedges on the cheese.
Top with coarsely crushed walnuts and honey drizzle.
Season with cracked black pepper.
notes: Gorgonzola Dolce is preferred for its creamy, mild flavor compared to the sharper Piccante variety.
Keep the apple wedges thick to maintain a slight bite after sautéing.

recipes.recipe_name: Corned Beef Ragù with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A wide white porcelain bowl contains a portion of rigatoni pasta. The pasta is coated in a thick, glossy tomato ragù. Large 2cm chunks of braised corned beef are nestled among the pasta tubes, showing a tender, shredded texture. The sauce is deep crimson with visible specks of finely diced carrots and celery. A snowy layer of finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese is concentrated in the center. Three fresh, whole basil leaves are placed as a garnish. The dish is presented on a dark walnut table with a folded grey cotton napkin and a heavy silver fork. Natural light creates soft highlights on the sauce and the textured edges of the pasta.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty sourdough bread
Pair with a medium-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti
instructions: Sauté onion, carrot, and celery in olive oil over medium heat until softened.
Add garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes while stirring.
Add corned beef chunks to the pan.
Pour in red wine. Deglaze the pan by scraping the bottom. Reduce liquid by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, salt, and pepper.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until sauce thickens.
Boil rigatoni in salted water until al dente.
Drain pasta and reserve 60ml of pasta water.
Combine pasta with the sauce and reserved water. Toss over heat until emulsified.
Divide into four bowls. Top with Pecorino Romano and basil.
notes: Use low-sodium corned beef if available to better control the salt levels of the ragù.
Ensure the pasta water is well-salted to season the rigatoni from within.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Smoked Tofu and Squash Stew
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a deep, matte-finish charcoal ceramic bowl on a dark rustic wooden table. A single portion of the vibrant stew fills the center, showing thick 2cm cubes of golden-brown seared smoked tofu and roasted orange squash. Small white cauliflower florets and whole black beans are visible through the rich, reddish-brown tomato sauce. Sliced brown mushrooms and bright green peas add texture and color contrast. On top, fresh green avocado is cut into neat 1cm cubes. The bowl rests on a woven textile runner. Beside the plate are three warm, folded corn tortillas and a fresh lime wedge. Natural side lighting highlights the steam and the glossy sauce texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Fresh lime wedges
Pickled red onions
Salsa roja
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut squash into 2cm cubes.
Break cauliflower into small florets.
Toss squash and cauliflower with 15ml oil and salt.
Roast vegetables for 20 minutes until tender.
Dice onion and slice mushrooms.
Sauté onion and mushrooms in remaining oil for 5 minutes.
Cut smoked tofu into 2cm cubes.
Add tofu to the pan. Brown for 4 minutes.
Stir in cumin and paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, black beans, and vegetable stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes over medium heat.
Fold in green peas and roasted vegetables.
Season with salt and pepper.
Cube avocado into 1cm pieces for garnish.
notes: Use firm smoked tofu to prevent it from breaking during browning.
Do not overcook the cauliflower to maintain a slight bite.
Adjust chili levels by adding fresh jalapeños if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Coriander-Scented Tavuk Göğsü
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick rectangular block of white pudding sits centered on a handmade cream ceramic plate. The pudding features a matte, slightly elastic surface showing the fine texture of integrated chicken fibers. A translucent, pale green syrup made from coriander stalks and honey is drizzled over the top, pooling naturally around the base. The dish is garnished with three toasted coriander seeds and a single fresh coriander leaf. The presentation is minimalist and clean. The setting uses a reclaimed wood table and a neutral linen napkin. A traditional silver dessert spoon rests beside the plate. Soft natural side-lighting emphasizes the creamy, dense texture of the pudding and the clarity of the herb-infused syrup.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with hot Turkish tea
Present on traditional handcrafted ceramic ware
Serve chilled as a refreshing end to a meal
instructions: Simmer chicken breast in water until internal temperature reaches 75°C and fibers separate easily.
Shred the meat into very fine, microscopic fibers.
Rinse fibers in cold water repeatedly to remove all meat flavor.
Squeeze meat completely dry.
Pound the meat into a smooth, fine paste.
Combine milk, sugar, rice flour, and cornstarch in a heavy pot.
Cook over medium heat while stirring constantly until the mixture thickens.
Add the chicken paste to the thickened milk.
Whisk vigorously to incorporate the fibers into a smooth, elastic consistency.
Simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour the mixture into a shallow tray and level the surface.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours until set.
Combine coriander stalks, seeds, honey, and water in a small pan.
Simmer for 10 minutes to create a concentrated syrup.
Strain the syrup and discard the solids.
Cut the chilled pudding into thick rectangular chunks.
Drizzle with the cold coriander syrup before serving.
notes: Rinsing the chicken thoroughly is essential to ensure a neutral dessert flavor
Use the coriander stalks to ensure zero-waste and provide a citrusy aroma
The pudding should have a slightly chewy, elastic texture

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese Kaki Fry Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. On the left side, a neat mound of steamed white short-grain rice. On the right, a rich, glossy, deep-umber Japanese curry sauce containing uniform 1cm cubes of soft carrots and potatoes. Six whole, plump oysters, deep-fried to a vibrant golden-brown panko crust, are positioned across the center where the rice meets the sauce. A small, precise heap of finely shredded bright green cabbage sits at the top edge of the plate. A tablespoon of crimson-red fukujinzuke pickles adds a sharp color contrast. The setting is a light oak bistro table with a linen napkin and a pair of dark wood chopsticks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chilled barley tea (Mugicha)
Provide a small side of Tonkatsu sauce for the oysters
Use a spoon and fork or chopsticks according to Yoshoku tradition
instructions: Wash rice until water runs clear. Cook in a rice cooker or pot with 720ml water.
Sauté onions, carrots, and potatoes in a pot with 15ml oil for 5 minutes.
Add 700ml water or dashi. Bring to boil. Simmer for 10 minutes until vegetables soften.
Remove from heat. Break curry roux into pieces and stir into the pot until dissolved.
Simmer on low heat for 5 minutes until thickened.
Pat oysters dry with paper towels. Season lightly with salt.
Dredge oysters in flour. Dip in beaten eggs. Coat thoroughly with panko breadcrumbs.
Heat frying oil to 180°C. Fry oysters in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden brown.
Drain oysters on a wire rack.
Place a portion of rice on half of each plate. Pour curry sauce over the other half.
Place 6 fried oysters on top of the curry. Serve with shredded cabbage and fukujinzuke.
notes: Ensure oysters are very dry before breading to prevent the crust from peeling.
Maintain oil temperature at 180°C to ensure a crisp, non-greasy finish.
The curry sauce should be thick enough to coat a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Pinakbet
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl holds a vibrant assembly of Chicken Pinakbet. Large, succulent chunks of pan-seared chicken thighs, skin-on and golden-brown, serve as the focal point. They are surrounded by thick, tender wedges of purple-skinned eggplant and pale green crescents of bitter melon. The vegetables retain their shape while being thoroughly coated in a thick, savory sauce made from softened, burst tomatoes and fermented shrimp paste. Small bits of sautéed ginger and garlic are visible in the rich, reddish-brown reduction. The dish is garnished with a scattering of freshly sliced scallions. It is presented on a dark wood table with a side bowl of fluffy steamed jasmine rice and a traditional spoon and fork set.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed long-grain jasmine rice
Provide extra calamansi or lime wedges on the side
Eat using a spoon and fork in the traditional Filipino manner

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into 5cm chunks
Bitter melon, deseeded and sliced into 1cm crescents

instructions: Toss bitter melon slices with salt. Let stand 10 minutes. Rinse and pat dry.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until skin is golden and crisp. Remove chicken from pan.
Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger in the same pan until fragrant.
Add shrimp paste. Stir for 2 minutes until darkened.
Add tomatoes. Cook until they soften and release juices.
Return chicken to the pan. Pour in water or stock.
Simmer for 10 minutes over medium heat.
Add eggplant and bitter melon. Cover the pan.
Cook for 8 minutes until vegetables are tender but not mushy.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Season with fish sauce to taste. Serve hot.
notes: Salting the bitter melon is essential to temper its sharp bitterness.
Do not overstir once vegetables are added to maintain their structure.
Ensure the shrimp paste is well-sautéed to develop a deep umami flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Almond-Crusted Chicken with Advocaat-Agave Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A clean white porcelain plate features four 3cm chunks of almond-crusted chicken arranged in a tight, organic cluster. The chicken has a deep golden-brown, textured crust from the crushed almonds. A glossy, pale yellow glaze made from advocaat and agave coats the chicken, catching the natural light. Small 1cm translucent, jelly-like cubes of fresh aloe vera are scattered over the top and around the base. Finely minced green chives and a few red chili flakes provide vibrant color contrast. The dish is presented in a modern bistro setting on a light wood table with a white cotton napkin and polished silver fork. Ample negative space surrounds the central arrangement.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a sophisticated starter in a modern European tasting menu
Pair with a dry sparkling wine to balance the richness of the advocaat

ingredients.name: Fresh aloe vera, peeled and diced into 1cm cubes

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm uniform cubes.
Pulse almonds in a food processor until they reach a coarse, sandy texture.
Season chicken cubes with salt and black pepper.
Dredge chicken in flour, dip in beaten eggs, then coat thoroughly with crushed almonds.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry chicken chunks until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Drain fried chicken on a wire rack.
Combine advocaat, agave syrup, lime juice, and chili flakes in a small saucepan.
Simmer glaze over medium heat for 3 minutes until thickened and glossy.
Toss warm chicken chunks gently in the glaze to coat.
Plate chicken immediately and top with diced aloe vera and chives.
notes: Ensure aloe vera is thoroughly rinsed of its bitter sap before cubing.
Maintain the oil temperature to ensure the almond crust stays crisp without burning.

recipes.recipe_name: Murgh Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features Murgh Masala served in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The center contains 800g of chicken cut into 4cm chunks, thoroughly coated in a thick, vibrant rust-orange gravy. The sauce exhibits a slight sheen from the bhuna technique. A single sprig of fresh green coriander sits atop the chicken chunks. The plate is accompanied by two pieces of charred garlic naan, folded neatly to the side. A small side dish holds crisp red onion rings and a fresh lemon wedge. The setting is a dark wood table with a neutral cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the tender chicken and the viscous, spiced sauce. Minimal negative space maintains a professional, modern bistro aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with garlic naan or basmati rice
Accompany with laccha pyaaz (red onion rings) and lemon wedges
Include a side of mint chutney
instructions: Heat 45ml oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add 5g cumin seeds. Fry until they sizzle.
Add 300g chopped onions. Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in 30g ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add 5g turmeric and 10g chili powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in 200ml tomato puree. Cook until oil separates from the masala.
Lower heat. Whisk 120g yogurt and stir into the pan slowly.
Add 800g chicken chunks. Increase heat to medium. Sear for 5 minutes.
Add 250ml water and salt. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in 10g garam masala. Simmer uncovered for 3 minutes to thicken.
Garnish with 15g fresh coriander.
notes: Do not skip browning the onions; it provides the base color and depth.
Whisk the yogurt before adding to prevent curdling in the hot sauce.
Ensure the chicken is in large chunks for a better mouthfeel.

recipes.recipe_name: Mustard Fish Curry with Spicy Avocado Mash
recipes.visual_description: A single, whole seared white fish fillet sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate, coated in a vibrant, opaque ochre-yellow mustard gravy.
