notes: Ensure garlic does not burn; it should be soft and golden
Use aged Manchego for a sharper flavor profile
The sauce should be a thin, flavorful jus, not a thick gravy

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Potato Curry with Cumin Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Aloo Chicken Curry served in a deep white porcelain bowl on a light oak table. The curry features large, succulent chunks of skinless chicken thigh and 3cm cubes of golden, tender potatoes submerged in a rich, vibrant tomato-based gravy. Beside the bowl sits a neat mound of fluffy, long-grain Basmati rice speckled with toasted cumin seeds. The dish is garnished with a scatter of fresh, bright green cilantro leaves. A small side of lime wedges and pickled red onions adds color. Natural sunlight highlights the glossy texture of the sauce and the steam rising from the rice. A clean cotton napkin and a polished spoon complete the professional presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Fresh lime wedges
Pickled red onions
Traditional stainless steel spoon
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Soak rice in cold water for 30 minutes.
Cut chicken into 4cm chunks.
Peel and cut potatoes into 3cm cubes.
Finely dice tomatoes and onions.
Heat 30ml oil in a heavy pot over medium heat.
Add 2g cumin seeds until they sizzle.
Add onions and sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add diced tomatoes and salt.
Cook until tomatoes soften and oil separates.
Add chicken chunks, potato cubes, turmeric, chili powder, and garam masala.
Sauté for 5 minutes to coat ingredients.
Pour in water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes.
Confirm chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Boil rice in salted water with remaining cumin seeds until tender.
Drain rice and fluff with a fork.
Garnish curry with chopped cilantro.
notes: Ensure potatoes are tender but hold their shape.
Wash rice thoroughly to prevent sticking.
Adjust chili powder for desired heat level.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Fricassée with Creamy Potato Purée
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion served on a clean white porcelain plate. A smooth, velvety mound of potato purée sits slightly off-center, providing a soft base. Two whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs are placed directly on top of the purée. The chicken skin is deeply caramelized and crispy. A glossy, ivory-colored cream sauce is draped over the chicken, flowing naturally down the sides of the potatoes. Finely chopped green parsley is sprinkled over the dish for a fresh color accent. The plate is set on a dark wood bistro table with a white cotton napkin and silver utensils. Natural side lighting emphasizes the rich textures of the sauce and the crispy skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty baguette to soak up the cream sauce.
Pair with a crisp glass of Chardonnay or Sauvignon Blanc.
Follow with a simple green salad dressed in vinaigrette.
instructions: Peel and dice potatoes into 3cm cubes.
Boil potatoes in salted water until tender, about 15 minutes.
Drain potatoes. Mash with 50g butter and 100ml cream until smooth. Season with salt.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add 20g butter.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Sear for 2 minutes. Remove from pan and set aside.
Add remaining 30g butter to the pan. Sauté shallots and garlic for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the pan bottom. Reduce liquid by half.
Add chicken stock and thyme. Return chicken to the pan.
Simmer for 15 minutes. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from the pan. Whisk remaining 100ml cream into the sauce.
Simmer sauce for 3 minutes until thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
Place a mound of potato purée on a plate. Top with two whole chicken thighs.
Spoon sauce over the chicken. Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Do not crowd the pan when searing chicken to ensure the skin becomes crispy.
Pass the potatoes through a fine-mesh sieve for a professional restaurant-style texture.
Check the chicken temperature at the thickest part near the bone.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Garlic and Chili Chicken with Jasmine Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The base is a mound of fluffy, white jasmine rice. On top, seared chicken chunks are piled naturally, coated in a glossy, dark amber glaze. The chicken chunks show caramelized edges from the wok. Visible bits of minced golden garlic and bright red chili flecks are distributed throughout the meat. Fresh, vibrant green Thai basil leaves are scattered over the top. The dish is placed on a dark teak wood table. A traditional ceramic Thai spoon and fork rest on a clean cotton napkin to the side. Natural, soft window lighting emphasizes the steam and the glistening texture of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with chopped chilies)
Accompany with a crispy fried egg (Kai Dao) on top of the rice
Eat using a spoon in the right hand and a fork in the left to push food onto the spoon
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice until water runs clear.
Combine rice with 450ml water in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15 minutes. Keep warm.
Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a wok over high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Add remaining 15ml oil to the wok.
Stir-fry minced garlic and chilies for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return chicken to the wok.
Add oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, and sugar.
Pour in chicken stock. Toss for 1 minute until sauce thickens and coats chicken.
Turn off heat. Fold in Thai basil leaves until just wilted.
Serve chicken over steamed rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding chicken to achieve proper searing.
Do not overcook the basil; it should only wilt to maintain its aromatic oils.
Adjust chili count based on preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, charred chunks of succulent chicken submerged in a glossy, vibrant orange-red tomato gravy. The sauce has a thick, velvety texture with visible flecks of ground spices. The chicken chunks show dark, caramelized edges from the high-heat roasting. Plating is in a clean, white porcelain bowl set on a dark wooden table. A single portion is shown with a light swirl of heavy cream on top and a scattering of bright green chopped cilantro. To the side sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan bread and a small bowl of steamed long-grain basmati rice. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the rich colors and creamy consistency of the sauce while maintaining professional negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or buttered roti
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of mint-yogurt raita and kachumber salad
Serve in a traditional hammered copper karahi
instructions: Combine yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp chili powder.
Toss chicken chunks in marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Place chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Roast chicken 15 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté onions until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in remaining garam masala, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens and oil separates.
Stir in butter and heavy cream. Season with salt.
Add roasted chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes to combine flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat.
Ensure the chicken is well-charred for authentic smoky flavor.
Let the sauce simmer until the oil separates to ensure spices are fully cooked.

Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Japanese-style Mixed Rice with Beef and Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Takikomi Gohan served in a handcrafted ceramic bowl on a dark wood table. The short-grain rice is lightly tinted umami-brown, glistening with dashi. Interspersed are bright orange julienned carrots, vibrant yellow corn kernels, and tender sliced shiitake mushrooms. Five 2cm seared chicken cubes with golden-brown skin and five 2cm seared beef chunks are arranged naturally across the surface. The meat shows a moist, seared texture. A sprinkle of bright green scallion rounds and fine ginger slivers provides a fresh finish. The setting includes bamboo chopsticks on a rest and a small side of yellow pickled radish. Natural light emphasizes the steam and varied textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional Chawan (rice bowl)
Accompany with Takuan (pickled daikon radish)
Provide bamboo chopsticks on a ceramic chopstick rest
Serve with hot green tea or miso soup
instructions: Rinse rice in cold water until starch runs clear. Drain for 30 minutes.
Whisk dashi stock, soy sauce, and mirin in a bowl.
Place drained rice into a heavy-bottomed pot. Pour in the dashi mixture.
Layer sliced shiitake, julienned carrots, and corn kernels evenly over the rice.
Cover pot tightly. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 15 minutes without opening the lid.
Season chicken and beef cubes with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken in a hot pan until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Sear beef in a separate pan until browned and medium-rare.
Turn off rice heat. Let steam for 10 minutes undisturbed.
Gently fold cooked chicken and beef into the rice using a paddle.
Garnish with sliced scallions and grated ginger before serving.
notes: Do not open the lid during the steaming phase to ensure even rice texture.
Use high-quality dashi for the most authentic flavor profile.
Adjust soy sauce quantity if using low-sodium varieties.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Kung Pao Spaghetti with Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of glossy, dark-sauced spaghetti twirled in the center of a wide white porcelain bowl. Large 3cm chunks of seared chicken are nestled among the noodles, showing a golden-brown crust. Whole dried red chilies and bright green scallion batons provide vibrant color contrast. Scattered roasted peanuts add texture. The dish sits on a dark oak bistro table with a crisp white cotton napkin. A pair of sleek dark wood chopsticks and a modern stainless steel pasta fork are placed beside the bowl. Natural, even daylight highlights the silky, emulsified sauce. The entire plate is visible, maintaining balanced negative space for a professional, uncluttered presentation that honors both culinary traditions.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with both chopsticks and a pasta fork to honor the fusion heritage
Pair with a crisp, high-acidity Italian white wine or a chilled jasmine tea
Provide extra chili oil on the side for individual heat preference

ingredients.name: Chicken thigh, boneless and skinless, 3cm chunks

instructions: Whisk light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, balsamic vinegar, sugar, and cornstarch in a small bowl.
Boil spaghetti in salted water until al dente.
Reserve 100ml of pasta cooking water.
Heat peanut oil in a wok over high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from the wok and set aside.
Add dried chilies and Szechuan peppercorns to the remaining oil and fry until fragrant.
Stir in ginger and garlic for 30 seconds.
Return chicken to the wok with cooked spaghetti and reserved water.
Pour in the sauce mixture and toss vigorously over high heat to coat.
Fold in peanuts and scallion batons before serving.
notes: Balsamic vinegar provides the necessary acidity and depth similar to traditional Chinkiang black vinegar
Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding chicken to achieve a proper sear
The cornstarch in the sauce helps it cling to the smooth surface of the spaghetti

recipes.recipe_name: Ricotta Gnocchi with Fresh Tomato Sauce and Buffalo Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: A central mound of pillowy ricotta gnocchi sits in a wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl. Each gnocchi is a 2cm hand-cut cushion, lightly coated in a vibrant red sauce made from blistered cherry tomato halves and olive oil. Large, irregular chunks of stark white buffalo mozzarella are nestled between the gnocchi, showing softened, glossy edges from the residual heat. Scattered fresh basil leaves provide a bright green contrast against the warm tones of the dish. The plating is clean and organic, positioned in the center of the bowl with ample negative space. The scene is lit with soft, natural light on a light oak table, accompanied by a folded white linen napkin and a silver fork.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm ciabatta bread for scarpetta
Pair with a chilled Vermentino or a light Valpolicella
instructions: Drain ricotta in a fine-mesh sieve for 4 hours.
Mix drained ricotta, egg yolk, grated Parmigiano, salt, and nutmeg in a bowl.
Sift flour over the mixture. Fold gently until a soft dough forms. Do not overwork.
Divide dough into four pieces. Roll each piece into a 2cm thick log on a floured surface.
Cut logs into 2cm pieces. Set aside on a floured tray.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic until golden. Remove garlic.
Add cherry tomatoes to the pan. Cook for 10 minutes until they burst and soften.
Boil a large pot of salted water. Cook gnocchi in batches. Remove once they float to the surface.
Transfer cooked gnocchi directly into the tomato sauce. Toss gently to coat.
Fold in half of the basil leaves. Season with salt.
Divide gnocchi into four plates. Top with fresh buffalo mozzarella chunks and remaining basil.
notes: Drying the ricotta is essential to prevent gummy gnocchi
Use a bench scraper for clean cuts when portioning the dough
Ensure the sauce is ready before boiling the pasta as gnocchi cook very fast

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Potato and Salami Hash with Asiago
recipes.visual_description: The dish features golden-brown, roasted potato cubes and thick chunks of seared salami arranged in a centered mound on a clean white porcelain plate. Melted Asiago cheese drapes over the warm potatoes, creating a creamy texture. Quartered, pan-seared artichoke hearts are nestled into the arrangement, showing charred edges. A dark, toasted pumpernickel and parsley crumble is scattered across the top for textural contrast. The plate is finished with a light drizzle of herb oil. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table and a linen napkin. Natural light highlights the crispy surfaces of the potatoes and the richness of the cheese, emphasizing a rustic yet refined presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of spicy grain mustard
Pair with a dry white wine or a crisp pilsner
Accompany with a simple arugula salad
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and dice potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Toss potatoes with 30ml olive oil and salt.
Spread potatoes on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 25 minutes until edges brown.
Cut salami into 1.5cm thick chunks.
Drain and quarter artichoke hearts.
Pulse pumpernickel bread in a processor into coarse crumbs.
Sauté crumbs in remaining oil with minced garlic until crisp.
Add salami and artichokes to the potato tray.
Roast for 10 minutes.
Grate Asiago cheese over the mixture.
Bake for 2 minutes until cheese melts.
Top with toasted pumpernickel crumbs and chopped parsley.
notes: Use a firm salami variety like Genoa or Soppressata for better texture
Ensure potatoes are completely dry before roasting to achieve maximum crispness
The pumpernickel crumbs provide an essential earthy contrast to the salty cheese

recipes.recipe_name: Honey-Pineapple Glazed Jerk Chicken with Charred Watermelon
recipes.visual_description: A white porcelain plate sits on a dark wood table. A whole, skin-on jerk chicken thigh is the centerpiece. The skin is dark, crispy, and coated in a glossy honey-pineapple glaze. Next to the chicken are two thick, 3cm-wide wedges of charred watermelon. The watermelon shows distinct black grill marks against its vibrant red flesh. Small 1cm cubes of fresh pineapple are scattered around the chicken, glistening with glaze. A single lime wedge and a few whole cilantro leaves provide a green contrast. The lighting is natural and bright. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, not sliced. The arrangement is clean with visible negative space. Authentic Caribbean influences appear in the spice-rubbed textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of rice and peas
Provide extra lime wedges
Pair with traditional ginger beer
instructions: Rub chicken with jerk seasoning and salt.
Heat oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down.
Sear for 6 minutes until crispy.
Flip chicken.
Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and rest.
Add honey, lime juice, and pineapple to the pan.
Simmer for 3 minutes until thickened.
Sear watermelon wedges in a separate hot dry pan for 1 minute per side.
Plate chicken whole.
Spoon glaze over chicken.
Place watermelon wedges alongside.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C for safety.
Use a very hot pan for watermelon to ensure char marks without softening the fruit.
Fresh pineapple provides better acidity than canned for the glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chocolate and Camembert Mussels
recipes.visual_description: Eight authentic mussel shells are arranged naturally on a bed of coarse gray sea salt inside a shallow stone bowl. Each shell is filled with a smooth, dark chocolate and Camembert ganache, leveled to the brim. A single, glistening drop of bright red Framboise and hot sauce reduction rests in the center of each shell. Tiny flecks of vanilla bean are scattered across the surface. The presentation is earthy and coastal, using the shells as sustainable, zero-waste vessels. The background features a weathered wooden table and a simple beige linen cloth. Soft side-lighting highlights the iridescent interior of the shells and the creamy, matte texture of the ganache.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a mignardise after a seafood-heavy French meal
Present on a bed of local sea salt or cleaned beach stones
Pair with a small glass of chilled Framboise eau de vie

ingredients.name: Large Mussels (cleaned, meat reserved for other use)

instructions: Steam mussels in a small amount of water until open.
Remove meat for another preparation. Scrub shells clean and boil for 10 minutes to sterilize.
Dry shells completely.
Heat cream in a small saucepan. Scrape vanilla seeds into the cream. Add the pod.
Bring to a simmer. Remove from heat. Steep for 10 minutes. Remove pod.
Place chopped chocolate and Camembert in a bowl.
Pour hot vanilla cream over the mixture. Let sit for 2 minutes.
Whisk gently until smooth and emulsified.
Stir in 20 ml of Framboise eau de vie and a pinch of salt.
Pipe the ganache into the cleaned mussel shells. Level with a palette knife.
Chill for 1 hour until set.
Mix remaining Framboise, hot sauce, and honey in a small pan.
Simmer over low heat until reduced to a thick glaze. Cool completely.
Place a small drop of the glaze on each set ganache shell before serving.
notes: The mussel liquor from steaming can be reduced and added (5ml) to the ganache for a deeper umami profile.
Dry the vanilla pod husks, grind them into powder, and use as a zero-waste garnish.
Ensure the Camembert is at room temperature before adding cream to ensure a smooth emulsion.

recipes.recipe_name: Corn and Paneer Kofta in Makhani Gravy
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl sits on a dark wood table. Four large, golden-brown paneer and corn kofta spheres are centered in a vibrant, smooth orange-red makhani gravy. The koftas are whole, showing a slightly textured, crispy exterior. A delicate swirl of fresh white cream decorates the surface of the sauce. Scattered across the top are bright yellow charred corn kernels and fresh, emerald-green cilantro leaves. Beside the bowl, a small basket contains warm, folded butter naan with visible charred spots. A side of thin-sliced red onion rings and a lime wedge provides contrast. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the creamy texture of the sauce and the rustic textures of the bread.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with hot butter naan or garlic kulcha
Accompany with laccha onion (sliced red onion rings with lemon and chaat masala)
Traditional copper or brass serving bowls can be used for authenticity
instructions: Mash 300g paneer and 100g boiled corn kernels together.
Mix in mashed potato, cornstarch, and 5g salt.
Form the mixture into 12 equal-sized spherical balls.
Heat oil to 175°C in a deep pan.
Fry kofta balls until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towels.
Boil tomatoes and cashews in 200ml water for 12 minutes.
Blend tomato mixture into a smooth puree and strain through a fine sieve.
Melt butter in a clean pan over medium heat.
Sauté ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute.
Add tomato puree, chili powder, and garam masala. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream and the remaining 100g of whole corn kernels.
Place three koftas in each bowl and pour the hot gravy over them.
notes: Ensure the paneer is dry before mashing to prevent koftas from breaking
Do not over-mix the kofta dough or it will become dense
Straining the gravy is essential for the signature smooth makhani texture

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Crema de Elote y Poblano
recipes.visual_description: A single whole seared chicken thigh sits centered on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken skin is golden-brown and crispy. It rests on a smooth, pale yellow corn cream sauce. Dark green poblano pepper strips, cut into batons, and whole charred corn kernels are scattered throughout the sauce. Small cubes of white cheese are melting into the warm cream. The plate is garnished with fresh cilantro sprigs. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wood table. A side of warm corn tortillas in a cloth basket and a silver fork and knife are present. Natural light highlights the textures of the crispy chicken and silky sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas kept in a traditional cloth-lined basket
Accompany with a side of Mexican red rice
Provide fresh lime wedges on the table for acidity
instructions: Roast poblano peppers over an open flame until skin is charred.
Place peppers in a bowl and cover with plastic wrap for 10 minutes.
Peel, deseed, and cut peppers into batons.
Remove kernels from corn cobs using a knife.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the skillet.
Sear until skin is golden and crispy.
Flip chicken and cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and let rest.
In the same pan, sauté onion, garlic, and two-thirds of the corn kernels for 5 minutes.
Add heavy cream and simmer for 3 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to a blender and process until smooth.
Return sauce to the skillet over low heat.
Stir in the poblano batons and remaining corn kernels.
Add cheese and stir until melted and the sauce is thick.
Place a pool of sauce on each plate and top with one whole chicken thigh.
notes: Ensure the chicken skin is completely dry before searing to achieve maximum crispness.
If Queso Oaxaca is unavailable, use any high-quality melting cheese like Monterey Jack or Muenster.
The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon but still fluid.

recipes.recipe_name: Spezzatino di Manzo con Funghi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spezzatino di Manzo served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The dish features four large, tender 4cm chunks of dark, braised beef coated in a rich, deep-red tomato and red wine sauce. Thick-cut quartered cremini mushrooms and softened diced onion pieces are nestled between the beef chunks. A single sprig of fresh rosemary rests on top for garnish. The plate sits on a dark wood bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin and a piece of crusty rustic bread. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the glossy texture of the sauce and the hearty texture of the ingredients. Moderate negative space emphasizes the rich colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread for scarpetta
Pair with a medium-bodied Italian red wine
Optionally serve over soft yellow polenta
instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Brown beef chunks in batches. Remove and set aside.
Add onions to the pot. Sauté until translucent.
Add garlic and mushrooms. Cook for 5 minutes.
Deglaze the pot with red wine. Scrape up browned bits.
Stir in tomatoes, beef stock, and rosemary.
Return beef to the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 90 minutes.
Remove lid. Simmer for 15 minutes to thicken sauce.
notes: Pat beef dry before searing to ensure a deep brown crust
Use a collagen-rich cut like chuck for maximum tenderness
The sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon

recipes.recipe_name: Turkish Turkey Köfte with Sumac Onions
recipes.visual_description: Four plump, oval-shaped turkey köfte chunks are positioned centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The turkey exhibits a deep, caramelized brown crust with visible char marks from the high-heat sear. To the side, a vibrant heap of thinly sliced red onions is tossed with deep burgundy sumac and bright green parsley. A small, neat mound of golden bulgur pilaf provides a textural base. The plate features a single charred long green pepper for authentic color. The setting is a light oak bistro table with a side of thick garlic yogurt in a small clay bowl and a folded cotton napkin. Natural light emphasizes the juicy texture of the meat and the crispness of the onions.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with thick garlic yogurt or haydari
Accompany with warm pita or lavash bread
Include charred long green peppers on the side
instructions: Mix ground turkey, grated onion, garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, cumin, and pul biber.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Knead the mixture by hand for 5 minutes until sticky.
Shape into 12 thick, oval-shaped chunks.
Refrigerate chunks for 30 minutes to firm.
Toss sliced red onions with sumac, lemon juice, and half the parsley.
Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear turkey chunks for 5 minutes per side.
Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat and rest for 3 minutes.
Serve chunks topped with sumac onion salad and remaining parsley.
notes: Squeezing the juice from the grated onion prevents the meat mixture from becoming too wet.
Kneading the meat is essential for the traditional springy texture of Turkish köfte.

recipes.recipe_name: Mussel and Blue Cheese Velouté with Rose Oil and Caramelized Shallots
recipes.visual_description: A shallow, wide-rimmed bone china bowl contains a pale, ivory-colored mussel velouté. The soup has a silky, aerated texture with fine bubbles. In the center, three plump, whole steamed mussels are stacked organically, not fanned. Small, dark mahogany cubes of caramelized shallots are clustered at the base of the mussels. Droplets of vibrant pink rose oil create distinct, shimmering circles on the surface. A single, crisp dried rose petal and a tiny sprig of chervil rest atop the mussels. The arrangement is off-center with significant negative space. The bowl sits on a grey-veined white marble surface next to a polished silver spoon and a folded white linen napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of warm, crusty sourdough baguette
Pair with a crisp, chilled Chablis or Sancerre
instructions: Heat grapeseed oil and rose petals to 60°C. Steep for 30 minutes. Strain and reserve oil.
Sauté 50g shallots in 10g butter until translucent. Add white wine and mussels. Cover and steam for 4 minutes.
Remove mussels from shells. Keep whole. Strain and reserve the cooking liquid.
Melt sugar in a small saucepan until it reaches a dark amber caramel stage. Deglaze with 20ml water. Set aside.
Sauté remaining 100g shallots in 30g butter. Add the liquid caramel. Cook until shallots are dark and sticky.
Combine reserved mussel liquid, fish stock, and heavy cream. Simmer for 10 minutes to reduce.
Whisk in the Roquefort cheese until fully melted. Pass the soup through a fine chinois.
Use an immersion blender to aerate the soup until a light foam forms on the surface.
Place three whole mussels and a spoonful of caramelized shallots in the center of each bowl.
Pour the hot velouté around the mussels. Garnish with droplets of rose oil.
notes: Ensure all mussels that do not open during steaming are discarded.
Do not boil the soup after adding the blue cheese to prevent curdling.
The rose oil should be used sparingly to avoid overpowering the mussels.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Braised Short Ribs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Galbi-jjim served in a deep, dark matte stoneware bowl. The focus is on large, thick chunks of braised beef short ribs, mahogany in color and glistening with a thick, savory glaze. The meat is presented whole on the bone, never sliced. Interspersed with the beef are large cubes of tender daikon radish and carrots with softened edges, alongside whole rehydrated shiitake mushrooms. The sauce is rich and dark, coating each element. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds and thinly sliced green onions. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wood table, featuring a stainless steel rice bowl and traditional long metal chopsticks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a bowl of steamed short-grain white rice
Accompany with napa cabbage kimchi
Include various small banchan side dishes
Use traditional Korean metal chopsticks and a long-handled spoon

ingredients.name: Beef short ribs, cut into 5cm chunks

instructions: Soak beef ribs in cold water for 30 minutes to remove excess blood.
Drain and rinse the ribs.
Blanch ribs in boiling water for 5 minutes.
Drain and wash ribs under cold running water.
Mix soy sauce, water, grated pear, sugar, mirin, garlic, and ginger in a bowl.
Place ribs and sauce in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Simmer on low heat for 60 minutes with the lid on.
Add radish, carrots, and mushrooms to the pot.
Simmer for 30 minutes until meat is tender and pulling away from the bone.
Remove lid and increase heat to reduce sauce until glossy.
Stir in sesame oil.
Garnish with sesame seeds and green onions.

The Korean pear acts as a natural meat tenderizer.
Ensure the sauce reduces enough to coat the back of a spoon.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Torta di Riso e Ortaggi Dolce
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of a multi-layered entremet stands on a white porcelain plate with gold trim. The slice reveals a base of smooth potato sponge, a thin layer of crimson tomato gelée, and a thick Arborio rice mousse. The exterior features a vibrant, glossy carrot mirror glaze. A small, architectural nest of honey-crisped capellini noodles sits on top. One dot of black garlic caramel and a thin line of red onion agrodolce syrup accent the plate. The setting is a white marble surface with a folded white linen napkin. Professional lighting creates soft, elegant shadows, emphasizing the textures. The composition uses wide negative space for a sophisticated, modern Italian patisserie aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a glass of chilled Vin Santo
Accompany with a ristretto espresso
Present on a silver tiered patisserie stand
instructions: Simmer rice in milk with vanilla and 50g sugar until very soft.
Cool rice and blend until smooth.
Fold whipped cream into rice mixture to create a mousse.
Whisk eggs with 50g sugar until pale.
Fold potato flour into eggs and bake at 180°C for 15 minutes.
Simmer peeled tomatoes with 20g sugar until thick.
Blend and strain tomatoes to create a smooth gelée.
Juice carrots and reduce by half with remaining sugar.
Bloom gelatin and stir into warm carrot juice for the glaze.
Fry capellini in honey until golden and crisp.
Reduce red onion juice with sugar to a thick agrodolce syrup.
Layer potato sponge, tomato gelée, and rice mousse in molds.
Freeze entremet until firm.
Pour carrot glaze over frozen cake at 32°C.
Garnish with capellini nest and black garlic caramel.
notes: Pass the potato flour through a fine sieve for a lighter sponge
Ensure the rice is fully hydrated before blending to avoid graininess
The carrot glaze must be applied at exactly 32°C for a perfect mirror finish

recipes.recipe_name: Aloo Matar Chicken Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served in a traditional hammered copper karahi bowl placed on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features large, tender chunks of moist chicken and 3cm golden potato cubes coated in a thick, vibrant reddish-brown gravy. Bright green peas are scattered throughout, providing pops of color and texture. The sauce shows a slight sheen from the tempered spices. The plate is garnished with a sprinkle of freshly chopped green cilantro. Beside the bowl sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan and a small ceramic dish of mango chutney. The setting is a modern bistro with a dark wood table and a cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or steamed basmati rice.
Include a side of cucumber raita to balance the heat.
Offer lime wedges and sliced red onions on the side.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, cut into 4cm chunks
potatoes, peeled and cut into 3cm cubes

instructions: Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Add cumin seeds and fry until they sizzle.
Add diced onions. Sauté until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides.
Reduce heat to medium. Add turmeric, chili powder, and coriander powder.
Pour in tomato puree. Cook for 5 minutes until oil separates from the masala.
Add potato cubes and water. Stir to combine.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add green peas. Cook for 5 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Stir in garam masala. Garnish with chopped cilantro.
notes: Ensure onions are properly browned to develop the base flavor.
Do not overcook the potatoes to maintain their cubed shape.
Always check the thickest piece of chicken for the safe 75°C internal temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Beef and Bean Stew with Rice
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic matte-black ceramic bowl sits on a dark walnut table. On one side, a mound of fluffy, steamed white long-grain rice provides a clean base. Next to it, the rich, dark-red beef stew features large, 3cm tender chunks of seared beef coated in a thick tomato-based sauce. Visible 1cm diced red and green bell peppers and quartered earthy mushrooms are interspersed with plump black beans. The dish is garnished with a sprig of fresh oregano and three rounds of pickled jalapeno. A single portion is shown with a heavy silver spoon resting on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural light highlights the glossy sauce and the texture of the unsliced meat.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side
Accompany with a side of fresh lime wedges
Traditional pairing with a cold hibiscus tea (Agua de Jamaica)
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm cubes and season with salt.
Dice onion and bell peppers into 1cm squares.
Quarter the mushrooms and mince the garlic.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef.
Sauté onion, bell peppers, and mushrooms in the same pot for 5 minutes.
Add garlic, oregano, and chopped pickled jalapenos. Cook 1 minute.
Return beef to the pot. Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef stock.
Simmer on low heat for 90 minutes until beef is tender.
Stir in beans and heat through for 5 minutes.
Boil rice in salted water until tender. Drain well.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper before serving.
notes: Do not slice the beef chunks before serving; they must remain whole for authenticity.
Ensure the sauce has thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon.
For extra heat, add 10ml of the jalapeno pickling liquid to the stew.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Mole Poblano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Mole Poblano served on a clean white porcelain plate. The centerpiece is a whole, bone-in chicken thigh completely coated in a thick, velvety, dark reddish-brown mole sauce. The sauce appears glossy and rich with visible texture from ground seeds and spices. Toasted white sesame seeds are sprinkled evenly over the chicken. Three small sprigs of fresh cilantro and four thin rings of raw red onion provide a vibrant color contrast. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy Mexican red rice is positioned. The background features a rustic wooden table with a small basket of warm corn tortillas wrapped in a colorful woven cloth and a simple cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas served in a traditional cloth-lined basket
Mexican red rice (arroz rojo)
Refried beans topped with crumbled queso fresco
instructions: Remove stems and seeds from all dried chilies.
Toast chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Place toasted chilies in a bowl of hot water and soak for 20 minutes.
Toast almonds, 15g of sesame seeds, and the cinnamon stick in a dry pan until golden.
Char the tomatoes, onion, and garlic in a dry pan until blackened in spots.
Drain chilies and place in a blender with toasted nuts, spices, and charred vegetables.
Add 100ml of chicken stock and blend until a smooth paste forms.
Heat oil in a large pot. Add the mole paste and fry for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in the remaining chicken stock and chopped dark chocolate. Simmer on low heat.
Season chicken thighs with salt. Sear in a separate pan until the skin is golden brown.
Transfer chicken to the mole sauce. Simmer until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Adjust seasoning with salt if necessary.
notes: Do not burn the chilies during toasting or the sauce will become bitter.
The mole sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C at the bone.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Caramelized Onion Crostini
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single, thick-cut baguette slice toasted to a golden brown. A generous mound of dark, jammy caramelized onions sits atop the bread. Resting on the onions are three distinct, seared beef cubes, approximately 2cm in size. The beef shows a dark brown crust with visible salt flakes and a moist texture. A single fresh thyme sprig is placed casually over the beef. The crostini is centered on a small, off-white ceramic plate with a slightly uneven rim. The background is a dark wood tabletop. A linen napkin lies to the side. The lighting is warm and directional, highlighting the glisten of the onions and the texture of the beef. No fanning or geometric patterns are used.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on a wooden board for a rustic communal feel
Pair with a glass of light-bodied red wine
Offer as an 'amuse-bouche' or early evening snack
instructions: Slice the baguette into 12 rounds, each 2 cm thick.
Brush bread with 15 ml olive oil. Toast in oven at 180°C until golden.
Peel and thinly slice the onions into half-moons.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium-low heat. Add onions and a pinch of salt.
Cook onions for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deep brown and soft.
Stir in balsamic vinegar. Cook for 2 minutes. Remove from heat.
Cut the beef into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining olive oil in a pan over high heat.
Sear beef cubes for 2 minutes, turning to brown all sides. Keep the center medium-rare.
Spread a spoonful of onions onto each toasted baguette slice.
Place 2 to 3 beef cubes on top of the onions.
Garnish with fresh thyme leaves.
notes: Ensure the pan is very hot before adding beef to achieve a good sear without overcooking the center.
Do not rush the onions; low heat is essential for deep flavor development.

recipes.recipe_name: Carbonnade Flamande
recipes.visual_description: A deep brown, glossy beef stew served in a wide, white porcelain bowl. The dish features large, 4cm tender chunks of braised beef coated in a thick, rich sauce made with dark Belgian ale. Soft, caramelized onion strands are visible throughout the sauce. The stew is positioned centrally with moderate negative space around the edges. A small cluster of fresh parsley and a sprig of thyme garnish the top. The stew sits on a dark wooden bistro table. Beside the bowl is a small side plate with thick-cut, golden-brown Belgian fries and a small ramekin of mayonnaise. A glass of dark abbey ale stands in the background. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the meat and the sheen of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Thick-cut Belgian fries
Fresh mayonnaise
Chilled Belgian Abbey Ale
Steamed green beans
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4cm chunks.
Pat meat dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned. Remove beef.
Add butter and sliced onions to the pot.
Sauté onions over medium heat until dark golden brown.
Stir in brown sugar and vinegar. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return beef and accumulated juices to the pot.
Pour in beer and beef stock. Add thyme and bay leaves.
Spread mustard onto sourdough slices. Place mustard-side down on the liquid.
Cover pot. Simmer on low heat for 2.5 hours.
Stir the dissolved bread into the sauce to thicken.
Season to taste. Remove bay leaves and thyme stems.
notes: Use a high-quality Belgian Dubbel for the best flavor profile.
Do not rush the onion caramelization; it provides the base color.
Ensure the beef is fork-tender before removing from heat.

Accompany with crusty bread
Pair with a robust Xinomavro red wine

Shape into small oval logs. Heat oil in a pan. Brown meat logs on all sides. Remove. Sauté remaining garlic and tomato paste in the same pan. Add passata and a splash of wine. Simmer for 10 minutes. Add meat logs to sauce. Simmer for 15 minutes until sauce thickens. Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Use high-quality cumin for authentic flavor
Chilling the meat helps the shapes hold during browning

recipes.recipe_name: Kadai Paneer
recipes.visual_description: The Kadai Paneer is presented in a traditional hammered copper serving bowl with brass handles. The dish features large 3cm cubes of firm paneer nestled in a thick, vibrant orange-red gravy. Visible textures include 2cm squares of charred green and red bell peppers and translucent onion petals. The sauce is glossy and speckled with coarse-ground spices. Top the dish with a fine nest of fresh ginger julienne and bright green coriander leaves. The bowl sits on a rustic dark wood surface. A side of charred garlic naan is stacked in a small wicker basket. A stainless steel condiment dish containing pickled red onion rings and a lime wedge provides a clean color contrast. Lighting is natural and highlights the rich, semi-dry consistency of the curry.

Accompany with laccha onion (onion rings with lemon and chaat masala)

instructions: Dry roast coriander seeds, cumin, dried chilies, and peppercorns until fragrant.
Grind spices into a coarse powder to make Kadai Masala.
Cut paneer into 3cm cubes.
Dice onions and bell peppers into 2cm squares.
Puree tomatoes until smooth.
Heat 15ml oil in a heavy pan.
Sauté bell peppers and onion petals for 2 minutes until slightly charred. Remove.
Heat remaining oil. Add ginger-garlic paste. Sauté 1 minute.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, and chili powder. Cook until oil separates from the masala.
Stir in the ground Kadai Masala.
Add paneer cubes and sautéed vegetables. Mix gently to coat.
Crush kasuri methi between palms and sprinkle over the dish.
Simmer for 3 minutes on low heat.
Garnish with chopped fresh coriander and ginger julienne.

recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain plate in a modern bistro setting. Three golden-brown, deep-fried conchiglioni pasta shells serve as the base, each filled with a generous dollop of whipped, creamy white ricotta. Small, vibrant red droplets of sun-dried tomato jam are placed around the shells. Tiny, emerald-green candied broccoli rabe florets and dark, glistening crumbles of caramelized sausage praline are scattered over the ricotta for texture. A light dusting of powdered sugar coats the pasta. The arrangement is organic and centered, leaving ample negative space. Natural light highlights the contrast between the crispy pasta ridges and the smooth cheese, with a cotton napkin and a small dessert spoon nearby.

Present as a contemporary take on Sicilian cannoli flavors
instructions: Boil pasta in water with 20g sugar until al dente.
Drain pasta and pat completely dry.
Simmer sun-dried tomatoes in 100ml water and 50g sugar for 15 minutes.
Puree tomatoes into a smooth jam and cool.
Fry sausage meat in a pan until rendered and crisp.
Add brown sugar to sausage and cook until caramelized and dark.
Drain sausage on paper towels to harden into a crumble.
Blanch broccoli rabe florets for 1 minute, then toss in remaining sugar.
Heat oil to 180°C and fry pasta shells until golden and crispy.
Whisk ricotta with honey and lemon zest until smooth.
Pipe ricotta into fried pasta shells.
Top with sausage crumble, candied rabe, and dots of tomato jam.
notes: Ensure pasta is completely dry before frying to prevent oil splatter.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Broccoli with Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chinese-style beef and broccoli served on a clean white porcelain plate. The focal point is the 3cm seared beef chunks, coated in a dark, glossy savory glaze. Accompanying the beef are vibrant green blanched broccoli florets and golden-brown halved shiitake mushrooms. A neat, small mound of steamed white jasmine rice is positioned to the side. The arrangement is natural and flowing with moderate negative space. The dish is garnished with fine slivers of green onion. The setting is a dark wood bistro table with dark wood chopsticks and a ceramic spoon on a white cotton napkin. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the glazed meat and fresh vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of chili oil or soy-marinated bird's eye chilies
Traditional ceramic tea cup with jasmine tea
Small side dish of pickled daikon radish
instructions: Rinse rice until water runs clear.
Cook rice in 600ml water until tender.
Toss beef chunks with cornstarch and 15ml soy sauce.
Marinate beef for 15 minutes.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling water for 2 minutes.
Drain and shock broccoli in ice water.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Sear beef chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 63°C.
Remove beef and set aside.
Stir-fry mushrooms until golden and tender.
Add ginger and garlic to the wok.
Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return beef and broccoli to the wok.
Stir in oyster sauce and remaining soy sauce.
Toss everything for 1 minute to glaze.
Drizzle with sesame oil.
Serve immediately over jasmine rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding beef to achieve wok hei
Do not overcrowd the pan to ensure chunks sear rather than steam
Velveting with cornstarch ensures the beef remains tender during high-heat cooking

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Beef and Chicken Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single portion of wide paccheri pasta tubes tossed in a vibrant, glossy tomato sauce. The pasta is centered in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Hearty 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin and golden-brown chicken thigh pieces are nestled naturally among the pasta tubes, never sliced or fanned. The sauce is thick and clings to the pasta, accented by visible slices of garlic. Fresh green basil leaves are torn and scattered over the top for color contrast. Pair with a light-bodied Mediterranean red wine
Provide a small bowl of freshly grated Pecorino Romano cheese

Cut beef and chicken into 3cm chunks.
Season all meat with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks for 4 minutes until browned. Remove from pan.

Drain pasta, reserving 100ml of cooking water.

Add reserved pasta water. Toss over high heat for 2 minutes until sauce coats the pasta.
