recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado with Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate in a modern bistro setting. The dish features 3cm cubes of seared beef tenderloin with a dark, glossy glaze, mixed with thick wedges of red onion and deseeded tomato. Halved cremini mushrooms are interspersed throughout, showing a golden-brown sear. The stir-fry is piled over hand-cut, thick golden potato batons. Vibrant green cilantro leaves are scattered as a garnish. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the textures of the charred vegetables and succulent meat. A cotton napkin and polished flatware sit beside the plate on a light wooden table. The arrangement is organic and professional.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of steamed long-grain white rice
Pair with a glass of Chicha Morada or a Pisco Sour
instructions: Cut potatoes into 1cm thick batons.
Soak potato batons in cold water for 20 minutes.
Drain and pat potatoes completely dry.
Heat vegetable oil to 180°C in a heavy pot.
Fry potatoes until golden and crisp.
Drain potatoes on paper towels and season with salt.
Cut beef into 3cm cubes.
Slice onions into 1cm thick wedges.
Cut tomatoes into 2cm thick wedges and remove seeds.
Halve the cremini mushrooms.
Heat 30ml oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef cubes in batches until browned.
Remove beef and set aside.
Add mushrooms and onions to the wok.
Sauté for 2 minutes until slightly softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and vinegar.
Add tomato wedges and toss for 1 minute.
Arrange fried potatoes on plates and top with beef mixture.
Garnish with chopped cilantro.
notes: Use a very high heat to achieve the traditional wok-char flavor
Ensure potatoes are dry before frying for maximum crispness

recipes.recipe_name: Rigatoni with Roasted Bell Pepper and Fresh Mozzarella
recipes.visual_description: The dish features rigatoni pasta coated in a vibrant, thick orange-red sauce made from roasted peppers and tomatoes. It is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Large 3 cm chunks of creamy white fresh mozzarella are nestled among the pasta tubes, slightly softened by the heat. The pasta is garnished with whole, bright green basil leaves and a dusting of fine parmesan. Visible 2 cm squares of roasted red pepper add texture. The arrangement is organic and centered, leaving a clean white rim. The setting is a rustic wooden bistro table with a neutral linen napkin and a small bowl of extra grated parmesan on the side. Natural light highlights the glossy texture of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a dry Italian red wine like Chianti
Offer extra virgin olive oil for drizzling at the table
instructions: Char bell peppers over an open flame or under a broiler until skin is black.
Place peppers in a bowl and cover with plastic wrap for 10 minutes.
Peel the charred skin off the peppers and remove seeds.
Dice two peppers into 2 cm squares.
Puree the remaining pepper with 15 ml of olive oil until smooth.
Sauté garlic in remaining olive oil in a large pan over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, oregano, salt, and pepper to the pan.
Simmer sauce for 15 minutes while breaking up tomatoes with a spoon.
Stir the pepper puree and diced peppers into the tomato sauce.
Boil rigatoni in salted water until 2 minutes before al dente.
Drain pasta and reserve 100 ml of pasta water.
Add pasta and reserved water to the sauce pan.
Toss over high heat until sauce coats the pasta.
Stir in half of the parmesan cheese.
Tear mozzarella into 3 cm chunks.
Top pasta with mozzarella chunks and fresh basil before serving.
notes: Ensure pasta is undercooked before adding to sauce to prevent overcooking.
Use high-quality buffalo mozzarella for a creamier texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Celery Hearts with Roasted Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion served on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole bone-in chicken thighs with crispy, deep-golden skin are placed atop a base of thick 10cm celery batons. The celery is tender and pale green, glistening with a translucent, amber-colored sauce. Small 1cm cubes of browned pancetta and fresh thyme leaves are scattered naturally over the meat. The sauce is glossy and pooled slightly around the celery. The plate features moderate negative space. The setting is a dark wood bistro table with a folded white cotton napkin and a silver fork. Lighting is natural and soft from the side, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and braised vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette to soak up the braising liquid
Pair with a dry white Burgundy or Chardonnay
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden. Flip and cook for 2 minutes. Remove from pan.
Add diced pancetta to the same pan. Fry until fat renders and bits are crisp.
Add celery batons to the pan. Sauté for 4 minutes until slightly softened.
Add smashed garlic and thyme sprigs. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in white wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to release browned bits. Reduce liquid by half.
Add chicken stock. Return chicken to the pan, skin-side up.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken and celery to a warm plate.
Increase heat to high. Boil liquid for 5 minutes to reduce. Whisk in cold butter to emulsify.
Strain sauce over the chicken and celery. Garnish with lemon zest.
notes: Use only the inner hearts of the celery for the most tender texture.
Ensure the chicken skin remains above the liquid level during braising to stay crisp.

recipes.recipe_name: Spinach and Ricotta Gnudi
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of seven vibrant green, 3cm round gnudi dumplings arranged naturally in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl. The dumplings have a rustic, slightly textured surface showing finely chopped spinach. They are coated in a glossy, translucent melted butter sauce. Three dark green, crisp-fried sage leaves are scattered on top. A light dusting of finely grated white Parmigiano-Reggiano covers the dish. The bowl sits on a dark, well-worn wooden table. Beside the bowl is a simple silver fork and a rustic linen napkin. The lighting is warm and soft, coming from the side to highlight the soft texture of the dumplings and the sheen of the butter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a 'primo' course before a meat dish or as a light main.
Pair with a crisp Italian white wine like Vernaccia.
Provide extra grated Parmigiano-Reggiano on the table.
instructions: Boil spinach in salted water for 2 minutes.
Drain and rinse with cold water.
Squeeze spinach tightly to remove all liquid.
Chop spinach very finely.
Mix spinach, ricotta, egg, and 75g of parmesan in a bowl.
Add nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
Fold in 60g of flour until a soft dough forms.
Shape dough into 3cm round balls.
Roll balls lightly in remaining flour.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add sage leaves and fry until crisp.
Boil gnudi in salted water until they float to the surface.
Transfer gnudi directly to the butter sauce.
Toss gently for 1 minute.
Serve immediately with remaining parmesan.
notes: Squeezing the spinach dry is the most important step for texture.
Do not overwork the dough or the gnudi will become heavy.
The name 'gnudi' means 'naked' in Italian, referring to ravioli filling without the pasta shell.

recipes.recipe_name: Espresso-Chili Braised Chicken with Arroz Rojo
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents two whole, mahogany-colored braised chicken thighs resting on a generous bed of Arroz Rojo. The chicken skin is deeply stained by the espresso-chili glaze, appearing rich and glossy. The rice is a vibrant orange-red, with visible grains and small pieces of softened tomato distributed throughout. A thick, dark sauce pools slightly at the base of the chicken. The arrangement is clean, centered on a wide, white matte porcelain plate, leaving ample negative space at the edges. A cluster of bright green cilantro and a sharp lime wedge provide a color contrast. The setting includes a dark wood table, a side of warm corn tortillas, and natural side-lighting that emphasizes the sauce's sheen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas wrapped in a cloth napkin.
Accompany with a side of pickled red onions.
Provide extra lime wedges for squeezing over the rich sauce.
instructions: Toast ancho chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Soak toasted chilies in hot water for 10 minutes until soft.
Blend rehydrated chilies, espresso, and 200g of crushed tomatoes until smooth.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden. Flip and sear 2 minutes. Remove chicken.
Sauté half the onion and half the garlic in the same pot for 3 minutes.
Add cumin and oregano. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the blended espresso-chili sauce and 100ml chicken stock.
Return chicken to the pot. Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
In a separate pot, heat remaining oil. Fry rice for 5 minutes until opaque and golden.
Add remaining onion and garlic. Cook for 2 minutes.
Stir in remaining 200g crushed tomatoes and 650ml chicken stock.
Cover rice and simmer on low heat for 18 minutes. Remove from heat and let stand for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork and serve with whole chicken thighs and braising sauce.
notes: Ensure the rice is toasted until it smells nutty before adding liquid to prevent mushiness.
The espresso adds a savory depth similar to Mexican chocolate in a mole sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Spiced Pork Tagine with Fluffy Couscous
recipes.visual_description: Present a single portion in a shallow, wide terracotta bowl. A mound of golden, fluffy couscous sits at the center. Top with three large, tender chunks of braised pork shoulder. The meat shows a deep mahogany sear and succulent texture. Surround the pork with thick 3cm squares of vibrant roasted red and yellow bell peppers. Spoon a rich, thick tomato-based sauce over the meat, highlighting the aromatic orange oil. Garnish with thin julienne strips of yellow preserved lemon and a scattering of bright green chopped cilantro. The setting features a dark wooden table, a folded white linen napkin, and a small side dish of harissa. Use natural, soft side-lighting to emphasize the textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of spicy harissa paste
Accompany with hot Moroccan mint tea
Provide crusty khobz bread for dipping into the sauce
instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chunks until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside.
Add onion to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes until soft.
Add garlic and Ras el Hanout. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return pork to the pot. Add tomatoes and vegetable stock.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add bell pepper squares. Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until pork is tender.
Place couscous in a heatproof bowl. Pour 300ml boiling salted water over it.
Cover bowl. Let stand for 5 minutes.
Fluff couscous with a fork. Incorporate a drizzle of olive oil.
Divide couscous among plates. Top with pork chunks, peppers, and sauce.
Garnish with preserved lemon and cilantro.
notes: Though pork is not traditional in Morocco, the spices and slow-braising technique provide an authentic flavor profile.
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Use a heavy cast iron pot or ceramic tagine for even heat distribution.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Basil Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Thai Basil Chicken served on a simple white ceramic plate. A mound of fluffy, steamed white Jasmine rice sits on the left side. To the right, a generous heap of stir-fry features golden-brown chicken chunks, vibrant green broccoli florets, and translucent onion wedges. The chicken is presented as natural 1cm cubes. Deep green, wilted basil leaves are interspersed throughout the glossy, umami-rich sauce coating the ingredients. The plate rests on a dark wooden table. A pair of wooden chopsticks and a traditional flat-bottomed ceramic spoon are placed on a rest. A small side dish of chili-infused fish sauce sits in the background under warm, natural kitchen lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with sliced bird's eye chilies)
Provide a flat-bottomed ceramic spoon and a fork for traditional Thai dining
Top with a crispy fried egg for additional protein and authenticity
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice until water runs clear.
Combine rice and 450ml water in a pot. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Steam broccoli florets for 4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Heat oil in a wok or large pan over high heat.
Add onion wedges and minced garlic. Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add chicken chunks to the pan. Sear until browned.
Continue cooking chicken until it reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Stir in soy sauce, oyster sauce, and fish sauce.
Add steamed broccoli to the pan. Toss to coat in sauce.
Remove pan from heat. Fold in fresh basil leaves until wilted.
Serve chicken mixture immediately over hot jasmine rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding chicken for best flavor.
Holy basil is the traditional choice, but Thai basil is a great substitute.
Do not overcook the basil; it should only just wilt to maintain its aroma.

recipes.recipe_name: Poached Chicken with Clarified Tomato Consommé
recipes.visual_description: A single, pristine cylinder of poached chicken breast stands vertically in the center of a wide-rimmed, white porcelain bowl. The chicken is pale ivory and moist. Surrounding the base is a shallow pool of crystal-clear, pale-gold tomato consommé. Three vibrant green droplets of basil oil float on the surface of the liquid, creating a sharp color contrast. The arrangement is minimalist and architectural, utilizing significant negative space. The lighting is focused and professional, casting soft shadows that emphasize the clarity of the broth and the smooth texture of the meat. The bowl sits on a dark grey travertine surface next to a precisely folded white linen napkin and a polished silver spoon.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an opening course in a multi-course tasting menu
Pair with a chilled, dry Chablis
Present with a silver bouillon spoon
instructions: Blend tomatoes with 5g salt into a coarse puree.
Place puree in a cheesecloth-lined sieve over a bowl.
Refrigerate for 12 hours to collect clear tomato water.
Blanch basil in boiling water for 10 seconds, then shock in ice water.
Blend basil with olive oil until smooth, then strain through a fine mesh.
Season chicken with remaining salt and white pepper.
Roll chicken tightly in plastic wrap to form a uniform cylinder.
Poach chicken in 75°C water until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from wrap and cut into four 4cm-thick cylinders.
Heat tomato water gently to 60°C without boiling.
Place one chicken cylinder in the center of each shallow bowl.
Pour the warm tomato consommé around the base of the chicken.
Garnish with three drops of basil oil.
notes: Do not boil the tomato water or it will lose its clarity.
Ensure the plastic wrap is food-grade and heat-stable for poaching.
The chicken must reach exactly 75°C for safety and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Lamb and White Bean Cassoulet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lamb and White Bean Cassoulet is served in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The dish features 4cm chunks of tender, braised lamb shoulder and 3cm thick chunks of garlic sausage nestled among creamy, whole haricot beans. A rich, dark amber sauce coats the ingredients. The top is covered in a crisp, golden-brown gratiné layer of toasted breadcrumbs. Freshly chopped green parsley is scattered across the surface. The bowl sits on a light oak bistro table next to a folded white cotton napkin. A side of crusty baguette pieces rests in a small basket. The lighting is soft and natural from the side, highlighting the textures of the meat and the crunchy crust.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty baguette to soak up the braising liquid
Pair with a glass of robust red wine from the Languedoc region
Include a simple green salad with a sharp vinaigrette to balance the richness

ingredients.name: dried haricot beans, soaked overnight and drained
garlic sausage, cut into 3cm thick chunks

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Heat oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat.
Sear lamb chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove lamb.
Brown sausage chunks in the same pot. Remove sausage.
Add onion and carrot to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Return lamb and sausage to the pot.
Add soaked beans, lamb stock, thyme, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Cover with a lid.
Transfer pot to the oven. Braise for 90 minutes.
Remove lid. Season with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle breadcrumbs evenly over the top.
Increase oven temperature to 200°C.
Bake uncovered for 15 minutes until the crust is golden-brown.
Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure beans are fully submerged in liquid during the braising process
If the sauce is too thin after braising, simmer on the stovetop for 5 minutes before adding breadcrumbs
Toulouse sausage is the most authentic choice for this regional dish

recipes.recipe_name: Apple and Pear Mostarda with Walnut Frangipane
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown walnut frangipane cake sits centrally on a handcrafted cream ceramic plate with subtle organic speckles. The cake is topped with a glistening mound of translucent, 1cm cubes of poached apple and pear, coated in a pale gold mustard syrup. Tiny yellow mustard seeds are distributed naturally throughout the fruit topping. Three whole toasted walnut halves are placed organically on top for height. The plate rests on a dark, textured reclaimed wood table. A beige undyed linen napkin lies loosely to the side. Soft natural side lighting emphasizes the moist crumb of the cake and the crystalline clarity of the preserved fruit. The background remains a clean, minimalist neutral stone.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve at room temperature with a small glass of Vin Santo
Traditionally enjoyed as a digestive-aiding sweet at the end of a meal
Present on locally crafted stoneware to honor regional artisanal traditions
instructions: Peel and core apples and pears. Reserve all skins and cores.
Boil reserved scraps in 200ml water for 15 minutes to extract pectin.
Strain liquid through a fine sieve into a clean saucepan. Discard solids.
Dice fruit flesh into 1cm cubes.
Add fruit cubes, honey, mustard seeds, and lemon juice to the strained liquid.
Simmer over medium heat until liquid reduces to a thick, syrupy glaze and fruit is translucent.
Toast walnuts at 160°C for 8 minutes.
Process 80g of walnuts into a fine meal. Reserve the remaining 20g as whole halves.
Beat softened butter with walnut meal, egg, and salt until smooth.
Divide walnut mixture into four 8cm greased tart molds.
Bake at 180°C for 15 minutes until golden and firm.
Top each warm walnut cake with a generous spoonful of fruit mostarda.
notes: Using the peels and cores creates a natural jelly without commercial pectin
The mustard seeds provide a subtle heat that balances the natural sugars of the fruit
For a deeper flavor, allow the fruit mostarda to sit for 24 hours before serving

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Beef and Mushroom Goulash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Hungarian Beef Goulash served in a deep, wide white porcelain bowl. The dish features large 3cm tender chunks of braised beef coated in a rich, deep mahogany-red sauce. Visible within the stew are glossy halved cremini mushrooms and softened bits of tomato and onion. The sauce has a velvety, thick consistency. Beside the stew, a neat mound of small buttered egg noodles provides a pale contrast. A dollop of thick white sour cream sits off-center, topped with a sprig of fresh flat-leaf parsley. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the moist texture of the meat and the sheen of the paprika-infused oil. The setting includes a dark wood surface and a simple cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with nokedli (Hungarian egg dumplings)
Accompany with fermented pickles or a cucumber salad
Pair with a glass of Kadarka or Egri Bikavér red wine
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add diced onions. Sauté until translucent and soft.
Stir in minced garlic and caraway seeds. Cook for 1 minute.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in paprika to prevent burning.
Add beef chunks. Return to heat. Brown meat on all sides.
Add diced tomatoes and halved mushrooms to the pot.
Pour in beef stock until meat is just submerged.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until sauce thickens to a velvety consistency.
notes: Do not brown the onions too quickly; slow cooking develops the necessary sweetness.
Always remove the pot from heat before adding paprika to avoid bitterness.
Substitute beef chuck with shin or brisket for more gelatinous texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Caribbean Green Banana Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Savory Green Banana Curry is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a light oak table. The dish features thick, firm 3 cm chunks of green banana simmered until tender, coated in a rich, vibrant yellow-orange coconut curry sauce. Large 2 cm squares of red bell pepper and softened red onion wedges are scattered throughout, providing pops of crimson and deep purple. A small mound of fluffy white long-grain rice sits to one side, partially immersed in the sauce. The arrangement is organic and professional. Garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and a lime wedge. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy sauce texture. A neutral cotton napkin and silver spoon rest beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of white long-grain rice
Accompany with fried plantains
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity
instructions: Peel the green bananas and cut into 3 cm thick chunks.
Dice the red onions and red bell peppers into 2 cm squares.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add onions and bell peppers to the pan. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic, grated ginger, curry powder, and dried thyme. Toast for 1 minute.
Add the green banana chunks to the pan. Stir to coat thoroughly with the spice mixture.
Pour in the coconut milk. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20 minutes until bananas are fork-tender.
Remove from heat. Stir in the lime juice and sea salt.
Garnish with fresh cilantro before serving.
notes: Use strictly green, unripe bananas for a starchy, savory texture similar to potatoes.
Do not overcook the bananas or they will become mushy.

recipes.recipe_name: Carne con Chile Rojo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Carne con Chile Rojo served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The dish features 3cm chunks of tender, slow-braised beef coated in a glossy, deep crimson chili and tomato sauce. The beef chunks are piled naturally in the center, never sliced or fanned. Garnish with a sprinkle of finely diced white onion and fresh cilantro leaves. A bright green lime wedge sits on the rim. The bowl is placed on a dark wood bistro table. Beside it, a small basket contains warm, folded corn tortillas wrapped in a white cloth. Natural side lighting highlights the rich texture of the sauce and the fibrous grain of the beef chunks. Minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas
Accompany with a side of Mexican red rice
Provide extra lime wedges for acidity

ingredients.name: Dried Guajillo chilies, stemmed and seeded

instructions: Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown beef in batches. Remove and set aside.
Toast dried chilies in a dry pan for 2 minutes until fragrant. Soak in hot water for 10 minutes.
Char tomatoes and unpeeled garlic in the same dry pan until skins blacken. Peel the garlic.
Blend soaked chilies, charred tomatoes, peeled garlic, and cumin until smooth.
Sauté half the diced onion in the pot until translucent.
Add the blended sauce and beef back to the pot. Pour in beef stock.
Simmer covered over low heat for 90 minutes until beef is tender.
Remove lid and simmer for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper before serving.
notes: Ensure beef is browned in small batches to maintain high heat and prevent steaming.
Strain the blended sauce through a fine-mesh sieve for a smoother restaurant-quality texture.
Use a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven to ensure even heat distribution during the long braise.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef with Basil Pesto and Parmesan
recipes.visual_description: Four thick rectangular chunks of seared beef sirloin are arranged centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The beef features a dark, caramelized crust and a juicy pink interior. A generous spoonful of textured, bright green basil pesto rests atop the beef chunks. Translucent, wide shavings of Parmesan cheese are draped over the pesto. The arrangement is organic, leaving significant white space around the edges. Two small whole basil leaves provide a fresh garnish. The setting is a modern bistro with a light oak table and a folded white cotton napkin. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the glistening oil and the coarse texture of the pesto and salt.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread
Accompany with a simple rocket salad
Pair with a medium-bodied red wine like Chianti
instructions: Toast pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat until golden.
Grate 40g of Parmesan cheese.
Shave the remaining 40g of Parmesan into thin ribbons.
Pulse basil, toasted nuts, garlic, and grated Parmesan in a food processor.
Slowly drizzle in 80ml of olive oil while pulsing to create a coarse pesto.
Season beef steaks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining oil in a heavy cast-iron skillet over high heat.
Sear beef for 4 minutes per side until a dark crust forms.
Remove beef from pan and rest for 8 minutes.
Cut beef into thick rectangular chunks.
Place beef chunks on plates and top with pesto and Parmesan shavings.
notes: Ensure the pan is smoking hot before adding the beef to achieve a proper crust.
Resting the meat is essential to retain internal juices.
Do not over-process the pesto; it should have a visible coarse texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Bell Pepper Stir-fry with Black Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the stir-fry is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The focal point is the glossy beef chunks, seared dark brown and coated in a rich, translucent savory sauce. Interspersed are vibrant 3cm squares of red and green bell peppers, translucent onion wedges, and plump halved shiitake mushrooms. Small specks of black fermented beans are visible, clinging to the ingredients. The arrangement is natural and free-flowing, showing moderate negative space around the edges. The dish sits on a light wood table alongside a small bowl of steamed white rice and dark wood chopsticks. Natural, even lighting highlights the varied textures of the tender meat and crisp vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Provide chopsticks and a short-handled ceramic spoon
Accompany with hot oolong tea
instructions: Cut beef into 3cm chunks.
Mix beef with 15ml soy sauce, 5g cornstarch, and 15ml oil.
Marinate for 20 minutes.
Rinse black beans and mash with minced garlic and ginger.
Dice bell peppers and onions into 3cm squares.
Halve the mushrooms.
Heat wok over high heat with 30ml oil.
Sear beef chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove beef and set aside.
Add remaining oil to wok.
Stir-fry onions, peppers, and mushrooms for 2 minutes.
Add black bean mixture and stir until fragrant.
Return beef to wok.
Add oyster sauce, remaining soy sauce, and Shaoxing wine.
Toss over high heat for 1 minute until sauce coats all ingredients.
notes: Ensure the wok is smoking hot before adding ingredients to achieve wok hei flavor.
Do not overcook the peppers to maintain a crisp-tender texture.
Rinsing the black beans prevents the dish from becoming overly salty.

recipes.recipe_name: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl holds a nest of glossy spaghetti coated in a creamy, pale yellow emulsion. Thick 1cm batons of golden-brown, crispy bacon are distributed throughout the pasta, providing a textured contrast. The sauce is smooth and fluid, not clumping or scrambled. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese and a heavy sprinkle of coarsely cracked black pepper finish the dish. The bowl sits on a rustic dark oak table next to a folded cream linen napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural light from a nearby window creates soft highlights on the silky pasta. The arrangement is clean and focused, highlighting the rich textures of the Italian classic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the sauce is fluid
Pair with a crisp Frascati or dry Italian white wine
Avoid adding extra cream to maintain Roman authenticity
instructions: Boil 4 liters of water with sea salt.
Cook spaghetti until al dente.
Cut bacon into 1cm thick batons.
Sauté bacon in a large pan over medium heat until fat renders and edges crisp.
Remove pan from heat and set aside.
Whisk 4 egg yolks and 1 whole egg in a bowl.
Stir finely grated Parmesan cheese into the eggs.
Add 30ml of hot pasta water to the egg mixture to temper.
Drain pasta and reserve 100ml of cooking water.
Add pasta to the pan with the bacon.
Pour egg and cheese mixture over the pasta.
Toss vigorously off the heat to create a creamy emulsion.
Add reserved pasta water if needed for a fluid consistency.
Season heavily with freshly cracked black pepper.
notes: Always remove the pan from heat before adding eggs to prevent scrambling.
Use high-quality, aged Parmesan for the best flavor profile.
Ensure the black pepper is coarsely cracked for better visual and textural impact.

recipes.recipe_name: Cured Kingfish with Añejo Flour Crisps
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist starter portion served on a handcrafted, cream-toned ceramic plate. Three 2cm thick chunks of salt-cured kingfish are arranged naturally in the center. The fish has a translucent, firm texture. Interspersed are golden, irregular flour-añejo crisps and translucent fermented radish rounds. Small crumbles of aged añejo cheese are scattered over the fish. The plate sits on a reclaimed wood table with a natural beige linen napkin. The scene is lit with soft, natural side lighting. The background features a small potted succulent. A pair of traditional wooden tongs rests nearby. The entire plate is visible with significant negative space to emphasize the eco-conscious, zero-waste aesthetic. The arrangement feels organic and unforced.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small glass of chilled tepache
Use volcanic stone or clay serving vessels
Provide small wooden picks for communal eating
instructions: Mix salt and sugar in a bowl.
Coat kingfish fillet thoroughly with the mixture.
Cure in refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Rinse fish under cold water to remove salt.
Pat fish dry with a clean cloth.
Cut fish into 2cm thick chunks.
Whisk flour, water, and 30g grated añejo cheese into a thick batter.
Heat oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Fry small spoonfuls of batter until golden and crisp.
Drain crisps on a reusable cloth.
Slice radishes into paper-thin rounds.
Arrange three fish chunks on each plate.
Place crisps and radish rounds between fish.
Garnish with remaining crumbled añejo cheese.
notes: Save fish bones and head for a sustainable seafood stock
Use radish green tops to create a zero-waste herb oil
Ensure fish is ultra-fresh for the curing process

recipes.recipe_name: Sichuan Chili Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sichuan Chili Chicken is presented in a shallow, hand-glazed ceramic bowl. The dish features 2cm irregular chunks of chicken, stir-fried to a deep golden-brown with a glistening finish. Dozens of vibrant red dried chili halves and thin slices of toasted garlic are scattered naturally throughout the meat. Bright green 3cm green onion batons provide a fresh contrast. The bowl sits on a rustic, well-used wooden kitchen table. A small side bowl of steamed white rice and a pair of bamboo chopsticks rest nearby. The lighting is warm and inviting, typical of a home kitchen, highlighting the crispy texture of the chicken and the glossy aromatics.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Provide bamboo or wooden chopsticks
Pair with a side of cold smashed cucumber salad
instructions: Cut chicken into 2cm chunks.
Mix chicken with soy sauce, wine, and cornstarch in a bowl.
Marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks in a single layer.
Fry until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and drain on paper towels.
Keep 15ml of oil in the wok.
Add garlic, ginger, and Sichuan peppercorns.
Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add dried chilies and fry until they darken slightly.
Return chicken to the wok.
Add sugar and green onion batons.
Toss for 1 minute to combine flavors.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches a safe internal temperature of 75°C.
Do not eat the whole dried chilies; they are for flavoring the oil.
Adjust the amount of dried chilies to control the spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Peanut and Mustard Braised Chicken Stew
recipes.visual_description: Present the stew in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl. The dish features large, 4cm chunks of tender, braised chicken and 3cm cubes of softened potatoes. The sauce is a rich, creamy ochre-orange hue from the peanut butter and cayenne, showing a glossy, thick consistency. Visible specks of softened diced onions and minced garlic are distributed throughout. A light garnish of fresh cilantro or sliced red chilies adds a pop of color. The bowl sits on a dark wood table with a textured cotton napkin. Beside the bowl, a side of white rice or fufu is served in a small, matching bowl. A simple metal spoon is placed on the right. Lighting is natural and even.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice
Traditional fufu or pounded yam
Side of pickled vegetables or fresh cucumber salad

ingredients.name: chicken thighs, boneless and skinless, 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks on all sides.
Remove chicken from the pot and set aside.
Sauté diced onions in the same pot until translucent.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in cayenne pepper, mustard, and peanut butter.
Slowly whisk in chicken stock and Worcestershire sauce until smooth.
Return chicken to the pot.
Add potato cubes.
Simmer for 30 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper before serving.
notes: Use natural peanut butter for the best flavor profile
Ensure the sauce does not boil too vigorously to prevent the peanut oil from separating
The potatoes act as a natural thickener for the braising liquid

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Basil Beef with Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish features succulent, seared beef chunks coated in a glossy, dark umami glaze. Bright red tomato wedges and translucent purple onion wedges provide vibrant color contrast. Fresh Thai basil leaves are scattered throughout, partially wilted from the heat. The beef is piled naturally on a clean white porcelain plate next to a neat mound of steamed jasmine rice. A crispy fried egg with a bright orange runny yolk sits atop the rice. The arrangement is organic and uncluttered, showing the textures of the seared meat and softened vegetables. The setting is a dark wood bistro table with a side of chili-fish sauce in a small ceramic dish. Natural light highlights the steam and sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed jasmine rice
Top with a crispy fried egg (Kai Dao)
Provide Prik Nam Pla (fish sauce with chilies) on the side
Eat using a spoon in the right hand and a fork in the left
instructions: Cut beef into 2cm chunks.
Pound garlic and chilies into a coarse paste using a mortar and pestle.
Cut onion into thin wedges.
Cut tomatoes into 6 wedges each.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat.
Add garlic-chili paste.
Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add beef chunks.
Sear beef for 2 minutes until browned.
Add onion wedges.
Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add tomato wedges.
Pour in oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, and sugar.
Toss for 1 minute on high heat to glaze the beef.
Fold in basil leaves.
Remove from heat immediately once basil wilts.
Verify beef internal temperature reaches 75°C if using poultry, or desired doneness for beef.
Serve immediately over jasmine rice.
notes: Use high heat to achieve wok hei
Do not overcook the tomatoes to maintain their shape
Ensure the egg has lacy, crispy edges

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo en Chilindrón
recipes.visual_description: The dish features whole golden-brown chicken thighs nestled in a rich, vibrant red tomato and onion sauce. The sauce has a thick, rustic texture with visible pieces of softened onion and garlic. Beside the chicken, crispy 2cm golden potato cubes are piled neatly, showing a high-contrast crunch against the saucy base. The plating uses a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. A light sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green parsley adds a pop of color over the deep red sauce. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the glisten of the olive oil. The background includes a rustic wooden table, a small side dish of green olives, and a crusty piece of bread.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty rustic bread
Pair with a glass of Spanish Rioja
Include a side of marinated olives
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan.
Brown chicken on all sides for 10 minutes.
Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pan.
Sauté onion until translucent and soft.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika for 1 minute.
Pour in white wine and scrape the pan bottom.
Add crushed tomatoes and chicken stock.
Return chicken to the pan.
Simmer for 20 minutes until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Fry potato cubes in remaining oil until golden and crisp.
Serve chicken in sauce with potatoes on the side.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches exactly 75°C for safety.
Use high-quality pimentón de la Vera for authentic flavor.
Keep potatoes separate until serving to maintain crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Bell Pepper and Tomato Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted bell pepper and tomato pasta bake served in a clean white porcelain shallow bowl. The rigatoni pasta is coated in a vibrant red tomato sauce, interspersed with bright red and yellow 2cm bell pepper chunks. Large, soft white chunks of melted mozzarella are nestled between the pasta tubes. A golden layer of toasted, coarse breadcrumbs provides a textured topping. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are scattered across the surface. The dish sits on a dark wood bistro table. Beside the bowl is a folded white linen napkin and a polished silver fork. Natural light illuminates the glossy sauce and the rustic textures of the breadcrumbs.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a light-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti
Offer extra virgin olive oil for drizzling at the table
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice bell peppers into 2cm chunks.
Mince garlic cloves.
Sauté peppers in 30ml olive oil until soft.
Add garlic and oregano. Cook 1 minute.
Crush tomatoes into the pan. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Boil pasta in salted water. Drain 2 minutes before al dente.
Toss pasta with sauce and half the basil leaves.
Transfer mixture to a baking dish.
Tear mozzarella into large chunks. Nestled chunks into the pasta.
Mix breadcrumbs with remaining olive oil. Sprinkle over the top.
Bake for 10 minutes until cheese melts and breadcrumbs are golden.
Garnish with remaining fresh basil.
notes: Ensure the pasta is undercooked before baking to avoid a mushy texture.
Use high-quality buffalo mozzarella for a creamier finish.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef and Pancetta Ragu with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a portion of al dente rigatoni pasta thoroughly coated in a rich, glossy tomato ragu. Large, tender 2cm chunks of braised beef and small, crisp cubes of rendered pancetta are distributed throughout the pasta. The sauce is deep red and thick, clinging to the ridges of the rigatoni. It is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl placed on a dark oak table. A delicate dusting of finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano sits at the center, garnished with three small, fresh basil leaves. A polished stainless steel fork rests on a folded white linen napkin beside the plate. The lighting is soft and natural, emphasizing the textures of the meat and sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty ciabatta bread
Pair with a medium-bodied Italian red wine like Chianti
Present as a 'primo piatto' or a substantial main course
instructions: Heat olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chunks in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced pancetta to the pot. Cook until fat renders and edges are crisp.
Add onion. Sauté for 5 minutes until translucent.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes, beef stock, and brown sugar.
Return beef to the pot. Season with salt and pepper.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 90 minutes until beef is tender.
Boil rigatoni in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 60ml of pasta water.
Toss pasta with the ragu and reserved water over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Garnish with grated parmesan and fresh basil.
notes: Ensure the beef is seared in batches to maintain high heat and prevent steaming.
The brown sugar balances the natural acidity of the canned tomatoes.
The reserved pasta water is essential for creating a cohesive sauce that sticks to the rigatoni.

recipes.recipe_name: Masala Garlic Chicken Noodles with Basil
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Masala Garlic Chicken Noodles served in a deep white porcelain bowl. The dish features 3cm golden-brown seared chicken chunks nestled among tangled wheat noodles. The noodles are coated in a vibrant orange-red masala sauce with visible bits of minced garlic and slit green chilies. Bright green fresh basil leaves are scattered throughout, slightly wilted from the heat. The chicken shows a caramelized exterior from high-heat sautéing. The setting is a dark wood bistro table with a cotton linen napkin. A side of thin-sliced red onion rings and a lime wedge sit on the edge of the plate. Lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the glossy texture of the sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Lacha pyaaz (pickled red onions)
Lime wedges
Chilled masala soda
instructions: Boil noodles in salted water until al dente. Drain and toss with 5ml oil.
Heat 25ml oil in a heavy-bottomed pan.
Add minced garlic and green chilies. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Add chicken chunks. Sear on high heat until golden-brown on all sides.
Add sliced onions and ginger paste. Cook until onions soften.
Stir in turmeric, chili powder, garam masala, and dried oregano.
Cook chicken until the internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Add cooked noodles to the pan. Toss well to coat in the spice mixture.
Remove from heat. Fold in fresh basil leaves.
Drizzle with lemon juice. Adjust salt and serve.
notes: Use chicken thighs for maximum moisture during high-heat sautéing.
Kashmiri chili powder provides vibrant color without excessive heat.
Ensure the pan is very hot before adding chicken to achieve a proper sear.

recipes.recipe_name: Lowcountry Okra and Sweet Corn Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lowcountry rice pilau served on a wide, matte white porcelain plate. The rice is fluffy and free-flowing, flecked with bright yellow sweet corn kernels and emerald green basil ribbons. Resting atop the rice are five whole, vibrant green okra pods, expertly charred with deep brown sear marks and a light dusting of smoked paprika. A smooth, vibrant red tomato-basil coulis is artistically pooled around the base of the rice, providing a sharp color contrast. The setting features a dark oak bistro table with a folded white linen napkin and a silver fork. Natural side-lighting highlights the textures of the charred vegetable skins and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fermented hot sauce.
Accompany with corn bread.
Traditionally eaten with a large spoon.
instructions: Simmer diced tomatoes with 10g basil for 15 minutes.
Blend mixture until smooth.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve.
Melt butter in a pot.
Sauté diced onion and minced garlic until translucent.
Add rice and corn kernels.
Toast for 2 minutes.
Add vegetable stock.
Bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 18 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Toss whole okra with oil, salt, and paprika.
Heat a cast-iron skillet.
Sear okra for 6 minutes until charred.
Fold chopped basil into the rice.
Spoon rice onto a plate.
Place whole charred okra on top.
Drizzle tomato coulis around the rice.
notes: Dry okra pods thoroughly before searing.
Use fresh seasonal corn for sweetness.
Keep rice covered for 5 minutes after cooking to steam.

recipes.recipe_name: Kozhi Thakkali Sadam
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant, orange-tinted rice served on a polished stainless steel thali. The rice grains are long, separate, and fluffy. Succulent 3cm chunks of spice-marinated chicken are distributed throughout the rice, showing a deep golden-brown sear. Softened tomato fragments and translucent onion slivers are visible between the grains. The dish is topped with a few crisp, dark green tempered curry leaves and a sprig of fresh coriander. On the side of the thali, a small white ceramic bowl contains creamy yogurt raita. A single lime wedge rests on the edge. The setting is a dark wood bistro table with natural side lighting and a cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with onion raita and lemon pickle
Present on a traditional stainless steel thali or a banana leaf
Pair with crispy papadums
instructions: Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves. Sauté until fragrant.
Add sliced onions and curry leaves. Fry until golden brown.
Stir in ginger and garlic pastes. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides.
Add tomatoes, turmeric, and chili powder. Cook until tomatoes soften into a paste.
Drain rice and add to the pot. Stir gently to coat grains in spice base.
Pour in water and add salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover with a tight lid. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest covered for 5 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Stir in coriander.

recipes.recipe_name: Almond-Crusted Lamb with Date and Cherry Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: Twelve 3cm cubes of almond-crusted lamb loin are arranged in a flowing, organic line across a grey-veined white marble platter. Each lamb cube features a thick, textured coating of golden-brown crushed smoked almonds. A glossy, deep-crimson cherry and date gastrique is drizzled with architectural precision around the meat, showing visible chunks of softened dates and halved tart cherries. Small, vibrant green micro-cilantro leaves provide a sharp color contrast. The lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows that highlight the crunchy almond texture and the succulent, medium-rare interior of the lamb. The background is a minimalist, dark slate surface, emphasizing the luxury of the brass serving utensils and the pristine marble.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on traditional brass or copper platters
Accompany with small bowls of lightly salted yogurt
Present with warm flatbread on the side
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C.
Pulse almonds in food processor until coarse crumbs form.
Season lamb loin with salt and black pepper.
Sear lamb in a hot pan for 2 minutes per side.
Remove lamb and brush with honey.
Press lamb into almond crumbs until fully coated.
Roast lamb for 8 minutes until internal temperature is 54°C.
Rest lamb for 6 minutes.
Sauté shallots and dates in butter for 3 minutes.
Add cherries and chicken stock to the pan.
Simmer until liquid reduces by two-thirds.
Whisk in pomegranate molasses.
Cut lamb into 3cm cubes.
Arrange 12 cubes on a serving platter.
Spoon cherry-date sauce over each piece.
Garnish with micro-cilantro.
notes: Ensure the lamb rests fully to maintain juice before cubing.
Use high-quality pomegranate molasses for authentic tartness.
Do not over-process almonds; texture is essential for the crust.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rustic chicken cacciatore served in a shallow, cream-colored ceramic bowl with minor surface imperfections. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs are the centerpiece, their skin appearing dark golden and tender from braising. The chicken is partially submerged in a thick, chunky tomato sauce featuring visible pieces of softened translucent onions and whole black olives. A single fresh rosemary sprig is placed casually on top. The bowl sits on a weathered dark wood kitchen table. Beside the bowl is a thick piece of torn crusty bread. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft overhead kitchen lighting, creating a cozy, authentic Italian home-dining atmosphere. A simple linen napkin and a stainless steel fork are placed to the left of the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty sourdough bread to soak up the tomato sauce
Pair with a side of simple polenta or rustic mashed potatoes
Traditional family-style dining involves placing the skillet in the center of the table
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper on all sides.
Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until golden brown.
Flip chicken and sear for 4 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, and the rosemary sprig.
Place chicken back into the skillet, nestled into the sauce.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C internally.
Stir in the olives 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use bone-in thighs for maximum flavor and protein content
Ensure the sauce reduces until thick to concentrate the savory tomato profile
Always check the thickest part of the chicken for a safe internal temperature of 75°C

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Candied Lemon and Olives
recipes.visual_description: A single portion served in a traditional shallow ceramic tagine base. Two whole, seared chicken thighs are the centerpiece, showing crisp, golden-brown skin glistening with a thick, vibrant saffron-yellow sauce. The sauce is textured with finely diced translucent onions. Scattered across the chicken are whole cracked green olives and thin, translucent julienne strips of bright yellow candied lemon peel. A generous dusting of coarsely chopped bright green cilantro and parsley provides contrast. The dish is placed on a rustic dark wood table next to a small bowl of fluffy, steamed couscous and a clean white cotton napkin. Natural side lighting highlights the glossy sauce and the texture of the citrus peel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed semolina couscous
Accompany with crusty khobz bread for dipping
Traditional hand-washing before the meal is customary
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-based pot or tagine over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown. Remove and set aside.
Add onions to the pot. Sauté for 8 minutes until soft.
Stir in garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, and turmeric. Cook for 1 minute.
Return chicken to the pot. Add chicken stock and saffron.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 35 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Stir in green olives and candied lemon peel. Simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Fold in fresh cilantro and parsley before serving.
notes: The candied lemon peel adds a unique sweet-bitter complexity that balances the salty olives.
Do not over-salt the sauce initially as the olives and lemon peel add salinity during simmering.

recipes.recipe_name: Strawberry Risotto with Aged Balsamic
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of fluid, pale pink risotto is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The rice has a creamy, free-flowing 'all'onda' consistency, spreading naturally across the surface. Mince-sized shallots and softened 1cm strawberry cubes are visible within the grains. The dish is topped with three whole strawberry halves arranged organically in the center. Small, vibrant green mint leaves are scattered lightly over the rice. A thin, dark drizzle of syrupy aged balsamic vinegar creates a sharp contrast against the pink rice. The setting features a light oak table with a silver fork and a white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the velvety texture of the starch emulsion.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on flat plates to allow the risotto to spread
Pair with the same Prosecco used in cooking
Serve as a 'primo piatto' or a light vegetarian main course
instructions: Heat vegetable stock in a pot. Keep at a low simmer.
Mince shallots finely.
Dice 300g of strawberries into 1cm cubes. Halve the remaining 100g for garnish.
Melt 30g butter in a wide, heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Sauté minced shallots until translucent. Do not brown.
Add rice to the pan. Toast for 2 minutes until edges look translucent.
Pour in Prosecco. Stir until the liquid evaporates completely.
Add one ladle of hot stock. Stir constantly.
Add more stock only after the previous ladle is absorbed.
Fold in the diced strawberries after 10 minutes of cooking.
Continue adding stock until rice is al dente, approximately 18 minutes total.
Remove pan from heat.
Add remaining 30g butter and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.
Stir vigorously for 1 minute to create a creamy emulsion.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Cover and rest for 2 minutes before serving.
notes: Carnaroli rice is preferred over Arborio for its superior texture and starch content
The stock must remain hot to prevent shocking the rice and slowing the cooking process
Maintain a fluid consistency; the risotto should move like a wave when the plate is shaken

recipes.recipe_name: Lomo Saltado
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lomo Saltado presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features 3cm chunks of seared beef sirloin with a deep brown crust. These are mixed with thick, glossy wedges of purple red onion and bright red Roma tomatoes. Golden, thick-cut potato batons are scattered through the beef mixture, all coated in a dark, shimmering sauce. A neat, molded dome of fluffy white rice sits on the side of the plate. Fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the top. The scene is set on a light wooden bistro table with a white cotton napkin and a small side bowl of spicy green aji sauce. The lighting is natural and even.

Accompany with Inca Kola or a glass of red wine
Traditionally eaten with both rice and potatoes in the same meal

Roma tomatoes, cut into thick wedges

instructions: Season beef chunks with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok over high heat until smoking.
Sear beef in batches until browned and medium-rare.
Remove beef from wok and set aside.
Add remaining oil to the wok.
Stir-fry onion wedges for 2 minutes until slightly charred but crisp.
Add garlic and aji amarillo paste. Stir for 30 seconds.
Return beef to the wok.
Pour in soy sauce and red wine vinegar. Toss quickly.
Add tomato wedges. Stir for 30 seconds to warm through.
Fold in the cooked potato fries and half the cilantro.
Remove from heat immediately.
Serve with white rice.
notes: Ensure the wok is extremely hot before adding beef to achieve a smoky flavor.
Do not overcook the tomatoes; they should be warm but hold their shape.
The potatoes should be added at the very last second to maintain some crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Garlic Beef Chunks with Corn Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Korean-style beef served in a deep white porcelain bowl, showing the entire plate. The base features steamed short-grain rice folded with bright yellow corn kernels and sliced green scallions. Thick, 3cm cubes of seared beef ribeye are arranged in a natural cluster atop the rice. The beef is coated in a glossy, dark brown soy-garlic glaze. Garnish the meat with crispy, golden-brown garlic chips and a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds. A small porcelain side dish contains vibrant red napa cabbage kimchi. Stainless steel chopsticks and a long-handled spoon rest on a cotton napkin on a light oak table. Natural side lighting emphasizes the succulent texture of the beef chunks and individual rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with napa cabbage kimchi
Accompany with a side of seasoned soybean sprouts (kongnamul munchim)
Use traditional Korean stainless steel chopsticks and a long-handled spoon
Serve with warm barley tea (bori-cha)
instructions: Rinse 300g rice until water runs clear.
Place rice, 450ml water, and 300g corn kernels in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and let steam for 10 minutes.
Cut 600g beef ribeye into 3cm cubes.
Slice 6 garlic cloves into thin rounds. Mince the remaining 4 cloves.
Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat.
Fry garlic slices until golden and crisp. Remove and drain on paper towels.
Increase heat to high in the same pan.
Sear beef cubes for 2 minutes per side until a dark crust forms.
Add minced garlic, 45ml soy sauce, and 15ml honey to the pan.
Toss beef for 1 minute until the sauce becomes a thick glaze.
Stir 15ml sesame oil and sliced scallions into the corn rice.
Place a portion of rice in a bowl and top with beef chunks.
Garnish with garlic chips and sesame seeds.
notes: Use a heavy cast iron pot for the rice to develop a slight crust at the bottom.
Ensure the pan is smoking hot before adding the beef to achieve a proper sear without overcooking the center.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish-Style Chicken, Sausage, and Beef Fideuá with Beans
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing a vibrant Fideuá base. Short, toasted pasta strands and creamy white beans are coated in a rich, deep-orange tomato and saffron sauce. Four whole, golden-brown seared chicken thighs with crispy skin sit prominently on top. Interspersed among the pasta are thick 3cm cubes of seared beef and 2cm chunks of dark, smoky chorizo. Small flecks of caramelized onion and bright green chopped parsley provide texture. The arrangement is rustic yet refined, showing visible steam. The setting includes a dark wooden bistro table, a folded linen napkin, and a side of lemon wedges for a modern Mediterranean aesthetic.

Accompany with crusty sourdough bread
Provide fresh lemon wedges for acidity

Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until crispy and golden.
Add beef cubes and sausage chunks to the pan.
Brown all meat thoroughly and remove from pan. Set aside.
Sauté diced onion in the remaining fat until translucent.
Stir in garlic, smoked paprika, and crushed tomatoes.
Cook until the mixture thickens into a dark, rich sofrito.
Add dry pasta to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast.
Pour in stock and add saffron. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef, sausage, and white beans to the pan.
Arrange chicken thighs on top of the pasta mixture.
Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until pasta is al dente and liquid is absorbed.

Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

Do not stir the pasta once the stock is added to allow a crust to form
Use a wide pan to ensure even evaporation of the stock

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Tofu with Peppers and Tomatoes

These chunks are submerged in a rich, chunky sauce made of crushed tomatoes and translucent diced onions. Vibrant red and yellow bell peppers, cut into 1cm wide strips, are draped over the tofu. Cut tofu into 3cm cubes.
Slice bell peppers into 1cm wide strips.
Dice onion and mince garlic.

Remove tofu from pan and set aside.
Add onion and peppers to the same pan.

Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable stock.
Simmer sauce for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return tofu cubes to the pan.
Simmer for 5 minutes to heat through.
Stir in fresh basil leaves.
Season with salt and pepper.

Ensure the sauce is thick enough to coat the tofu chunks heavily.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey and Mushroom Ragù with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A wide, white porcelain pasta bowl sits on a dark oak table. The bowl contains rigatoni pasta coated in a thick, glossy tomato ragù. The turkey is cut into 1.5cm cubes, browned and tender, interspersed with quartered cremini mushrooms. The sauce has a deep red hue from slow-simmered crushed tomatoes and onions. Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion and mushrooms to the same pan.
Sauté until vegetables are softened and browned.
Add bell pepper and garlic.
Cook for 3 minutes while stirring.
Stir in tomato puree and oregano.
Simmer sauce for 5 minutes.
Add rice and stir to coat in the sauce.
Pour in hot chicken stock.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until rice is tender.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Use a wide pan to ensure even rice cooking.
Do not stir the rice once the stock is added.
Ensure chicken skin remains above the liquid level to stay crispy.

recipes.recipe_name: Miso-Cured Lamb with King Crab and Cherry-Pineapple Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single, dark-textured ceramic plate features two 3cm cubes of miso-seared lamb loin, positioned off-center. Next to the lamb, two large, succulent chunks of King crab meat are delicately placed. A vibrant yellow pineapple gel is applied in three organic, varying-sized dots. Four halves of deep-red pickled cherries are nestled between the proteins, providing a sharp color contrast. A single, bright green shiso leaf is torn into small, precise shards and scattered as a garnish. The arrangement is fluid and asymmetric, utilizing significant negative space on the matte charcoal surface. Lighting is dramatic, casting soft shadows that highlight the glistening glaze on the lamb and the fibrous texture of the crab.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on handcrafted Wabi-sabi ceramic ware
Provide high-quality bamboo chopsticks
Accompany with a small cup of chilled Junmai Daiginjo sake
instructions: Mix miso, mirin, and sake in a bowl.
Coat lamb loin thoroughly with the miso mixture.
Marinate lamb in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Wipe excess marinade from the lamb.
Sear lamb in a hot pan to an internal temperature of 52°C.
Rest the meat for 5 minutes.
Cut the lamb into 3cm cubes.
Blend pineapple and strain through a fine sieve.
Simmer pineapple juice with agar-agar for 1 minute.
Chill the liquid until set, then blend into a smooth gel.
Pit and halve the cherries.
Dissolve sugar in rice vinegar over low heat.
Pour vinegar over cherries and let cool.
Steam King crab meat for 3 minutes.
Break crab meat into large, natural chunks.
Arrange lamb cubes and crab chunks on a plate.
Add dots of pineapple gel and pickled cherry halves.
Garnish with torn shiso leaves.
notes: Ensure the lamb is wiped clean of miso to prevent burning during searing
Use fresh King crab for the best texture and sweetness
The pineapple gel should be perfectly smooth for a professional finish

recipes.recipe_name: Instant Pot Finnish Lohikeitto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Lohikeitto served in a wide, matte-grey ceramic bowl. The soup features a rich, opaque white broth. Large 3cm chunks of pale pink salmon and 2cm cubes of yellow potato are piled in the center, breaking the surface. Bright orange 1cm carrot rounds add vibrant color. A generous scattering of finely chopped bright green dill covers the top. The bowl sits on a rustic, dark oak table. Beside it lies a thick slice of buttered dark rye bread on a small side plate. The lighting is warm and diffused, highlighting the velvety texture of the cream-based broth and the natural, rustic shapes of the root vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with dark sourdough rye bread (ruisleipä) and salted butter
Accompany with a side of pickled cucumbers
Enjoy with a glass of cold milk or light beer
instructions: Cut salmon into 3cm chunks.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2cm cubes.
Peel and slice carrots into 1cm rounds.
Finely dice the onion.
Set Instant Pot to Sauté mode.
Melt butter and add diced onion.
Sauté onion for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add potato cubes, carrot rounds, allspice berries, and fish stock.
Lock lid and set to Pressure Cook on High for 4 minutes.
Perform a quick pressure release immediately.
Open lid and select Sauté mode again.
Pour in heavy cream and stir.
Add salmon chunks to the simmering liquid.
Cook for 3 minutes until salmon is opaque and firm.
Turn off heat.
Stir in chopped fresh dill.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Use waxy potatoes to ensure cubes hold their shape during pressure cooking.
Do not overcook the salmon; the residual heat of the broth finishes the cooking process.
Remove allspice berries before serving if preferred.

recipes.recipe_name: Sausage and Tomato Ragu with Buttered Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl on a light oak bistro table. The base consists of a smooth, fluid bed of golden yellow polenta, showing a glossy sheen from the butter. Centered on the polenta is a rustic ragu made of deep red San Marzano tomatoes. The ragu features large, 3cm chunks of seared pork sausage with visible caramelized edges. The sauce is thick and textured with crushed tomato pieces and translucent onions. A single sprig of fresh rosemary and a light sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan cheese garnish the center. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy polenta and the hearty, matte texture of the sausage chunks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a shallow ceramic bowl
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied red wine like Barbera
Provide crusty ciabatta bread to clean the plate
instructions: Boil 800ml salted water in a heavy pot.
Whisk in 200g polenta gradually.
Reduce heat to low and cook for 30 minutes, stirring frequently.
Remove sausage meat from casings and break into 3cm chunks.
Brown sausage chunks in olive oil over medium-high heat.
Remove sausage from the pan. Sauté diced onion in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and rosemary. Cook for 1 minute.
Crush tomatoes by hand and add to the pan with the sausage.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Stir 60g butter and 50g Parmesan into the polenta until fluid and glossy.
Incorporate remaining 40g butter into the tomato sauce.
Season with salt and pepper.
notes: Ensure the polenta remains fluid; add a splash of warm water if it stiffens.
Keep sausage in large chunks to maintain a rustic texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Adobo with Garlic Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A mound of garlic fried rice sits off-center on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole bone-in chicken thighs, braised to a deep mahogany brown, rest against the rice. The chicken skin is glossy and coated in a thick, dark adobo reduction. Whole black peppercorns and a single bay leaf are nestled in the sauce. Sprinkles of crispy, golden-brown fried garlic and fresh green onion rings garnish the top. The arrangement is natural and uncluttered. A side of pickled papaya strips provides a bright orange contrast. The scene is set on a dark wood table with a cotton napkin and a traditional spoon and fork set. Soft, natural light emphasizes the rich textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Atchara (pickled papaya)
Provide a small bowl of spicy vinegar for dipping
Use a traditional spoon and fork set
instructions: Marinate chicken in soy sauce, vinegar, crushed garlic, and peppercorns for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Remove chicken from marinade and sear skin-side down until golden brown.
Add sliced onions to the pot and sauté until translucent.
Pour in the remaining marinade, water, and bay leaves.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken and boil the sauce over high heat until thick and syrupy.
In a separate pan, fry minced garlic in oil until golden and crisp.
Add cold rice to the pan and stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Toss chicken back into the reduced sauce to glaze thoroughly.
Serve the glazed chicken beside the garlic rice.
notes: For best results, use day-old rice for the garlic fried rice to prevent clumping.
Adjust vinegar levels at the end if the sauce is too salty.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Artichokes with Cannellini Purée and Pancetta
recipes.visual_description: A single whole braised artichoke sits upright in the center of a wide, matte white porcelain plate. The artichoke is tender and olive-green, with its leaves slightly opened to reveal a golden-brown interior from the braising process. It rests on a circular bed of creamy, ivory-colored cannellini bean purée that is perfectly smooth and fluid. Scattered around the base are 1cm thick cubes of crispy, golden-brown pancetta. A glossy, translucent herb-flecked reduction is drizzled over the artichoke and pools slightly on the purée. Freshly torn mint and parsley leaves provide vibrant green accents. The lighting is soft and natural, highlighting the velvety texture of the purée and the crisp edges of the meat chunks.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with thick slices of toasted sourdough bread
Pair with a chilled Vermentino or Soave wine
Provide a small side bowl for discarded artichoke leaves
instructions: Prepare a bowl of cold water with the juice of one lemon.
Trim artichoke stems to 5cm length.
Peel the outer skin of the stems with a paring knife.
Remove tough outer leaves until pale green leaves appear.
Cut off the top 3cm of the artichoke crown.
Use a spoon to scoop out the fuzzy choke from the center.
Place trimmed artichokes immediately into the lemon water.
Dice pancetta into 1cm cubes.
Sauté pancetta in a deep pan with 20ml olive oil over medium heat until crisp.
Remove pancetta and set aside on a paper towel.
Place artichokes in the same pan with the stem side up.
Add smashed garlic cloves, chopped mint, parsley, white wine, and vegetable stock.
Cover the pan and simmer for 25 minutes until the artichoke base is tender.
Drain and rinse the cannellini beans.
Blend beans with 40ml olive oil and salt in a high-speed blender until smooth.
Warm the bean purée in a small saucepan over low heat.
Remove artichokes from the braising liquid.
Boil the remaining liquid over high heat for 5 minutes until reduced by half.
Spread a generous circle of bean purée on each plate.
Place one whole artichoke in the center of the purée.
Distribute the crispy pancetta chunks around the artichoke.
Spoon the reduced braising sauce over the artichoke and purée.
notes: Ensure the bean purée is passed through a fine-mesh sieve for a professional restaurant texture
Keep artichokes submerged in lemon water to prevent oxidation and browning during prep

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican-style Chicken with Esquites and Roasted Tomato Salsa
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a vibrant, creamy base of sautéed corn kernels, lightly coated in white Mexican crema and flecked with bright green cilantro. A single, whole pan-seared chicken thigh sits atop the corn, boasting a deeply browned, crispy skin seasoned with dark red chili powder. Surrounding the corn is a rustic, chunky salsa made from tatemado-style charred tomatoes and onions, showing deep red and black scorched flecks. The plate is finished with a sprinkle of snow-white crumbled cotija cheese. Presented on a clean white porcelain plate over a light oak wood table. A single lime wedge sits on the side. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the charred vegetables and crispy poultry.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas in a cloth-lined basket
Accompany with a side of pickled red onions
Provide extra lime wedges for squeezing over the chicken
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Season chicken thighs with salt and ancho chili powder.
Heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down for 6 minutes until crispy.
Flip chicken and transfer skillet to oven.
Roast until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Place whole tomatoes and half the onion on a tray.
Broil until skins are charred and blackened.
Pulse charred vegetables and garlic in a blender until chunky.
Dice the remaining onion finely.
Sauté diced onion and corn kernels for 8 minutes.
Stir in Mexican crema and juice from half the lime.
Spoon corn onto the center of the plate.
Place one whole chicken thigh on top of the corn.
Drizzle chunky salsa around the base.
Garnish with crumbled cotija cheese and chopped cilantro.
notes: Ensure the skillet is very hot before searing chicken for maximum skin crispness.
If cotija is unavailable, substitute with a dry feta or ricotta salata.
For extra authenticity, add a sprig of epazote to the corn while sautéing.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Mushroom Chicken Pasta is presented on a clean, wide-rimmed white porcelain plate. The rigatoni pasta is tossed in a smooth, garlic-infused cream sauce made from blended cottage cheese. Large, rustic chunks of chicken breast, seared to a deep golden brown, are placed centrally. Thick-cut wedges of sautéed cremini mushrooms and finely diced onions are distributed evenly through the pasta. To the side, vibrant green broccoli florets, cut into bite-sized pieces and lightly charred, offer a crisp texture. The setting is a light wood bistro table with a grey linen napkin and silver fork. Natural light highlights the glossy sauce and the matte finish of the vegetables.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty sourdough bread
Accompany with a crisp green salad
Use a deep pasta bowl for a more traditional European presentation
instructions: Boil pasta in salted water until al dente. Drain and reserve 60ml of pasta water.
Blend cottage cheese with minced garlic and chicken stock until completely smooth.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Season chicken chunks with salt and pepper. Sear until golden and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from pan.
Add remaining oil to the same pan. Sauté diced onions and quartered mushrooms until browned.
Steam or pan-sear broccoli florets until tender-crisp and bright green.
Lower heat to medium. Add the blended cottage cheese mixture to the pan with onions and mushrooms.
Stir in the cooked pasta and reserved pasta water to emulsify the sauce.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Toss gently to coat in the sauce.
Serve immediately with the broccoli arranged on the side.
notes: Ensure the cottage cheese is blended thoroughly to prevent a grainy texture in the sauce.
Rice can be substituted for pasta; follow the same sauce preparation and serve the chicken and mushrooms over a bed of fluffy white rice.
Do not boil the sauce after adding the cottage cheese to prevent curdling.

recipes.recipe_name: Khao Man Gai
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Khao Man Gai served on a clean white porcelain plate. A central, rounded mound of fragrant, glistening Jasmine rice sits adjacent to thick, succulent chunks of poached chicken. The chicken skin is pale and moist. Fresh cucumber rounds are arranged on the side. A small ceramic bowl containing a dark brown garlic and coriander sauce is placed on the plate. Garnished with vibrant green whole coriander sprigs. The setting is a modern bistro with a light wood table. A set of Thai-style spoons and forks rests on a folded cotton napkin. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the soft textures of the meat and the individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of clear chicken broth garnished with coriander
Include fresh cucumber slices on the plate
Provide extra bird's eye chilies for heat
instructions: Place chicken in a large pot and cover with water.
Add coriander roots, half the ginger, and salt to the water.
Simmer chicken until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pot and let rest.
Reserve the poaching liquid.
Mince remaining garlic and ginger.
Sauté garlic and ginger in a pan with oil until fragrant.
Add rice to the pan and stir to coat grains.
Add 600 ml of reserved broth to the rice.
Cover and cook until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Mince coriander leaves and chilies.
Mix coriander, chilies, soy sauce, soybean paste, and sugar for the sauce.
Cut chicken into thick chunks.
Serve chicken over rice with sauce on the side.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches 75°C for safety
Do not discard the chicken fat; use it to sauté the rice for extra flavor
Use coriander roots in the poaching liquid for authentic aroma

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Pork and Sausage Bean Ragout with Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is served in a shallow white porcelain bowl on a dark wood bistro table. A single portion of al dente pasta is tossed in a creamy, savory sauce. Large 3cm cubes of seared pork and turkey are mixed with 4cm chunks of browned sausage. The meat pieces show a rich, caramelized exterior. Plump white cannellini beans and quartered brown mushrooms are scattered throughout the arrangement. Small 5mm cubes of softened apple are visible in the sauce. A dusting of finely grated Pecorino cheese covers the top. A thick, toasted slice of rustic bread rests on the edge of the plate. Natural light illuminates the glossy sauce and textures. A cotton napkin and simple fork sit beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra virgin olive oil for drizzling
Use bread for 'fare la scarpetta' to clean the sauce from the plate
instructions: Cut pork and turkey into 3cm cubes.
Cut sausage into 4cm chunks.
